variable_coverage.construction: ΔWC_t is the source-defined change in working capital (ΔAR−ΔInventory−ΔAP−ΔTP−ΔOther Assets(net)); preserve the paper’s separately printed Compustat item-coded formula using signed cash-flow statement fields. Scale by average total assets for t, i.e. TA_(t−1),TA_t.
Past CFO is Compustat item 308 CFO_(t−1), scaled by average total assets for year t−1 (TA_(t−2),TA_(t−1)); this composes the predictor’s one-year lag and its own denominator history.
Current CFO is Compustat item 308 CFO_t, scaled by average total assets for t (TA_(t−1),TA_t).
Future CFO is Compustat item 308 CFO_(t+1), scaled by average total assets for t+1 (TA_t,TA_(t+1)).

required_coverage.detail: Target article says KLD ratings began in 1991 and merges KLD with Compustat through 2009; actual row-level rating fields and historical population are not supplied locally or covered by a coordinator confirmation.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No live local KLD fields or exact coverage proof were verified. Catalog absence is not evidence of an absent license.

requirements.description: Historical firm-year linkage between KLD rating records and Compustat GVKEY/annual firm-years.

required_coverage.population: KLD firms matched to Compustat including historical changes in names/identifiers.
required_coverage.detail: Paper reports the match and resulting counts but does not describe the KLD identifier or the matching/link-validity rules.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The source identifies matched samples but does not provide a reproducible identifier crosswalk.

requirements.description: CRSP history used to identify the first appearance of each sampled firm for FIRM_AGE.

required_coverage.population: Compustat firms in the target KLD sample; all historical CRSP records before each observation are needed.
required_coverage.detail: No earliest CRSP observation year is specified; preserve the open beginning and the target firm-year end of 2009.

routes.mapping_notes: CRSP monthly DATE/PERMNO observations can locate first CRSP appearances; the source does not say whether it uses monthly or daily CRSP files or its firm/security linkage convention.
routes.coverage_notes: Exact fields are live; no local coverage confirmation supports the full historical CRSP history needed to identify each firm’s first appearance.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Local fields/access are proven, but the full historical coverage and choice of first-security versus first-firm appearance are not confirmed.

requirements.description: GVKEY-to-PERMNO links needed to connect Compustat firm-years to historical CRSP appearance dates.

required_coverage.population: Compustat firms in the KLD sample; valid CRSP security/company links for each historical observation.
required_coverage.detail: Open beginning: first appearance can precede 1991. The source does not state link-type, primary-link, or valid-date filtering rules.

routes.mapping_notes: CCM links GVKEY to PERMNO with link validity dates and type/primary markers. The target paper does not document the CRSP linkage rules used for first appearance.
routes.coverage_notes: Exact link fields are live; historical link validity and complete population coverage are unverified.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Local link fields/access are proven, but full history, link conventions and population coverage remain unverified.

requirements.description: Securities Data Company New Issue Database records to construct the equity-offering indicator EO for the following fiscal year.

required_coverage.population: KLD/Compustat sample firms with an equity offering in t+1; firm identifiers and issue dates required.
required_coverage.detail: The baseline sample years are 1991–2009 and EO is defined for the following year, implying t+1 fiscal-year labels 1992–2010; the source does not state how event dates are assigned to non-calendar fiscal years.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No matching SDC/New Issue fields or exact route were verified in the local catalog; this is not an access-barrier finding.

requirements.description: Fortune America’s Most Admired Companies firm-year lists used to code ADMIRED.

required_coverage.population: Firms in the paper’s 1991–2009 KLD/Compustat population.
required_coverage.detail: The paper says the source is Fortune Magazine issues 1991–2009; list transcription, identifier matching and the annual observation date are not documented in the local workspace.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The historical source list and reproducible firm-year linkage were not verified.

requirements.description: Study-specific KLD/Compustat sample matching, financial-company exclusion and baseline missing-data selection.

required_coverage.population: Initial 28,741 matched observations, excluding SIC 6000–6999, then 18,160 observations with sufficient DA/RAM/control data.
required_coverage.detail: Sample size and broad exclusions are stated, but the precise cross-source join, valid-data filters and construction-sample population are not fully documented.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The source does not give an executable sample-formation/linkage recipe.

requirements.description: Two-digit-SIC industry-year advertising intensity (AD_IND_INT).

required_coverage.population: Two-digit SIC comparison industries represented by the study sample.
required_coverage.detail: XAD and sales fields exist in Compustat, but the target paper says only “advertising intensity” for the two-digit SIC industry-year; it does not state whether the aggregation is mean firm intensity, aggregate XAD/aggregate sales, or another denominator/population rule.

routes.mapping_notes: Live XAD, SALE and historical SIC fields support input retrieval, but the target does not state the industry-year aggregation or denominator/population formula.
routes.coverage_notes: Exact fields/access are verified; coverage of the study firms and the required industry-year aggregation remains unverified.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The mandatory industry-level aggregation formula and comparison population remain unspecified.

requirements.description: Firm identifiers and alleged GAAP-violation periods required to map AAERs to fiscal-year outcomes (including the CEO/CFO-only dependent variable).

required_coverage.population: AAER firms and alleged violation periods matched to the paper’s 1991–2009 KLD/Compustat observations; a narrower CEO/CFO action flag is also required.
required_coverage.detail: Paper assigns each action to alleged violation periods, not the release date; it does not specify an event-period-to-fiscal-year convention or the binary coding details for the CEO/CFO subset.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The event-date/identifier mapping and executive-specific coding rule are unresolved; release posting dates cannot substitute for violation-period dates.

requirements.description: SEC AAER and LexisNexis release corpus used to identify enforcement cases for Table 5.

required_coverage.population: Accounting/auditing enforcement actions searched by the authors from 1996 through February 2011, including case and respondent details.
required_coverage.detail: The paper’s search end is February 2011; its source also notes that some pre-September 1995 AAERs were not publicly available on the SEC website. The current SEC page is expressly non-exhaustive.

routes.source_name: U.S. SEC Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Releases
routes.mapping_notes: The public SEC list links accounting/auditing enforcement releases. It does not provide a verified structured field for each alleged violation period or a complete firm-year matching table. The target also searched LexisNexis through February 2011.
routes.coverage_notes: SEC itself says the list is not exhaustive; paper uses SEC and LexisNexis release searches and assigns alleged violation years. The public route is a partial discovery route only.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The SEC public page is accessible but incomplete; the LexisNexis corpus, complete release population and historical fields are not verified.

variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Absolute value of discretionary accruals. Raw inputs are Compustat annual fields, KLD category ratings, CRSP history, SDC offering events, Fortune inclusion lists, and/or AAER releases as identified by the linked requirement IDs. When a variable is a supporting residual or composite, use the listed supporting-model closure.

design_coverage.reason: Tables 3–5 use two-dimensional firm and year clustering; no additional cluster data beyond firm/year identifiers are stated.

The source names multiple regressions and logistic regression, but does not fully specify the underlying estimator/link for every baseline model; the AAER printed equation conflicts with the logit prose.
Source includes industry dummies; Table 3 and RAM models identify two-digit SIC industry structure. Industry coding is derived from the annual Compustat historical SIC field.
GVKEY/CRSP link fields are available locally; the source’s KLD/Compustat and CRSP linkage conventions are not fully described.
All continuous variables are winsorized at the top and bottom 1 percent; variable exclusions are not separately stated in this passage.
Paper states 1991–2009 KLD/Compustat sample, excludes SIC 6000–6999, and reports the complete-data N; exact joins and missing-data filters are not executable from the source.
No estimation weights are reported for the frozen baseline regressions.

implementation_issues.description: The paper does not state the aggregation formula for two-digit-SIC industry-year advertising intensity (AD_IND_INT), although it names the input and industry-year level.
The article describes the baseline fit as a multiple regression but does not name the underlying estimator. The supporting accrual and RAM regressions are also not assigned an explicit estimator.

The supporting discretionary-accrual fit leaves its total-accrual component calculation, estimator and exact fitting cells incomplete; it adds lagged ROA but does not give a complete grouping/sample rule.
FIRM_AGE requires CRSP first-appearance dates linked to the Compustat firm, but the source does not state the monthly/daily CRSP choice or valid-link conventions.

review_notes: Local Compustat and CRSP files have exact live-field probes but no coordinator historical-coverage confirmation. KLD, SDC New Issue, Fortune historical lists, and complete AAER violation-period records have no verified local route. The SEC page is an accessible but expressly non-exhaustive discovery source.

variable_coverage.construction: Financial accounting effective tax rate: total income tax expense (Compustat TXT) divided by pretax book income (PI) before special items (SPI). Pretax income excludes discontinued operations, extraordinary items, and special items. Negative pretax income is set to missing; the remaining non-missing ETRs are reset so the largest observation is 1 and the smallest is 0. Formula: TXT / (PI before SPI). Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Advertising expense (Compustat XAD) divided by net sales (SALE); missing values are set to 0 when used as a control in Equation (1). Formula: XAD / SALE; missing control values = 0. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Reported capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) divided by gross property, plant, and equipment (PPEGT). Formula: CAPX / PPEGT. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Calculated from ExecuComp as the average annual value realized from exercise of options for the top executives, grossed up by the fraction of options owned by covered executives, and scaled by average total assets. Formula: Average annual realized option-exercise value for top executives, grossed up by the fraction of options owned by covered executives, scaled by average total assets. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Indicator for a firm with a non-missing, non-zero value for pretax income from foreign operations (Compustat PIFO). Formula: Indicator = 1 when PIFO is non-missing and non-zero. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.
Ratio of intangible assets (Compustat INTANG) to total assets (AT). Formula: INTANG / AT. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Sum of long-term debt (Compustat DLTT) and long-term debt in current liabilities (DLC), divided by total assets (AT). Formula: (DLTT + DLC) / AT. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.
Natural logarithm of total assets (Compustat AT). Formula: ln(AT). Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Indicator for a firm with a non-missing value of tax loss carry-forward (Compustat TLCF). Formula: Indicator = 1 when TLCF is non-missing. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.
Gross property, plant, and equipment (Compustat PPEGT) divided by total assets (AT). Formula: PPEGT / AT. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Selling, general, and administrative expense (Compustat XSGA) divided by net sales (SALE); missing values are set to 0 when used as a control in Equation (1). Formula: XSGA / SALE; missing control values = 0. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

Research and development expense (Compustat XRD) divided by net sales (SALE); missing values are reset to 0, including when used as a control in Equation (1). Formula: XRD / SALE; missing values = 0. Reconstruct from the listed raw inputs using the source's stated period and population.

variable_coverage.construction: TACC: Pre-tax total accruals from statement-of-cash-flow data: EBEI (#123) plus total tax expense TTE (#16), less CFO (#308) plus income taxes paid ITP (#317) net of extraordinary items/discontinued operations EIDO (#124), scaled by beginning-of-year total assets. The body explains that TTE is added back and ITP is added back to CFO. Source formula/construction: [(EBEI_it + TTE_it) − ((CFO_it + ITP_it) − EIDO_it)] / AT_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

SCALED INTERCEPT: Scaled intercept; all variables, including the intercept, are divided by beginning-of-year total assets (Compustat #6). Source formula/construction: 1 / AT_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

ΔREV − ΔAR: Change in sales (Compustat #12) less change in accounts receivable (Compustat #302), divided by total assets at year t−1. Source formula/construction: (change in sales − change in accounts receivable) / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

PPE: Gross property, plant, and equipment (Compustat #7) divided by total assets at year t−1. Source formula/construction: PPE (#7) / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

PERMDIFF: Permanent book-tax difference (total book-tax difference less temporary book-tax differences), using {BI_t − [(CFTE_t + CFOR_t)/STR_t]} − (DTE_t/STR_t), divided by beginning-of-year total assets (Compustat #6). The source PDF p. 7 shows CFTE + CFOR. BI is pre-tax book income (#170), CFTE current federal tax expense (#63), CFOR current foreign tax expense (#64), DTE deferred tax expense (#50), and STR the statutory rate. Missing CFOR, UNCON, MI, and CSTE are set to zero; if CFTE is missing it is computed from total tax expense less CFOR, CSTE, and DTE. Source formula/construction: ({BI_t − [(CFTE_t + CFOR_t)/STR_t]} − DTE_t/STR_t) / AT_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp, r_statutory_rates. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.; Annual statutory tax-rate input STR used in permanent-difference and BTD formulas; state/federal rate construction and state assignment are not specified as a local source.

INTANG: Goodwill and other intangibles (Compustat #33) divided by total assets at year t−1; missing #33 is set to 0. The source also gives a conditional substitution using goodwill (#204), but the condition is unclear in the supplied reading. Source formula/construction: INTANG / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

UNCON: Income (loss) reported under the equity method (Compustat #55) divided by total assets at year t−1; missing values are set to 0. Source formula/construction: UNCON / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

MI: Income (loss) attributable to minority interest (Compustat #49) divided by total assets at year t−1; missing values are set to 0. Source formula/construction: MI / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

CSTE: Current state income tax expense (Compustat #173) divided by total assets at year t−1; missing values are set to 0. Source formula/construction: CSTE / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

LAGPERM: PERMDIFF at year t−1 divided by total assets at year t−1. Source formula/construction: PERMDIFF_{t−1} / total assets_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. DTAX: Discretionary permanent differences from the residual of Equation (1). Source formula/construction: Residual ε_it from Equation (1). Raw requirements: r_comp, r_statutory_rates. DFIN: Performance-matched modified-Jones discretionary accruals. Source formula/construction: Equation (3) residual minus the median residual for the joint industry × PTROA-decile group, excluding the observation. Raw requirements: r_comp. Compustat annual industrial firm-year accounting, balance-sheet, tax, industry, PPE, sales, cash-flow, price and share fields for DTAX/BTD/DFIN construction and controls.

PTROA: Pre-tax income (Compustat #170) divided by total assets (Compustat #6) at year t−1. Source formula/construction: #170_t / #6_{t−1}. Raw requirements: r_comp. NOL_D: Indicator equal to 1 if the firm has net operating losses (Compustat #52), and 0 otherwise; the Table 6 note places it at year t by default. variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: One-year-ahead change in return on net operating assets; Table 5 identifies ΔRNOA_{t+1} as the dependent variable. The paper does not state the exact subtraction formula/window for this dependent variable. RNOA at each date uses the operating-income and NOA component recipe given in the RNOA_t term of this model. Raw component fields: COMP.FUNDA: gvkey, datadate, fyear, sich, at, act, che, lct, dlc, dltt, dp, dvc, dvp, ni, msa, recta, xint, idit, pstk, tstkp, dvpa, ivao, mib, ceq, seq, sale, capx, mkvalt, oancf, ivncf, fincf, ppent, prcc_f, csho Preserve raw missing values and denominators; do not impute missing source components or force an observed classification.

Source formula: OI_t / Average NOA_t Source definition: Current RNOA = OI / Average NOA. OI = CNI + NFE. CNI is net income/loss (#172) minus preferred dividends (#19) plus the change in marketable-securities adjustment (#238) and the change in cumulative translation adjustment in retained earnings (#230). NFE = interest expense (#15) × (1−MTR) + preferred dividends (#19) − interest income (#62) × (1−MTR) + lagged #238 − current #238. MTR is the applicable highest federal rate plus 0.02: federal rates are 34% for 1989–1992 and 35% for 1993–2005. NOA = NFO + CSE + minority interest (#38), where NFO = FO − FA; FO = current debt (#34) + long-term debt (#9) + preferred stock (#130) − preferred treasury stock (#227) + preferred dividends in arrears (#242); FA = cash/short-term investments (#1) + long-term receivables, investments and advances to affiliated companies (#32); CSE = common equity (#60) + preferred treasury stock (#227) − preferred dividends in arrears (#242). The source preserves change notation for #238/#230 and does not give an arithmetic averaging interval for Average NOA. Use Compustat GVKEY/year and effective-dated CCM links for CRSP age/market variables.
The future-profitability models do not report fixed effects.
The article does not specify clustered standard errors.
No weighting scheme is stated.
The paper reports a future-profitability regression but does not identify its estimator; keep the estimator choice as an implementation issue.
Construct the three lifecycle classifications, five-year A&R medians, annual ratios and source-based exclusions while retaining missing component values.

implementation_issues.description: The exact subtraction window for ΔRNOA_(t+1), ΔRNOA_t, ΔATO_t and ΔPM_t is not stated; the annual-difference reading is retained as the conservative source-consistent construction.
Average NOA appears in RNOA and ATO denominators, but the article does not specify the averaging interval; a one-year component window is retained for timing only, not treated as a resolved formula.
The source supplies federal rate plus 0.02 for 1989–2005; the t+1 dependent variable requires a 2006 RNOA, and the 2006 MTR is not specified.

Compustat item #32/#60 and preferred/marketable-security special-item mappings must be matched to current annual fields and preserve source-level missingness; current catalog labels do not prove vintage equivalence.

review_notes: Selected Model 1 is the principal direct comparison of life-cycle classifications. Model 2 adds a separate interaction test, rather than only additional controls.

evidence.quote: Our initial sample consists of all firm-years from 1988 to 2000 inclusive with sufficient data on the 2001 Compustat annual industrial and research files to estimate accruals.
evidence.description: Original Compustat source vintage and 1988–2000 firm-year sample.

evidence.quote: In addition, we require at least the six years of prior data to ensure that any abnormal accruals behavior associated with start-up firms
evidence.description: Six-year prior-data sample screen.

evidence.quote: To identify firms that undergo mergers and acquisitions, we follow Collins and Hribar (2002) and use the footnote codes appearing in Compustat.
evidence.description: M&A exclusions use Compustat footnote codes; exact code fields are not named.

evidence.quote: We calculate auditor tenure as the number of years that the firm has retained the given auditor, and code auditor changes attributable to audit firm mergers as a continuation of the prior auditor.
evidence.description: Tenure accumulation and audit-firm-merger continuation rule.

evidence.quote: We determine which observations are in the top or bottom 0.5 percent of the distribution of cash flow from operations, Current Accruals or Jones Model residuals annually and delete them to remove outliers.
evidence.description: Annual cross-sectional tail trimming; this is not described as a rolling time window.

evidence.quote: when the auditor-client relationship lasts at least five years, we retain all available observations, and when the auditor-client relationship lasts for less than five years, we eliminate all of these auditor-client observations.
evidence.description: Relationship-duration screen is based on total relationship length and keeps all available years.

evidence.quote: we eliminate the first year of the audit in all of our multivariate tests.
evidence.description: First auditor-engagement year omitted from multivariate analyses.

evidence.quote: We estimate the residuals and the coefficients contemporaneously. That is, for each year, we estimate the model within two-digit SIC industries, and use the residuals from this regression as our estimate of discretionary accruals.
evidence.description: Jones residuals and coefficients are fitted contemporaneously within year and two-digit SIC.

evidence.quote: coefficient estimates from an OLS regression by industry-year, where an industry is defined by its two-digit SIC code; to reduce sampling error and to be consistent with prior literature, we eliminate industry-years with fewer than eight firms;
evidence.description: Supporting Jones coefficient fits are OLS by SIC-year with a minimum cell size of eight firms.

evidence.quote: We scale all variables by average total assets.
evidence.description: Scale for accrual, revenue and PPE measures; average assets adds the preceding fiscal-year value.

evidence.quote: Accruals - operating income after depreciation (Compustat annual data item 178) - cash flow from operations (Compustat annual data item 108);
evidence.description: Jones-model raw input definitions and cited historical Compustat items.

evidence.quote: CA - change in current assets (Compustat annual data item 4); - Cash - change in cash and cash equivalents (Compustat annual date item 1);
evidence.description: Current-accrual component definitions; the original reading OCRs the displayed formula imperfectly.

evidence.quote: CL - change in current liabilities (Compustat annual data item 5); - STD - change in short-term notes and current portion of long-term debt (Compustat annual data item 34);
evidence.description: Remaining current-accrual component definitions.

evidence.quote: Age - the number of years for which total assets was reported in Compustat since 1980; Size - the log of total assets;
evidence.description: Age and Size definitions.

evidence.quote: Cash Flow - the firm’s cash flow from operations divided by average total assets; Auditor Type - an indicator set to 1 if the auditor is a Big N Auditor, and set to 0
evidence.description: Cash Flow and Auditor Type definitions.

evidence.quote: This measure varies with mergers of the large accounting firms; the Big N is the largest number of major accounting firms considered.
evidence.description: The Big N indicator changes across audit-firm mergers, but the group list is not specified.

evidence.quote: Industry - a control based on two-digit SIC codes (62 industries); and Year - a control for calendar year.
evidence.description: Two-digit SIC and calendar-year fixed-effect definitions.

evidence.quote: Accruals = alpha + beta_1*Tenure + beta_2*Age + beta_3*Size + beta_4*IndustryGrowth + beta_5*CashFlow + beta_6*AuditorType + beta_7-69*Industry + beta_1988-1999*Year + epsilon.
evidence.description: Coordinator-verified transcription of the displayed main equation; the year coefficient range is printed as 1988–1999.

evidence.quote: Here we use a truncated regression approach because the ordinary least squares (OLS) estimates are generally biased toward zero when a sample is truncated. Thus, we estimate a maximum likelihood truncated regression model to arrive at an unbiased coefficient on Tenure.
evidence.description: Sign-specific outcomes are estimated by maximum-likelihood truncated regression.

evidence.quote: Each cell contains a coefficient estimate and p-values in square brackets.
evidence.description: Reported inference contains p-values; standard-error method is not given.

requirements.description: Recreate the matched U.S. publicly traded loan-facility and public-bond issue population in 1988–2003, with each loan facility a separate record; exclude utilities and financial institutions, non-fund-based/very short bridge facilities, convertible or callable bonds, and records missing the required spread. Preserve year-specific loan/bond samples and complete prior-year accounting requirements.

required_coverage.detail: Paper reports 12,676 facilities from 3,261 firms and 3,681 bonds from 709 firms; final Table 5–7 complete-case counts differ. Exact source-level historical population completeness has not been confirmed.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No frozen coverage confirmation establishes the complete matched population or complete-case loan/bond observation sets.

Formula: Current dividend yield × (1 + current dividend growth rate) + current dividend growth rate.. Inputs/route requirements: r_dividend_yield_growth. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: For each country-year, the measure is the median across firms of accruals scaled by lagged total assets; accruals equal change in current assets minus change in current liabilities minus change in cash plus change in the current portion of long-term debt included in current liabilities minus depreciation and amortization expense plus change in income taxes payable, all divided by total assets in t−1. The two debt/tax inputs are set to zero when missing. The country-year median is ranked across country-years into deciles 1–10; higher rank denotes more aggressiveness. The regressions use the rank lagged one year. Formula: Rank_{country-year}(median_firm[((Δcurrent assets − Δcurrent liabilities − Δcash + Δcurrent portion of long-term debt in current liabilities − depreciation/amortization + Δincome taxes payable) / total assets_{t−1})]); enter at t−1.. Inputs/route requirements: r_worldscope_firm_accounts, r_worldscope_firm_year_ids. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

design_coverage.reason: The baseline generalized ordered-logit equation reports no added fixed effects.
The baseline fit reports no observation or probability weights.

implementation_issues.description: CV_FORECAST is called a coefficient of variation without formula or zero/negative-mean rule; STDEV/MEANEST is only a candidate.
DOWN_REV has conflicting endpoints: before q announcement in prose, before q ends in Table 4 note.
ΔROE uses q−4 in prose and q−1 in Table 4 note; q−4 is used for maximum temporal coverage while retaining the conflict.
Table 5 prints v_it inside the exponential, while Equation (2) and Appendix omit it.
The paper identifies both Compustat and I/B/E/S but omits its historical issuer crosswalk, date/tie policy and auditor company-key join. Local link tables are candidates only.
Big 5 classification requires mapping historical auditor names/keys and carrying auditor status to each quarter.
Winsorization is specified at both 1st-percentile tails, but ties, missing values and pooled versus period-specific cutoffs are not stated.
Current local I/B/E/S products do not establish the precise 1993–1999 historical vintage or EPS adjustment state; the paper notes actual-EPS calculation differences around its sample boundary.

review_notes: Each fit carries the ten-threshold joint-estimation closure and all 14 observed variables.
One-row probes establish access and live fields only; no coordinator coverage confirmation establishes historical/population coverage.
Historical issuer links and current I/B/E/S vintage correspondence remain unresolved; sampled rows/catalog counts are not coverage evidence.

design_coverage.reason: The baseline generalized ordered-logit equation reports no added fixed effects.
The baseline fit reports no observation or probability weights.

implementation_issues.description: CV_FORECAST is called a coefficient of variation without formula or zero/negative-mean rule; STDEV/MEANEST is only a candidate.
DOWN_REV has conflicting endpoints: before q announcement in prose, before q ends in Table 4 note.
ΔROE uses q−4 in prose and q−1 in Table 4 note; q−4 is used for maximum temporal coverage while retaining the conflict.
Table 5 prints v_it inside the exponential, while Equation (2) and Appendix omit it.
The paper identifies both Compustat and I/B/E/S but omits its historical issuer crosswalk, date/tie policy and auditor company-key join. Local link tables are candidates only.
Big 5 classification requires mapping historical auditor names/keys and carrying auditor status to each quarter.
Winsorization is specified at both 1st-percentile tails, but ties, missing values and pooled versus period-specific cutoffs are not stated.
Current local I/B/E/S products do not establish the precise 1993–1999 historical vintage or EPS adjustment state; the paper notes actual-EPS calculation differences around its sample boundary.

review_notes: Each fit carries the ten-threshold joint-estimation closure and all 14 observed variables.
One-row probes establish access and live fields only; no coordinator coverage confirmation establishes historical/population coverage.
Historical issuer links and current I/B/E/S vintage correspondence remain unresolved; sampled rows/catalog counts are not coverage evidence.

design_coverage.reason: The baseline generalized ordered-logit equation reports no added fixed effects.
The baseline fit reports no observation or probability weights.

implementation_issues.description: CV_FORECAST is called a coefficient of variation without formula or zero/negative-mean rule; STDEV/MEANEST is only a candidate.
DOWN_REV has conflicting endpoints: before q announcement in prose, before q ends in Table 4 note.
ΔROE uses q−4 in prose and q−1 in Table 4 note; q−4 is used for maximum temporal coverage while retaining the conflict.
Table 5 prints v_it inside the exponential, while Equation (2) and Appendix omit it.
The paper identifies both Compustat and I/B/E/S but omits its historical issuer crosswalk, date/tie policy and auditor company-key join. Local link tables are candidates only.
Big 5 classification requires mapping historical auditor names/keys and carrying auditor status to each quarter.
Winsorization is specified at both 1st-percentile tails, but ties, missing values and pooled versus period-specific cutoffs are not stated.
Current local I/B/E/S products do not establish the precise 1993–1999 historical vintage or EPS adjustment state; the paper notes actual-EPS calculation differences around its sample boundary.

review_notes: Each fit carries the ten-threshold joint-estimation closure and all 14 observed variables.
One-row probes establish access and live fields only; no coordinator coverage confirmation establishes historical/population coverage.
Historical issuer links and current I/B/E/S vintage correspondence remain unresolved; sampled rows/catalog counts are not coverage evidence.

The baseline fit reports no observation or probability weights.

implementation_issues.description: CV_FORECAST is called a coefficient of variation without formula or zero/negative-mean rule; STDEV/MEANEST is only a candidate.
DOWN_REV has conflicting endpoints: before q announcement in prose, before q ends in Table 4 note.
ΔROE uses q−4 in prose and q−1 in Table 4 note; q−4 is used for maximum temporal coverage while retaining the conflict.
Table 5 prints v_it inside the exponential, while Equation (2) and Appendix omit it.
The paper identifies both Compustat and I/B/E/S but omits its historical issuer crosswalk, date/tie policy and auditor company-key join. Local link tables are candidates only.
Big 5 classification requires mapping historical auditor names/keys and carrying auditor status to each quarter.
Winsorization is specified at both 1st-percentile tails, but ties, missing values and pooled versus period-specific cutoffs are not stated.
Current local I/B/E/S products do not establish the precise 1993–1999 historical vintage or EPS adjustment state; the paper notes actual-EPS calculation differences around its sample boundary.

review_notes: Each fit carries the ten-threshold joint-estimation closure and all 14 observed variables.
One-row probes establish access and live fields only; no coordinator coverage confirmation establishes historical/population coverage.
Historical issuer links and current I/B/E/S vintage correspondence remain unresolved; sampled rows/catalog counts are not coverage evidence.

The baseline fit reports no observation or probability weights.

implementation_issues.description: CV_FORECAST is called a coefficient of variation without formula or zero/negative-mean rule; STDEV/MEANEST is only a candidate.
DOWN_REV has conflicting endpoints: before q announcement in prose, before q ends in Table 4 note.
ΔROE uses q−4 in prose and q−1 in Table 4 note; q−4 is used for maximum temporal coverage while retaining the conflict.
Table 5 prints v_it inside the exponential, while Equation (2) and Appendix omit it.
The paper identifies both Compustat and I/B/E/S but omits its historical issuer crosswalk, date/tie policy and auditor company-key join. Local link tables are candidates only.
Big 5 classification requires mapping historical auditor names/keys and carrying auditor status to each quarter.
Winsorization is specified at both 1st-percentile tails, but ties, missing values and pooled versus period-specific cutoffs are not stated.
Current local I/B/E/S products do not establish the precise 1993–1999 historical vintage or EPS adjustment state; the paper notes actual-EPS calculation differences around its sample boundary.

review_notes: Each fit carries the ten-threshold joint-estimation closure and all 14 observed variables.
One-row probes establish access and live fields only; no coordinator coverage confirmation establishes historical/population coverage.
Historical issuer links and current I/B/E/S vintage correspondence remain unresolved; sampled rows/catalog counts are not coverage evidence.

Table 5 prints v_it inside the exponential, while Equation (2) and Appendix omit it.

R_t is defined as an ex-dividend stock return for fiscal year t and R_t3 as annual compounded returns in t+1…t+3, but the source does not name the return product/field, exact date interval, return aggregation or beginning-year price convention. CRSP RETX is a plausible candidate, not a verified mapping.

The source gives annual sample labels and a Compustat data vintage, while CRSP uses calendar-dated observations. Use Compustat fyear as the fiscal-year label and datadate/fyr to align CRSP dates; do not substitute filing dates. The exact fiscal-year return endpoints are not stated.

The five-change IS measure at t uses DAP/PDI levels t−5…t. The first primary year (1993) therefore needs DAP from 1988; the 1988 supporting fit’s lagged Assets and prior Sales require raw 1987 accounting data. The source’s stated fit cutoff of 1988 is not the earliest raw predictor year.

The study-level data paragraph excludes financial/regulated SIC 4000–4999 and 6000–6999, while the separate accrual-fit paragraph does not restate whether those sectors are excluded from all 1988–2000 fits. Exact fit population and per-fit Ns remain unspecified.

The primary EPS definition requires split/dividend adjustment and the support/sample inputs refer to legacy Compustat item numbers. Current field labels are plausible matches, but exact mapping and current-vintage treatment must be confirmed before construction.

The study uses the 2004 Compustat combined-industrial annual vintage; the available local COMP.FUNDA probe is a current-vintage file and does not establish historical vintage equivalence or reproduction of the reported sample size.

The source specifies three-standard-deviation winsorization of support-fit regressors each year and primary percentile/extreme screens, but does not fully detail operation order, tie handling, or boundary handling for the reversed fractional IS ranks.

review_notes: The work item’s model formulas agree with the source’s verified Regression (1) and Regression (4) transcriptions. The source specifies PDI=NI−DAP and that both PDI and DAP are beginning-assets deflated; this is retained as construction, not treated as a raw vendor field.

The source’s primary sample period is fiscal-year labels 1993–2000. Its accrual-fit years are 1988–2000, but lagged Assets and ΔSales at the first fit year require raw 1987 records. The first IS at 1993 requires six DAP/PDI levels (1988–1993), not only five levels.

The article excludes SIC 4000–4999 and 6000–6999 for the study-level data; the support-fit paragraph reports two-digit-SIC/year fits and 650 retained cross-sections but does not independently restate that exclusion. The support population remains unresolved.

Local COMP.FUNDA, CRSP.DSF and CCM link-table access/field presence are supported only by the exact preferred one-row probes. No local coverage confirmations were supplied; none of these sampled files is treated as historically or population-complete.

Use current-vintage local sources only as candidate routes with vintage differences noted. Historical Compustat numeric item codes were not mapped by numeric/name resemblance; exact vintage/product mapping and EPS split-adjustment handling remain open.

design_coverage.reason: The source reports annual cross-sectional fits but does not identify any fixed-effect dimension or explicitly state that fixed effects are absent. Year is the repeated-fit dimension, not a year fixed effect.
No observation-level cluster variable is specified. Yearly coefficient averages use the time-series distribution; rating-model tenure coefficients also receive an autocorrelation correction.
No regression weights are reported.
Annual cross-sectional estimates are averaged across 1990–2000; t-statistics use the time-series variability of annual coefficients.

implementation_issues.description: The benchmark, exact return-adjustment convention and estimator for Beta computed from 60 monthly returns are not reported. The CRSP market return used for CAR does not by itself identify this Beta benchmark.

The source uses 2001 Compustat active/research, CRSP and I/B/E/S vintages. Exact historical population, outcome-specific yearly fit N, restricted ≥5-year tenure sample, and issuer/security link coverage are not established by current field probes.

Legacy Compustat items #18, #25/#199, #9/#34/#6, #149, quarterly #8/#61/#17 and S&P #282/#280 must be mapped to source-era series and category codes. The current debt-rating column is not evidence for the separate common-stock ranking measure.

For analyst forecasts the source requires the mean one-year-ahead forecast for t issued immediately after the t−1 earnings announcement. The target fiscal period, origin snapshot and the 1990–2000 sample-year label must be retained separately; exact table-year endpoint convention is not explicit.

For stock/debt ratings, the authors use an additional second-order autocorrelation correction for tenure-related t-statistics. The supplied printed correction-factor equation is corrupted and is not reproducible as transcribed.

Construct Standardized difference: avoid quarterly losses as SDiff_avoid-loss,y = (Observed_left_bin_y − Expected_left_bin_y) / EstimatedSD(Observed − Expected); Expected_left_bin_y = mean(counts in adjacent bins); counts rescaled to N=1,000.. Source definition: Burgstahler–Dichev standardized difference for the avoid-loss threshold (quarterly earnings level deflated by beginning-of-quarter-t stock price) in year y, evaluated in the earnings bin just left of zero. It is the actual observation count minus the expected count, divided by the estimated standard deviation of that difference; the expected count is the average of the two adjacent bins. The authors compute the threshold-year statistic using a standardized N of 1,000 based on the actual bin proportion. Bins have width .0025. A negative value indicates threshold achievement; |statistic| ≥ 2.33 is the stated one-tailed threshold criterion.. At the six-digit input-output industry level, the focal industry’s supplier-industry R&D measure is the sum across supplier industries (excluding the focal industry) of each supplier industry’s annual R&D expense divided by total assets, weighted by its input coefficient: dollars of that supplier industry’s output used to produce one dollar of focal-industry output. Industry R&D is aggregate Compustat R&D expense divided by aggregate industry assets; missing R&D values are set to zero. Where a six-digit IO industry has no Compustat firms, the authors use firms at the five-, four-, two-, then one-digit level. IO weights use the 1987 Use table for 1984–1989, the 1992 table for 1990–1994, and annual updates of the 1992 benchmark tables for 1995–2003.

At the six-digit input-output industry level, the focal industry’s customer-industry R&D measure is the sum across customer industries (excluding the focal industry) of each customer industry’s annual R&D expense divided by total assets, weighted by the percentage of focal-industry output sold to that customer industry. The weights exclude exports and include personal consumption, private fixed investment, and government consumption/investment as final uses. Final-use R&D intensity is set to zero for personal consumption and to the mean customer-industry R&D intensity for private fixed investment and government consumption/investment. Industry R&D is aggregate Compustat R&D expense divided by aggregate industry assets; missing R&D values are set to zero. Where a six-digit IO industry has no Compustat firms, the authors use five-, four-, two-, then one-digit firms. variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Firm-year average of four implied cost-of-equity estimates from the Claus–Thomas, Gebhardt–Lee–Swaminathan (GLS), Ohlson–Juettner–Nauroth (OJ), and Easton modified PEG models. Each estimate is the internal rate of return that equates the stock price with its model-specific expected sequence of residual income or abnormal earnings. CT uses forecast EPS and beginning-of-year book value through T=5, clean-surplus book-value forecasts and a constant payout fraction; terminal residual income grows at expected inflation, proxied by the annualized country-specific median of one-year-ahead realized monthly inflation. GLS uses three explicit forecast years, then linearly fades forecast ROE toward the historic three-year average ROE in a country-year within Campbell industries; negative yearly target returns are replaced by country-industry medians, and residual income is constant from T=12. OJ combines one-year-ahead EPS and dividends with short-term growth equal to the mean of forecast EPS growth from years 1 to 2 and the I/B/E/S five-year growth forecast, and long-term growth equal to expected inflation; a positive forecast earnings change is required. Modified PEG uses one- and two-year-ahead EPS and year-1 dividends, assumes abnormal-earnings growth persists, and requires positive forecast earnings changes including reinvested dividends. Required inputs are the current price, mean analyst EPS forecasts for years 1 and 2, and either year-3 EPS or long-term growth; missing year-3-to-5 EPS forecasts are filled recursively using long-term growth, and missing long-term growth is imputed from the forecast EPS change from years 2 to 3. Prices and mean forecasts are measured at month +7 after fiscal year-end; prices are shifted to the beginning of the fiscal year for full-year discounting. Forecast dividends use the firm’s historic three-year payout ratio, with the country-year median substituted when missing or outside [0,1]. Long-run inflation growth is country-specific; negative inflation is replaced by the country historical median over 1980–2005. IRRs are solved iteratively until imputed and actual prices differ by at most 0.001; only positive estimates are retained. Formula/construction: mean(r_CT, r_GLS, r_OJ, r_PEG).

implementation_issues.description: The ln(B/M) book-equity field and market-value date are unspecified; quarterly Compustat candidates do not resolve this retained predictor.

The EBO definition attributes current-month shares outstanding to I/B/E/S, while the sample section attributes shares to CRSP. The I/B/E/S summary probe has no share-count column; CRSP SHROUT is a candidate, not a resolution.

Indus requires the prior-year industry mean; the first 1979 fit therefore needs 1978 values although the stated valuation sample begins in 1979. The exact prior-year population is unreported and Table 2 gives time-series averages, not the annual series.
The paper cites Fama/French (1997), but current public FF48 definitions reflect later classification changes. The exact historical vintage and SIC assignment policy used in the paper are unresolved.

The Table 7 note lists eight characteristics including log(D/B), but displayed Panel A headers and the Model 1–3 sequence omit D/B. The frozen seven-term RHS is preserved and the source conflict is recorded.
The within-year Fama–MacBeth estimator and Newey–West lag/bandwidth are not specified, so exact coefficient estimation and reported inference are not both recoverable from the source.

For missing Ltg, the source says FY2/FY1 but elsewhere calls the fallback the growth rate implicit in FY1/FY2; it does not say whether to subtract one. Preserve the printed ratio wording pending a source-correct resolution.
The sample requires date-valid Compustat-to-CRSP and I/B/E/S-to-CRSP links plus NYSE/AMEX and ADR filters. Link selection and code mappings are not reported.

requirements.description: Annual accounting fields for ACC_bs/ACC_cf, ΔRevenue, PPE, lagged total assets, DACC inputs, and the Compustat parts of the sample screens.

required_coverage.population: NYSE/AMEX Compustat firms meeting the paper’s statement-data screens and the cross-sectional firm-year pools used to estimate annual industry models.
required_coverage.detail: The 1988–1997 baseline years require t−1 accounting observations for balance-sheet changes, ΔRevenue, and TA(t−1); window arithmetic: 1988–1997 less 12 months = 1987–1997.

routes.mapping_notes: The local current Compustat annual table contains these named columns and descriptive labels. The paper specifies 1998-vintage Compustat numeric item codes (including #4/#5/#1/#34/#14 and cash-flow items #302–308/#124/#125); no field mapping is inferred from item-number/name resemblance. Current fields are candidates for reconstructing the reported accounting definitions, but code meanings, source vintage, and original format selection remain unverified.
routes.coverage_notes: Probe confirms exact-resource access and live fields only. No coordinator confirmation establishes 1987–1997 NYSE/AMEX firm-year, event-free estimation-pool, or statement-item coverage; source vintage is 1998.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The route proves current named fields only. The source vintage is 1998, exact item-number mappings are unverified, and no frozen confirmation establishes full sample or fit-pool coverage.

variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Absolute abnormal accruals, |DACC|, measuring abnormal-accrual magnitude. DACC = TA − ETA (Equation (3)); ETA uses Equation (1) coefficient estimates with (ΔREV − ΔREC) (Equation (2)). The paper defines ΔREC as the change in receivables but does not report its scaling; ΔREV is scaled by total assets at t−1. Formula/construction: |DACC_{i,t}| = |TA_{i,t} − ETA_{i,t}|; ETA_{i,t} = β̂_0(1/A_{i,t−1}) + β̂_1(ΔREV_{i,t} − ΔREC_{i,t}) + β̂_2 PPE_{i,t} + β̂_3 ROA_{i,t−1}; β̂ coefficients are estimated in supporting Equation (1).. The baseline dependent variable is a generated result of its frozen supporting fit; the raw requirements above supply the fit inputs.

Source definition: Natural logarithm of the market value of common equity at fiscal year-end; market value is Compustat shares outstanding times closing share price. Formula/construction: ln(CSHO_{i,t} × PRCL_F_{i,t}).

Source definition: Standard deviation of operating cash flow, with each CFO scaled by total assets at the beginning of the fiscal year. Equation (4) states the window t−4 through t, while Table 3 defines it as t−4 through t−1; the paper does not reconcile these incompatible windows. Formula/construction: SD(CFO_{i,s}), s = t−4,...,t; each CFO is scaled by total assets at the beginning of its fiscal year.
Source definition: Operating cash flow scaled by total assets at the beginning of the fiscal year. Formula/construction: OANCF-XIDOC_{i,t} / AT_{i,t−1}.
Source definition: Total long-term debt (Compustat DLTT) scaled by total assets. Formula/construction: DLTT_{i,t} / AT_{i,t}.
Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if net income is below zero and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1[net income_{i,t} < 0]; 0 otherwise.

Source definition: Market value of equity divided by book value of equity, with book value defined as total assets minus total liabilities (Compustat LT). Formula/construction: market value of equity_{i,t} / (AT_{i,t} − LT_{i,t}).

The stated two-digit SIC ranges are 2833–2836, 3570– 3577, 3600–3674, 5200–5961, and 7370–7370 (as printed in the supplied text). Formula/construction: 1[SIC in {2833–2836, 3570–3577, 3600–3674, 5200–5961, 7370–7370}]; 0 otherwise.

Source definition: Absolute value of prior-year total accruals scaled by total assets at the end of year t−1 (the beginning of fiscal year t). Formula/construction: abs(total accruals_{i,t−1} / AT_{i,t−1}).
Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the company is audited by a Big 4 auditor and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1[Big 4 auditor]; 0 otherwise.
Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if audited by Grant Thornton or BDO Seidman and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1[Grant Thornton or BDO Seidman auditor]; 0 otherwise.

A national (city) specialist has the largest annual audit-fee market share in its two-digit SIC industry and at least a 10-percentage-point lead over the closest competitor in the national (city) market; the city is an MSA. Formula/construction: 1[National Specialist = 1 and City Specialist = 1]; 0 otherwise.

A national (city) specialist has the largest annual audit-fee market share in its two-digit SIC industry and at least a 10-percentage-point lead over the closest competitor in the national (city) market; the city is an MSA. Source definition: Total accruals for company i in year t: income from continuing operations (Compustat IB) minus operating cash flow (OANCF-XIDOC), divided by total assets (AT) at the end of year t−1. Formula/construction: (IB_{i,t} − OANCF-XIDOC_{i,t}) / AT_{i,t−1}. This is an assigned supporting-model input used to construct a baseline measure; retain its fit and all raw components.

Source definition: Reciprocal of total assets for company i at the end of year t−1. Formula/construction: 1 / AT_{i,t−1}. This is an assigned supporting-model input used to construct a baseline measure; retain its fit and all raw components.

Source definition: Change in revenue (Compustat SALE) from the prior year, divided by total assets at the end of year t−1. Formula/construction: (SALE_{i,t} − SALE_{i,t−1}) / AT_{i,t−1}. implementation_issues.description: The source gives conflicting GROWTH definitions: Table 4 specifies 100×(sales_{t−1}/sales_{t−(1+i)})^(1/i), i=3…5, while the narrative uses a different lag/history expression. The t−6 raw start follows the table definition; retain the conflict.
The Appendix A1 expected-value/residual formula has a corrupted summation glyph in the assigned reading; the candidate transcription is not source-confirmed.
The positive/negative RESAVP split and zero treatment are not reported, so its two regressor definitions are not unique.
The beta market-model frequency, estimation sample and window are not specified; the raw window remains unbounded.
EFF requires analyst-by-firm coverage counts over the entire I/B/E/S firm universe, not only focal sample firms; analyst and ticker history must be joined without survivor-only restriction.
Paper’s Compustat inputs came from the 1995 snapshot; current standardized products can differ in restatements, coverage and identifiers.
No analyst EPS split-adjustment product is proven in the local catalog; IBES management-guidance ID/split products do not cover these analyst forecasts and are not substitutes.

variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the outside director leaves the restating company board within three years of the restatement announcement/year, and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1 if the director leaves within three years of the restatement; 0 otherwise..

Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the director is a member of the firm’s audit committee, and 0 otherwise. The reference date for membership is not separately stated. Formula/construction: 1 if audit committee member; 0 otherwise..
Source definition: Number of quarters for which net income is restated. Formula/construction: Count of restated quarters..
Source definition: Product of AUDIT COMM, equal to 1 for an audit committee member and 0 otherwise, and DURATION, the model’s severity measure. Formula/construction: AUDIT COMM × DURATION.

Source definition: Firm stock return over the same three-year window used to measure DEPARTURE or OTHER DIRECTOR LOSS, less the CRSP value-weighted return over that same window; both returns are continuously compounded before differencing. The source does not specify whether the model input is multiplied by 100; descriptive statistics show percentages. Formula/construction: Continuously compounded firm stock return − continuously compounded CRSP value-weighted return over the corresponding three-year outcome window..
Source definition: Total assets in billions at the year-end before the restatement announcement. Formula/construction: Total assets at prior year-end, in $billions..

Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the CEO of the restating company changes within three years of the restatement, and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1 if CEO changes within three years of the restatement; 0 otherwise..
Source definition: Number of directors on the board of the restating company. Measurement date is not separately stated. Formula/construction: Count of directors on the restating company’s board..

Source definition: Board shareholding in the restating company, measured as the percentage of firm equity held by the board as a whole. Measurement date is not separately stated. Formula/construction: 100 × board-held firm equity / total firm equity..

Source definition: Ratio of outside directors to total board size. Measurement date is not separately stated; descriptive statistics report this ratio as a percentage, but regression scaling is not specified. Formula/construction: Outside director count / total board size..

Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the CEO is the company’s founder or belongs to the founding family, and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1 if CEO is founder/founding-family member; 0 otherwise..
Source definition: Age of the director in the restatement year. Formula/construction: Director age in the restatement year..

Source definition: Number of years the director has served on the restating company’s board at the restatement announcement. Formula/construction: Years on the restating company board at announcement..

Source definition: Director’s shareholding in the restating company, measured by the percentage of total company equity held by the director. Measurement date is not separately stated. Formula/construction: 100 × director-held firm equity / total firm equity..

Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the director is CEO of another public company, and 0 otherwise. Reference date is not separately stated. Formula/construction: 1 if director is CEO of another public company; 0 otherwise..

Source definition: Number of outside-director positions the sample director holds in other public companies, excluding the restating company. The measurement date for this RHS control is not stated. Formula/construction: Count of outside-director positions in public companies other than the restating company..

Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the director is a financial expert under the SEC Standards Relating to Listed Company Audit Committee definition, and 0 otherwise. The paper references the SEC definition but does not reproduce its criteria. Formula/construction: 1 if financial expert under the cited SEC definition; 0 otherwise..
Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the director joined the board after the CEO, and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1 if director joined board after CEO; 0 otherwise..

Source definition: Indicator equal to 1 if the director was a net seller of the company’s stock during the misstatement period, and 0 otherwise. Formula/construction: 1 if net seller during misstatement period; 0 otherwise..

variable_coverage.construction: ΔFINC: Difference between the high- and low-Ψ pools’ future-earnings incremental explanatory power estimates within a two-digit SIC industry-year. Each group’s FINC is the unrestricted Equation (4) R² less the restricted current-earnings regression R². Reported formula: ΔFINC_{i,t} = FINC^H_{i,t} − FINC^L_{i,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔΨ: Differential relative firm-specific return variation: the high-Ψ minus low-Ψ group ratio of summed residual sums of squares to summed total sums of squares from weekly firm-return fits, aggregated within each two-digit SIC industry-year. High/low firms are selected as the two top and two bottom firm-year Ψ values within each constituent four-digit SIC industry. Reported formula: ΔΨ_{i,t} = Ψ^H_{i,t} − Ψ^L_{i,t}; each Ψ^g_{i,t} = Σ_{j∈g}Σ_w ε²_{j,w,t} / Σ_{j∈g}Σ_w(r_{j,w,t}−r̄_{j,t})².. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

I: Industry-structure control: square root of the number of firms used to construct the future earnings-response and return-variation measures in the two-digit industry-year; the paper defines it using the number of constituent four-digit industries. Reported formula: I_{i,t} = sqrt(2 n_{i,t}), with n_{i,t} the number of four-digit industries in two-digit SIC industry i in year t.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔS: Difference between the high- and low-Ψ pools' size controls. Section 3.2.1 equation (16) defines each pool measure as the average of log inflation-adjusted total assets, while Table 1 and Table 5 describe it as the log of average inflation-adjusted total assets; the exact order of averaging and logging is unresolved. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔD: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ asset-weighted average diversification. Firm diversification is the number of distinct four-digit lines of business reported in Compustat’s Industry Segment file; weights are total assets. Reported formula: ΔD_{i,t} = D^H_{i,t} − D^L_{i,t}; D^g_{i,t} = Σ_j A_{j,t}s_{j,t}/Σ_j A_{j,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔVE: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ two-digit-industry averages of firm-level five-year standard deviations of past earnings-per-share changes. Earnings changes are scaled by the previous year-end price. Reported formula: ΔVE_{i,t} = VE^H_{i,t} − VE^L_{i,t}; firm volatility is stdev(ΔEPS_t/P_{t−1}) over the prior five years.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔVβ: High-minus-low difference in the two-digit industry beta-volatility control. The Section 3.2 prose says each firm’s standard deviation across twelve monthly CAPM betas is averaged across firms; Table 1 instead says the measure is a simple average of monthly-beta variances within a corresponding four-digit industry. The source does not resolve this aggregation conflict. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔINS: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ two-digit-industry institutional ownership, weighted by firm total assets. Annual firm ownership is the simple average of quarterly ownership; missing ownership values are set to zero. Reported formula: ΔINS_{i,t} = INS^H_{i,t} − INS^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔR&D: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ two-digit-industry total-assets-weighted ratios of research and development expenditures to total assets. Reported formula: ΔR&D_{i,t} = R&D^H_{i,t} − R&D^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Δr: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ two-digit-industry value-weighted stock returns in year t−1. Reported formula: Δr_{i,t} = r^H_{i,t−1} − r^L_{i,t−1}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔFD: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ R² values from fits of current earnings changes on current and one-, two-, and three-year-ahead dividend changes. DIV is dividends per share plus stock-repurchase value over common shares outstanding; ΔDIV is set to zero if a firm neither pays dividends nor repurchases shares. Reported formula: ΔFD_{i,t} = FD^H_{i,t} − FD^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t − r_{f,t}: Firm daily return minus the daily T-bill rate. The source defines the daily rate as the simple rate that compounds over the calendar days in the month to the one-month T-bill return. Reported formula: r_t − r_{f,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t − r_{m,t}: The paper's printed RHS return input is firm daily return minus the value-weighted market return. This is retained exactly as printed, although unusual for a CAPM equation. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

design_coverage.reason: Construct the original firm-year universe by CRSP/Compustat matched records from 1983–1995; delete non-10/11 CUSIP suffix duplicates; assign SIC from the sales-largest business segment; exclude financials and utilities; require uninterrupted weekly-return years; then build four-digit high/low and two-digit industry-year pools.
Use dated GVKEY–PERMNO links and dated segment/company identifiers; sampled fields do not establish historical link completeness.
The baseline uses time-random effects; no fixed-effect dummy family is reported. The time-random-effects panel/year grouping and industry-year inputs are part of the model data.
The paper reports p-values but does not identify a standard-error correction or clustering procedure; no extra cluster variable can be inferred.
No regression weights are reported. Asset weighting is part of construction of selected industry controls (diversification, ownership, R&D), not a fit weight.
Generalized least squares with time-random effects is reported for the frozen baseline; supporting regression estimators, monthly beta fit window, and some variable aggregations remain unspecified.
Preserve the stated sample exclusions, CUSIP duplicate removal, segment-based SIC assignment, top/bottom two firm selection within four-digit SIC, and high-minus-low pool aggregation.

implementation_issues.description: The four supporting regressions’ exact estimators and the monthly beta model’s daily estimation window are not reported; the paper’s equations and labels are preserved without inferring OLS or a beta window.

The paper conflicts on the order of logging and averaging the inflation-adjusted size measure and on beta-volatility aggregation (firm-level standard deviations versus variances of monthly betas). These source alternatives remain unresolved.

The study uses the legacy seasonally adjusted finished-goods PPI series and an historical Compustat/CRSP vintage. Current BLS/Compustat/CRSP data revisions may change the underlying series; no direct replacement is assumed.

variable_coverage.construction: ΔFERC: Difference between the high- and low-Ψ pools’ future-earnings response coefficient estimates within a two-digit SIC industry-year. Each group’s FERC is the sum of the coefficients on future earnings changes one, two, and three years ahead in Equation (4). Reported formula: ΔFERC_{i,t} = FERC^H_{i,t} − FERC^L_{i,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔΨ: Differential relative firm-specific return variation: the high-Ψ minus low-Ψ group ratio of summed residual sums of squares to summed total sums of squares from weekly firm-return fits, aggregated within each two-digit SIC industry-year. High/low firms are selected as the two top and two bottom firm-year Ψ values within each constituent four-digit SIC industry. Reported formula: ΔΨ_{i,t} = Ψ^H_{i,t} − Ψ^L_{i,t}; each Ψ^g_{i,t} = Σ_{j∈g}Σ_w ε²_{j,w,t} / Σ_{j∈g}Σ_w(r_{j,w,t}−r̄_{j,t})².. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

I: Industry-structure control: square root of the number of firms used to construct the future earnings-response and return-variation measures in the two-digit industry-year; the paper defines it using the number of constituent four-digit industries. Reported formula: I_{i,t} = sqrt(2 n_{i,t}), with n_{i,t} the number of four-digit industries in two-digit SIC industry i in year t.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔS: Difference between the high- and low-Ψ pools' size controls. Section 3.2.1 equation (16) defines each pool measure as the average of log inflation-adjusted total assets, while Table 1 and Table 5 describe it as the log of average inflation-adjusted total assets; the exact order of averaging and logging is unresolved. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔD: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ asset-weighted average diversification. Firm diversification is the number of distinct four-digit lines of business reported in Compustat’s Industry Segment file; weights are total assets. Reported formula: ΔD_{i,t} = D^H_{i,t} − D^L_{i,t}; D^g_{i,t} = Σ_j A_{j,t}s_{j,t}/Σ_j A_{j,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔVE: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ two-digit-industry averages of firm-level five-year standard deviations of past earnings-per-share changes. Earnings changes are scaled by the previous year-end price. Reported formula: ΔVE_{i,t} = VE^H_{i,t} − VE^L_{i,t}; firm volatility is stdev(ΔEPS_t/P_{t−1}) over the prior five years.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔVβ: High-minus-low difference in the two-digit industry beta-volatility control. The Section 3.2 prose says each firm’s standard deviation across twelve monthly CAPM betas is averaged across firms; Table 1 instead says the measure is a simple average of monthly-beta variances within a corresponding four-digit industry. The source does not resolve this aggregation conflict. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔINS: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ two-digit-industry institutional ownership, weighted by firm total assets. Annual firm ownership is the simple average of quarterly ownership; missing ownership values are set to zero. Reported formula: ΔINS_{i,t} = INS^H_{i,t} − INS^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔR&D: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ two-digit-industry total-assets-weighted ratios of research and development expenditures to total assets. Reported formula: ΔR&D_{i,t} = R&D^H_{i,t} − R&D^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Δr: Difference between high- and low-Ψ pools’ two-digit-industry value-weighted stock returns in year t−1. Reported formula: Δr_{i,t} = r^H_{i,t−1} − r^L_{i,t−1}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

ΔFD: Difference between high- and low-Ψ groups’ R² values from fits of current earnings changes on current and one-, two-, and three-year-ahead dividend changes. DIV is dividends per share plus stock-repurchase value over common shares outstanding; ΔDIV is set to zero if a firm neither pays dividends nor repurchases shares. Reported formula: ΔFD_{i,t} = FD^H_{i,t} − FD^L_{i,t}.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t − r_{f,t}: Firm daily return minus the daily T-bill rate. The source defines the daily rate as the simple rate that compounds over the calendar days in the month to the one-month T-bill return. Reported formula: r_t − r_{f,t}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

r_t − r_{m,t}: The paper's printed RHS return input is firm daily return minus the value-weighted market return. This is retained exactly as printed, although unusual for a CAPM equation. design_coverage.reason: Construct the original firm-year universe by CRSP/Compustat matched records from 1983–1995; delete non-10/11 CUSIP suffix duplicates; assign SIC from the sales-largest business segment; exclude financials and utilities; require uninterrupted weekly-return years; then build four-digit high/low and two-digit industry-year pools.
Use dated GVKEY–PERMNO links and dated segment/company identifiers; sampled fields do not establish historical link completeness.
The baseline uses time-random effects; no fixed-effect dummy family is reported. The time-random-effects panel/year grouping and industry-year inputs are part of the model data.
The paper reports p-values but does not identify a standard-error correction or clustering procedure; no extra cluster variable can be inferred.
No regression weights are reported. Asset weighting is part of construction of selected industry controls (diversification, ownership, R&D), not a fit weight.
Generalized least squares with time-random effects is reported for the frozen baseline; supporting regression estimators, monthly beta fit window, and some variable aggregations remain unspecified.
Preserve the stated sample exclusions, CUSIP duplicate removal, segment-based SIC assignment, top/bottom two firm selection within four-digit SIC, and high-minus-low pool aggregation.
