variable_coverage.construction: ACCURACY: Negative absolute value of the I/B/E/S analysts’ mean annual earnings forecast minus actual I/B/E/S earnings, divided by the stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year. Higher values indicate more accurate forecasts. Formula: −|mean I/B/E/S annual EPS forecast − actual I/B/E/S EPS| / prior fiscal-year-end stock price. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

SUE: Absolute unexpected earnings scaled by the stock price at the end of the prior year; unexpected earnings equals actual earnings less the mean analyst forecast. Formula: |actual earnings − mean analyst forecast| / prior-year-end stock price. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BIAS: Signed forecast error scaled by stock price at the end of the prior fiscal year; forecast error equals the I/B/E/S mean annual analyst forecast less actual I/B/E/S earnings. Formula: (mean I/B/E/S annual EPS forecast − actual I/B/E/S EPS) / prior fiscal-year-end stock price. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

SMTH1: Negative of the ratio of the rolling standard deviation of income before extraordinary items scaled by average total assets to the rolling standard deviation of cash flow from operations scaled by average total assets; rolling calculation requires at least three and at most five years. Cash flow from operations equals income before extraordinary items minus accruals; accruals equal change in current assets minus change in current liabilities minus change in cash plus change in current debt in current liabilities minus depreciation and amortization. Larger values (closer to zero) indicate smoother earnings. Formula: − SD(NI before extraordinary items / average total assets) / SD(CFO / average total assets). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
LNASSETS: Log of total assets measured in millions of U.S. dollars. Formula: ln(total assets in USD millions). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
LEV: Total debt divided by total assets. Formula: total debt / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
BM: Ratio of book value to market value of equity. Formula: book value of equity / market value of equity. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

STD_SALES: Standard deviation of sales, used to capture volatility in the firm’s operating environment. The paper does not state its scaling or calculation window. Formula: standard deviation of sales. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%LOSS: Proportion of years in which the firm experiences losses over the last three to five years. Formula: loss years / years in the 3–5-year history. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPCYCLE: Log of days of accounts receivable plus inventories. Formula: ln(days accounts receivable + inventory days). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SG: Average sales growth over the past three to five years. Formula: average sales growth over prior 3–5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPLEV: Net property, plant, and equipment divided by total assets. Formula: net PP&E / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AVECFO: Average cash flow from operations divided by total assets, measured over the last five years. Formula: average(CFO / total assets) over past 5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

SMTH2: Negative of the level correlation between cash flow from operations and total accruals. Table 2 says both inputs are scaled by average total assets, whereas Appendix A says total assets; the denominator wording conflicts. It is calculated over rolling windows requiring at least three and at most five years, and larger values (closer to one) indicate smoother earnings. The source does not specify an exact formula. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

LEV: Total debt divided by total assets. Formula: total debt / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
BM: Ratio of book value to market value of equity. Formula: book value of equity / market value of equity. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

STD_SALES: Standard deviation of sales, used to capture volatility in the firm’s operating environment. The paper does not state its scaling or calculation window. Formula: standard deviation of sales. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%LOSS: Proportion of years in which the firm experiences losses over the last three to five years. Formula: loss years / years in the 3–5-year history. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPCYCLE: Log of days of accounts receivable plus inventories. Formula: ln(days accounts receivable + inventory days). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SG: Average sales growth over the past three to five years. Formula: average sales growth over prior 3–5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPLEV: Net property, plant, and equipment divided by total assets. Formula: net PP&E / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AVECFO: Average cash flow from operations divided by total assets, measured over the last five years. Formula: average(CFO / total assets) over past 5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ILLIQ: Combined illiquidity measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of available ZERORET and LN(BIDASK); if BIDASK is unavailable, use the percentile rank of ZERORET. ZERORET is the percent of fiscal-year trading days with no price change. BIDASK is the fiscal-year median relative bid–ask spread, (ASK−BID)/((ASK+BID)/2), and LN(BIDASK) is the transformed component. The reference population and scaling convention for “scaled percentile rank” are not reported. Formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ZERORET), scaled_percentile_rank(ln(BIDASK))) when BIDASK available; scaled_percentile_rank(ZERORET) otherwise. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

LNMVE: Natural logarithm of market value of equity at fiscal year-end, with MVE measured in U.S. dollars (millions). Formula: ln(MVE). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
BM: Book value of common equity divided by market value of equity. Formula: book value of common equity / market value of equity. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

LOSS: Indicator equal to 1 if net income before extraordinary items is negative, and 0 otherwise. Formula: 1(NI before extraordinary items < 0). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
STDRET: Annual standard deviation of monthly stock returns. Formula: annual SD(monthly stock returns). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ADR EX: Indicator equal to 1 if the firm trades on a U.S. exchange during the year, and 0 otherwise. Formula: 1(trades on a U.S. exchange during year). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ADR NEX: Indicator equal to 1 if the firm has an ADR but is not traded on a U.S. exchange during the year, and 0 otherwise. Formula: 1(has ADR and is not traded on a U.S. exchange during year). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%CLHLD H: Percentage of the firm’s shares that are closely held if that proportion exceeds the sample median of %CLHLD, and 0 otherwise; %CLHLD is the average proportion of shares closely held at the end of year t. Formula: %CLHLD × 1(%CLHLD > sample median). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%CLHLD L: Percentage of the firm’s shares that are closely held if that proportion is below the sample median of %CLHLD, and 0 otherwise; %CLHLD is the average proportion of shares closely held at the end of year t. Formula: %CLHLD × 1(%CLHLD < sample median). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

FUND SMTHC: Control for fundamental earnings smoothness: average of the scaled percentile ranks of the fitted values for SMTH1 and SMTH2 from the fundamental smoothness regression. SMTH1 and SMTH2 definitions and the required construction regressions are recorded in their supporting models. Formula: average(scaled percentile rank(FUND SMTH1), scaled percentile rank(FUND SMTH2)). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

TRANS: Aggregate firm-level transparency measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of ANALYST, R ACCURACY, INTGAAP S, BIG5, and (1−DIS SMTHC); if R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the remaining four components. ANALYST is the average number of analysts forecasting year t earnings over the SMTH estimation period. R ACCURACY is the residual from a fitted regression of ACCURACY on SUE and BIAS; ACCURACY is the negative absolute I/B/E/S mean annual forecast error (mean forecast less reported actual earnings) scaled by prior fiscal-year-end stock price, SUE is absolute unexpected earnings (actual less mean forecast) scaled by prior-year price, and BIAS is the signed I/B/E/S forecast error scaled by prior fiscal-year-end price. INTGAAP S indicates a firm reporting under IFRS or U.S. GAAP with above-median transparency excluding INTGAAP and a mandatory or voluntary international-standards adoption. BIG5 indicates a Big-5-affiliated auditor. DIS SMTHC is the average scaled percentile rank of the residuals from the SMTH1 and SMTH2 fundamental-smoothness fits. The percentile-rank reference population and scaling convention are not reported. Formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); when R ACCURACY is unavailable, average the four remaining scaled percentile ranks. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Formula: (mean I/B/E/S annual EPS forecast − actual I/B/E/S EPS) / prior fiscal-year-end stock price. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

SMTH1: Negative of the ratio of the rolling standard deviation of income before extraordinary items scaled by average total assets to the rolling standard deviation of cash flow from operations scaled by average total assets; rolling calculation requires at least three and at most five years. Cash flow from operations equals income before extraordinary items minus accruals; accruals equal change in current assets minus change in current liabilities minus change in cash plus change in current debt in current liabilities minus depreciation and amortization. Larger values (closer to zero) indicate smoother earnings. Formula: − SD(NI before extraordinary items / average total assets) / SD(CFO / average total assets). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
LNASSETS: Log of total assets measured in millions of U.S. dollars. Formula: ln(total assets in USD millions). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
LEV: Total debt divided by total assets. Formula: total debt / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
BM: Ratio of book value to market value of equity. Formula: book value of equity / market value of equity. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

STD_SALES: Standard deviation of sales, used to capture volatility in the firm’s operating environment. The paper does not state its scaling or calculation window. Formula: standard deviation of sales. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%LOSS: Proportion of years in which the firm experiences losses over the last three to five years. Formula: loss years / years in the 3–5-year history. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPCYCLE: Log of days of accounts receivable plus inventories. Formula: ln(days accounts receivable + inventory days). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SG: Average sales growth over the past three to five years. Formula: average sales growth over prior 3–5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPLEV: Net property, plant, and equipment divided by total assets. Formula: net PP&E / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AVECFO: Average cash flow from operations divided by total assets, measured over the last five years. Formula: average(CFO / total assets) over past 5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

SMTH2: Negative of the level correlation between cash flow from operations and total accruals. Table 2 says both inputs are scaled by average total assets, whereas Appendix A says total assets; the denominator wording conflicts. It is calculated over rolling windows requiring at least three and at most five years, and larger values (closer to one) indicate smoother earnings. The source does not specify an exact formula. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
LNASSETS: Log of total assets measured in millions of U.S. dollars. Formula: ln(total assets in USD millions). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
LEV: Total debt divided by total assets. Formula: total debt / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
BM: Ratio of book value to market value of equity. Formula: book value of equity / market value of equity. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

STD_SALES: Standard deviation of sales, used to capture volatility in the firm’s operating environment. The paper does not state its scaling or calculation window. Formula: standard deviation of sales. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%LOSS: Proportion of years in which the firm experiences losses over the last three to five years. Formula: loss years / years in the 3–5-year history. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPCYCLE: Log of days of accounts receivable plus inventories. Formula: ln(days accounts receivable + inventory days). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SG: Average sales growth over the past three to five years. Formula: average sales growth over prior 3–5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
OPLEV: Net property, plant, and equipment divided by total assets. Formula: net PP&E / total assets. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AVECFO: Average cash flow from operations divided by total assets, measured over the last five years. Formula: average(CFO / total assets) over past 5 years. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ILLIQ: Combined illiquidity measure: average of the scaled percentile ranks of available ZERORET and LN(BIDASK); if BIDASK is unavailable, use the percentile rank of ZERORET. ZERORET is the percent of fiscal-year trading days with no price change. BIDASK is the fiscal-year median relative bid–ask spread, (ASK−BID)/((ASK+BID)/2), and LN(BIDASK) is the transformed component. The reference population and scaling convention for “scaled percentile rank” are not reported. Formula: average(scaled_percentile_rank(ZERORET), scaled_percentile_rank(ln(BIDASK))) when BIDASK available; scaled_percentile_rank(ZERORET) otherwise. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

LNMVE: Natural logarithm of market value of equity at fiscal year-end, with MVE measured in U.S. dollars (millions). Formula: ln(MVE). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
BM: Book value of common equity divided by market value of equity. Formula: book value of common equity / market value of equity. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

LOSS: Indicator equal to 1 if net income before extraordinary items is negative, and 0 otherwise. Formula: 1(NI before extraordinary items < 0). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
STDRET: Annual standard deviation of monthly stock returns. Formula: annual SD(monthly stock returns). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ADR EX: Indicator equal to 1 if the firm trades on a U.S. exchange during the year, and 0 otherwise. Formula: 1(trades on a U.S. exchange during year). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ADR NEX: Indicator equal to 1 if the firm has an ADR but is not traded on a U.S. exchange during the year, and 0 otherwise. Formula: 1(has ADR and is not traded on a U.S. exchange during year). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%CLHLD H: Percentage of the firm’s shares that are closely held if that proportion exceeds the sample median of %CLHLD, and 0 otherwise; %CLHLD is the average proportion of shares closely held at the end of year t. Formula: %CLHLD × 1(%CLHLD > sample median). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%CLHLD L: Percentage of the firm’s shares that are closely held if that proportion is below the sample median of %CLHLD, and 0 otherwise; %CLHLD is the average proportion of shares closely held at the end of year t. Formula: %CLHLD × 1(%CLHLD < sample median). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

FUND SMTHC: Control for fundamental earnings smoothness: average of the scaled percentile ranks of the fitted values for SMTH1 and SMTH2 from the fundamental smoothness regression. SMTH1 and SMTH2 definitions and the required construction regressions are recorded in their supporting models. Formula: average(scaled percentile rank(FUND SMTH1), scaled percentile rank(FUND SMTH2)). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%CLHLD H × TRANS: Interaction between %CLHLD H (the closely held-share proportion when above the sample median, zero otherwise) and TRANS. TRANS averages the scaled ranks of analyst following, residual forecast accuracy, serious IFRS/U.S.-GAAP adoption, Big-5 auditor, and one minus discretionary smoothness; it falls back to four components when R ACCURACY is unavailable. The paper uses separate high- and low-ownership interaction terms in full-sample Table 7 column 1. Formula: %CLHLD_H × average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); omit R ACCURACY when unavailable. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

%CLHLD L × TRANS: Interaction between %CLHLD L (the closely held-share proportion when below the sample median, zero otherwise) and TRANS. TRANS averages the scaled ranks of analyst following, residual forecast accuracy, serious IFRS/U.S.-GAAP adoption, Big-5 auditor, and one minus discretionary smoothness; it falls back to four components when R ACCURACY is unavailable. The paper uses separate high- and low-ownership interaction terms in full-sample Table 7 column 1. Formula: %CLHLD_L × average(scaled_percentile_rank(ANALYST), scaled_percentile_rank(R ACCURACY), scaled_percentile_rank(INTGAAP S), scaled_percentile_rank(BIG5), scaled_percentile_rank(1−DIS SMTHC)); omit R ACCURACY when unavailable. variable_coverage.construction: PRICE: Price per share three months after the end of fiscal year t; measured in dollars per share. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

BVE: Book value of equity at the end of year t divided by the number of shares outstanding; measured in dollars per share. Reported formula: BVE_it = book value of equity at end of year t / shares outstanding.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

PVINCOME: Present value of expected future abnormal earnings for years t+1 through t+3. Expected EPS1, EPS2, and EPS3 are proxied by mean analyst forecasts AF1_post, AF2_post, and AF3_post issued after the year-t earnings announcement. AF3_post is the mean long-term earnings-growth forecast multiplied by AF2_post, as stated. Expected book value rolls forward as BVE1 = BVE + expected EPS1 - expected dividends1 and BVE2 = BVE1 + expected EPS2 - expected dividends2. Expected dividends in years 1 and 2 equal expected EPS times PAYOUT. PAYOUT is the prior-three-year average dividends-to-net-income ratio; if a year has negative net income, that year’s net income is set to 6% of total assets for this calculation. Cost of equity r is max(Rf + beta*(Rm-Rf), Rf); Rf is the year-end 10-year Treasury Note rate and Rm-Rf is fixed at 7.6%. Beta is the estimated coefficient on the CRSP value-weighted index including dividends from a market-model regression using daily returns over the 250 trading days before the year-t earnings announcement. Reported formula: PVINCOME_it = [E_t(EPS1_it) - r_it*E_t(BVE_it)]/(1+r_it) + [E_t(EPS2_it) - r_it*E_t(BVE1_it)]/(1+r_it)^2 + [E_t(EPS3_it) - r_it*E_t(BVE2_it)]/[(1+r_it)^2*r_it]; E_t(BVE1_it)=BVE_it+E_t(EPS1_it)-E_t(DIV1_it); E_t(BVE2_it)=E_t(BVE1_it)+E_t(EPS2_it)-E_t(DIV2_it); E_t(DIVj_it)=E_t(EPSj_it)*PAYOUT_it (j=1,2); r_it=max(Rf_t+beta_it*(Rm-Rf),Rf_t), Rm-Rf=7.6%.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

MEET1: Indicator equal to one when the current-year earnings surprise is at least −$0.005 per share (one-half cent), and zero otherwise. PVINCOME: Present value of expected future abnormal earnings for years t+1 through t+3. Expected EPS1, EPS2, and EPS3 are proxied by mean analyst forecasts AF1_post, AF2_post, and AF3_post issued after the year-t earnings announcement. AF3_post is the mean long-term earnings-growth forecast multiplied by AF2_post, as stated. Expected book value rolls forward as BVE1 = BVE + expected EPS1 - expected dividends1 and BVE2 = BVE1 + expected EPS2 - expected dividends2. Expected dividends in years 1 and 2 equal expected EPS times PAYOUT. PAYOUT is the prior-three-year average dividends-to-net-income ratio; if a year has negative net income, that year’s net income is set to 6% of total assets for this calculation. Cost of equity r is max(Rf + beta*(Rm-Rf), Rf); Rf is the year-end 10-year Treasury Note rate and Rm-Rf is fixed at 7.6%. Beta is the estimated coefficient on the CRSP value-weighted index including dividends from a market-model regression using daily returns over the 250 trading days before the year-t earnings announcement. Reported formula: PVINCOME_it = [E_t(EPS1_it) - r_it*E_t(BVE_it)]/(1+r_it) + [E_t(EPS2_it) - r_it*E_t(BVE1_it)]/(1+r_it)^2 + [E_t(EPS3_it) - r_it*E_t(BVE2_it)]/[(1+r_it)^2*r_it]; E_t(BVE1_it)=BVE_it+E_t(EPS1_it)-E_t(DIV1_it); E_t(BVE2_it)=E_t(BVE1_it)+E_t(EPS2_it)-E_t(DIV2_it); E_t(DIVj_it)=E_t(EPSj_it)*PAYOUT_it (j=1,2); r_it=max(Rf_t+beta_it*(Rm-Rf),Rf_t), Rm-Rf=7.6%.. Leverage: debt (Compustat items #9 debt in current liabilities plus #34 long-term debt) divided by total shareholders’ equity (item #216).
Times-interest-earned: operating income after depreciation (Compustat item #178) divided by interest expense (item #15).

For all four fits the year-0 portfolio rank remains fixed while audit outcomes and control variables are contemporaneous at each horizon.

Per-share residual-income intrinsic-value measure based on current book value and expected future abnormal earnings. EPS forecasts for years +1 and +2 are IBES means; for fewer than 5% of firm-years, IBES forecasts are available through year +5, and otherwise the mean long-term growth forecast g is applied recursively to the preceding mean forecast for years +3 to +5. Future book value follows the ex-ante clean-surplus relation: prior book value plus forecast EPS minus forecast dividends. Current indicated annual dividends divided by year+1 EPS forecast define the payout ratio; it is held constant for future dividends and winsorized to lie between 10% and 50%. Indicated annual dividends are four times the latest quarter’s declared dividends, and EPS1 is used as deflator. The discount rate k_t is the 10-year Treasury yield on April 1 of t+1 plus beta times a 5% equity risk premium; beta is the same-year median beta of firms in the same beta decile. The underlying beta estimator is not stated. P1 assumes abnormal earnings remain constant after year +5. The Appendix A terminal term is transcribed as printed with unbound s; its horizon/exponent meaning is unresolved.. Preserve Appendix A’s item codes and product definitions; the live route confirms only field presence and requires independent semantic/date linkage. The source’s printed P1 terminal term and P3 ROE horizon conflict with its prose; do not replace them with a silent correction.

MVE=ln[(December 31 t−1 share price × shares outstanding × applicable Worldscope FX conversion)/1,000,000]. Natural log is specified; current market input/FX fields and code identity are unverified.
DISCLOSE is the country-of-domicile count across eight specified disclosure areas where domestic GAAP has no/weaker requirement than IAS, based on standards in force 1993-01-01.

requirements.description: Compustat annual financial statement, price, share and industry fields needed for the 1994–2003 firm-year population, MJT/APMJ construction, volatility controls and second-stage controls.

required_coverage.population: U.S. Compustat firm-years eligible under the paper’s Compustat cash-flow-history rule, including FF48 industry-year peer cells.
required_coverage.detail: Anchor 1994–2003; source Appendix B σCFO/σREV needs t−5…t and each annual ratio uses lagged assets, so earliest raw year is 1988 for t=1994; first-stage lagged-assets and Δsales/receivables also require prior-year records. Current data vintage is used. The source says Compustat cash-flow data are available starting in 1988, matching this computed raw-history requirement; no broader local coverage is inferred.

routes.mapping_notes: Annual Compustat raw fields are semantically mapped using the paper’s definitions and live catalog labels: IB/income before extraordinary items, OANCF/operating cash flow, SALE, RECT, PPEGT/gross PPE, AT, PRCC_F, CSHO and CEQ. The source also uses historical Compustat item numbers (notably total debt item 181) and leaves several year indices/denominators unstated; those mappings remain unverified.
routes.coverage_notes: The exact file and columns were read by the shared bounded probe. No coordinator coverage confirmation supports complete firm-year history or the 1994–2003 sample population; local historical coverage remains unverified.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Exact live access/columns are proven; population coverage is not. The underlying source-vintage sample and current Compustat historical coverage are not confirmed.

requirements.description: Broader Compustat FF48 industry-year peer population used to estimate modified-Jones discretionary accruals before applying the final five-year volatility-history screen.

required_coverage.population: Compustat peer firms in the target sample’s 1994–2003 FF48 industry-year cells, with t−1 history for lagged assets and revenue changes; accrual estimation is performed without the later five-year volatility-data restriction.
required_coverage.detail: The source says the first-stage accruals are estimated before imposing the five-year volatility rule and requires at least 10 observations per FF48 industry-year cell, but does not report the precise peer universe, missing-data filters or cell counts. The transformed volatility input reaches t−6 after its within-window lagged-assets denominator.

routes.mapping_notes: Fields support modified-Jones peer regressions for the final sample’s target firm-years, including FF48 industry-year cells with at least 10 observations. The source explicitly says these accruals are estimated before imposing the five-year volatility-data restriction; exact peer inclusion/missingness rules remain unresolved.
routes.coverage_notes: Exact local file/fields are verified by the shared probe. The broader first-stage peer population and its historical coverage are not confirmed.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The first-stage sample is broader than the final volatility-complete baseline sample; exact peer eligibility and local historical coverage remain unverified.

requirements.description: Compustat field timing for simulation controls whose year index/denominator period is unstated (CFO, logTA/logMVE, LEV and M/B).

required_coverage.population: The same 1994–2003 Compustat sample firms; source does not state the observation-year index for every named control.
required_coverage.detail: The target period is 1994–2003, but the source does not say whether CFO is divided by current or lagged assets and does not consistently state time indices for these controls. Preserve unknown raw-year bounds.

routes.mapping_notes: The source identifies these Compustat measures but does not specify current versus lagged total assets for CFO, nor the year index for logTA, logMVE, leverage and M/B in all simulation fits.
routes.coverage_notes: Bounds are intentionally null because these source definitions do not fix the relevant fiscal-year row; the panel anchor alone is insufficient to assign exact historical dates.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Exact local fields are present, but the paper’s timing choice is unresolved; no finite raw-year interval is licensed.

requirements.description: Source timing and scaling specification for σCFO/σREV used in PART generation, controls and the transformed accrual fit.

required_coverage.frequency: annual firm-year and rolling volatility window
required_coverage.population: Compustat firm-years for the 1994–2003 study observations, with raw history for each rolling volatility calculation.
required_coverage.detail: Appendix B supports t−5…t for main volatility measures; Table 1 says current year plus the prior four years; the transformed fit uses σCFO over t−5…t−1. Each constituent CFO/revenue ratio uses total assets at s−1, extending the raw span one year before the rolling window.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The paper gives conflicting windows: Table 1 says current year plus the prior four years, while Appendix B says t−5…t; the transformed WLS fit uses t−5…t−1. Each annual CFO and cash-based revenue value in these windows is scaled by assets at s−1, so the conservative raw-history union reaches t−6. Preserve the windows and inner scaling separately.

requirements.description: Performance-matching inputs and assignment for APMJ: same industry-year firm with closest ROA.

required_coverage.population: Eligible firms in the same industry-year comparison population as each sample firm.
required_coverage.detail: Source specifies same industry-year and closest ROA, but does not fully state the ROA formula, tie/missing-value handling, or whether any matching candidate exclusions apply.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The comparison rule is partly described but its ranking variable and edge-case rules are unresolved.

variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Absolute value of the modified-Jones total discretionary-accrual residual (MJT). Formula: |MJT| Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route).

Source definition: Continuous partitioning variable formed as a weighted combination of one of logTA (log total assets), σCFO (cash-flow standard deviation scaled by lagged total assets), or σREV (cash-based-revenue standard deviation scaled by lagged total assets), and a random error term. Across 20 settings, the weight on the selected target increases while the error-term weight decreases, generating approximately 0%–95% correlations. The source does not give the exact coefficients or full formula; the volatility-window statements conflict.  Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route).

Source definition: Natural logarithm of market value of equity. Formula: ln(market value of equity) Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). Exact observation-year/denominator timing remains unstated in the paper.

Source definition: Cash flows from operations, deflated by total assets. The table note does not identify whether current or lagged total assets are used. Formula: cash flows from operations / total assets Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). Exact observation-year/denominator timing remains unstated in the paper.

Source definition: Sales growth defined by sales in year t divided by sales in year t−1. Formula: Sales_t / Sales_{t−1} Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route).

Source definition: Ratio of total debt (Compustat data item 181) to total assets; the table does not specify the year index. Formula: total debt / total assets Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). Exact observation-year/denominator timing remains unstated in the paper.

Source definition: Market-to-book ratio, defined as price times shares divided by common equity. Formula: (price × shares) / common equity Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). Exact observation-year/denominator timing remains unstated in the paper.

Source definition: Total accruals: income before extraordinary items (Compustat data 123) less cash from operations (data 308), divided by lagged total assets. Formula: (NIBE − CFO)/lagged total assets Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). TACC is income before extraordinary items less CFO, scaled by lagged total assets.

Source definition: Change in sales adjusted for the change in receivables, divided by lagged total assets. Formula: (ΔSales − ΔAccountsReceivable)/lagged total assets Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). The source defines adjusted revenue change as Δsales less Δreceivables, divided by lagged assets.

Source definition: Gross property, plant, and equipment divided by lagged total assets. Formula: Gross PPE/lagged total assets Raw source: Compustat annual fields in r_comp_annual (GVKEY/datadate and the item fields mapped in the local route). Use gross PP&E (PPEGT) scaled by lagged assets.

requirements.description: I/B/E/S U.S. quarterly firm earnings observations and the most timely individual analyst forecast available strictly before the quarter’s earnings report date, plus fiscal-quarter key and event/forecast timing fields needed to form surprise distributions and annual fiscal-year summaries. Required fiscal years are 1984–1999; the paper requires a report date and at least one earlier forecast per observation. The current local Detail History product has candidate actual, forecast, fiscal-period and timing columns, but their semantic mapping to the historical detail-file fields remains unverified.

required_coverage.frequency: Quarterly firm events/forecasts; outcomes aggregated by fiscal year.
required_coverage.population: U.S. I/B/E/S detail-file firm-quarter earnings observations with a quarterly report date and at least one analyst forecast before that date; the source reports 176,519 observations.
required_coverage.detail: Original fiscal years 1984–1999; raw inputs are quarterly actual earnings, individual forecast values and forecast dates, fiscal period ends, report/event dates, currency/measure and U.S.-firm indicators. No lag, lead, or rolling estimation window is specified.

The assigned source requires reported EPS less the most recent individual forecast dated before the earnings report. for a December year-end firm, the pre -mandatory-adoption window is 2003
and 2004, while the post -mandatory-adoption window is 2005 and 2006.

evidence.quote:
For each firm-year, we retrieve all annual earnings forecasts
issued during the 12-month period prior to the year-end from each analyst covering the firm.
evidence.description: Defines annual forecast lookback and per-analyst firm-year selection base.

evidence.quote:
If an analyst issues more than one annual forecast for
a firm-year, we retain only the last forecast.
evidence.description: Defines forecast selection within analyst-firm-year.

evidence.quote: Thus, our sample is composed of a constant set of analyst-firm pairs matched across the pre - and post- mandatoryadoption windows.
evidence.description: Defines constant analyst-firm-pair composition for forecast outcomes.

evidence.quote:
We require that annual
earnings announcements be made no later than 240 calendar days after the
fiscal year-end.
evidence.description: Defines the announcement-date cutoff after fiscal year-end.

sample period based on the ADR databases of the Bank of New York and
Citibank.

primary exchange listing during our sample period.

Exhibit 21 country text matching is an imperfect classifier and requires manual review of country-name ambiguities; the paper notes this issue.

evidence.quote: Uncorrected: An indicator variable equal to one if the loan is issued during a period of an uncorrected material internal control weakness. We define this period from the day of the first material internal control weakness through the day of the first report where the weakness has been corrected.

evidence.quote: Revolver: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan’s type is revolver, zero otherwise.
evidence.description: icw_financial_covenants Revolver source definition

evidence.quote: Interest Rate: The interest rate is based on the All-in-Drawn-Spread measure reported by DealScan. This measure is equal to the amount the borrower pays in basis points over LIBOR for each dollar drawn down, so it accounts for both the spread of the loan and the annual fee paid to the bank group. LPC always uses the LIBOR spread or the LIBORequivalent spread option to calculate the All-in-Drawn spread.
evidence.description: icw_financial_covenants Interest Rate source definition

evidence.quote: Secured: An indicator variable taking the value of one if the loan is backed by collateral, zero otherwise.

evidence.quote: Loan Size: A logarithm of the loan’s amount.
evidence.description: icw_financial_covenants Loan Size source definition

evidence.quote: Maturity: The number of months between the facility’s issue date and the date when the loan matures.
evidence.description: icw_financial_covenants Maturity source definition

evidence.quote: Credit Rating: The numerical equivalent of S&P, Moody’s, Fitch, or DPR senior debt rating. It is set as equal to 1 for the highest senior debt rating, through 27 for the lowest senior debt rating. For firms not rated by S&P, we assign the Moody’s senior debt rating; for firms not rated by either S&P or Moody’s, we assign the Fitch senior debt rating; finally, for firms not rated by S&P, Moody’s, or Fitch, we assign the DPR senior debt rating. We use a conventional conversion scheme to match ratings from all four rating agencies. The corporate credit rating variable is set to 28 for firms without an available S&P, Moody’s, Fitch, or DPR debt rating. Credit ratings are collected from the S&P Historical Rating Database and from the Mergent FISD database. Financial Covenants: The number of financial covenants imposed by the loan agreement.

TA_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1}: Total accruals scaled by total assets at t−1. Total accruals are EBXI (Compustat annual item 123; earnings before extraordinary items and discontinued operations) less CFO from continuing operations (Compustat annual item 308 less item 124). Source formula: TA_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

ΔSALES_{it} / Assets_{i,t−1}: Change in revenues from t−1 to t (Compustat annual item 12), scaled by prior-year total assets (item 6). Source formula: ΔSALES_{it} / Assets_{i,t−1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

PPE_{it} / Assets_{i,t−1}: Gross property, plant and equipment (Compustat annual item 7), scaled by prior-year total assets (item 6). Source formula: PPE_{it} / Assets_{i,t−1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

DISX_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1}: Discretionary expenditures are advertising (Compustat annual item 45), R&D (item 46), and SG&A (item 189), scaled by total assets at t−1 (item 6). If SG&A is available, missing advertising and R&D are set to zero. Source formula: DISX_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

1 / Assets_{i,t−1}: Inverse of prior-year total assets (Compustat annual item 6). Source formula: 1 / Assets_{i,t−1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

SALES_{i,t−1} / Assets_{i,t−1}: Annual sales revenues from the preceding fiscal year (Compustat item 12), scaled by total assets at t−1 (item 6). Source formula: SALES_{i,t−1} / Assets_{i,t−1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

DROA1: First difference in annual ROA in year 1 after the SEO, adjusted by subtracting the change in ROA of a size- and performance-matched nonissuing firm. ROA is income before extraordinary items divided by beginning-of-period total assets. Source formula: ΔROA_{issuer,year 1} − ΔROA_{matched nonissuer,year 1}. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

RM_2: Year-0 aggregate real earnings management proxy equal to abnormal cash flows from operations and abnormal discretionary expenses, both multiplied by negative one, then summed. Source formula: −R_CFO − R_DISX. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

Discretionary accruals: Year-0 (SEO-year) discretionary accruals. DA is total accruals scaled by assets at t−1 less fitted normal accruals from Eq. (1). Total accruals are Compustat 123 earnings before extraordinary items and discontinued operations minus operating cash flows from continuing operations, Compustat 308 less 124. The normal-accrual fit uses the displayed scaled constant, change in revenue, and gross PPE, each divided by lagged assets. Source formula: (TA_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1}) − [k̂1/Assets_{i,t−1} + k̂2·ΔSALES_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1} + k̂3·PPE_{it}/Assets_{i,t−1}]. Raw resource mapped to COMP.FUNDA annual fields listed in R-COMP-ANNUAL; exact historical item-number mapping remains as described in the requirement.

−DCOL_t=−{[(LCT_t−DLC_t)−(LCT_{t−1}−DLC_{t−1})]/average AT_t}; preserve the Table 5 negative-liability term.

design_coverage.reason: The selected fit is annual cross-sectional OLS; the paper describes 40 separate annual regressions and reports no fixed-effect dummies. Annual grouping is part of the estimator, not evidence of year fixed effects.
No clustered standard errors are reported for this baseline; the paper reports Fama–MacBeth t-statistics across the annual coefficient series.
Table 5 Panel C equation and notes do not name a weight variable or weighting procedure.

implementation_issues.description: The paper specifies that ROA and accrual components are deflated by average total assets but does not define the average-assets endpoints or exact fiscal-year/date convention. For annual ROA_{t+1}, this affects which AT observations are paired with OIADP_{t+1}; for t accrual measures it affects scaling alongside the t−1 changes.

The sample footnote requires Compustat item 12 in current and previous years but does not state its semantic item name. The current Funda SALE field is only an unverified candidate; it is not mapped by item-number/name resemblance. The sample cannot be exactly filtered until this mapping is resolved.

The article identifies the SIC exclusion range but not the source field (Compustat SICH vs CRSP HSICCD) or whether SIC is evaluated at the financial year-end, another date, or a different annual classification. This can change which firms are included.

The Compustat–CRSP matched sample needs effective-dated GVKEY/PERMNO links, but the paper does not report the link product, linktype/linkprim/used-flag filters, multiple-security treatment, or exact match date.

The table specifies numeric winsorization bounds +1 and −1 but does not specify which annual regression variables are treated as “each component of earnings,” whether winsorization is cross-sectional by year or pooled, or its order relative to deflation.
The authors report Fama–MacBeth means and t-statistics from 40 annual cross-sections but do not state any serial-correlation adjustment or exact finite-sample t-statistic formula.

The displayed final multivariate row reports t-statistics under the seven accrual terms but not under the intercept or ROA_t; the regression-specific annual Ns are not reported. Preserve these omissions rather than infer model statistics from descriptive counts.

The assessment routes to current local Compustat and CRSP tables while retaining the paper’s 1962–2001 design; the authors’ contemporaneous data vintage and any historical vendor revisions are not identified.

The paper’s item wording distinguishes item 1 “Cash and Short Term Investments” from item 193 “Short Term Investments”; use CHE only for the former and IVST only for the latter. The local labels support this split, but any alternative label/source interpretation should be resolved before construction.

Estimate Equation 4 in annual cross-sections and report mean coefficients over 43 years; t-statistics use the standard error of those coefficients. The paper does not name the within-year cross-sectional estimator, so it remains unknown.

implementation_issues.description: Table 3 caption says earnings is scaled by lagged price, while Table 1 and Appendix A specify net income before extraordinary items divided by lagged market value of equity, with Appendix A identifying data25×data199. The assessment uses Appendix A’s explicit formula and flags the Table 3 wording; the paper does not explain whether “price” is shorthand for a per-share equivalent.

Equation (2) visually repeats μ1 for the size/M/B/leverage terms, but Equation (4) and Table 3 specify distinct return-characteristic terms, consistent with μ1–μ4. Use the complete Equation (4) RHS and flag the Equation (2) display typo.

The paper cites historical Compustat item numbers, while the local annual file exposes named fields. Do not equate items 25, 199, 60, 9, 34, or 18 to fields by number/name resemblance; an authoritative historical item crosswalk and units/date definitions are needed for exact field mapping.

The paper states 1962–2005 data and 1963–2005 firm-year fits, but annual CRSP returns begin in month four after actual fiscal year end and compound twelve monthly returns. Fiscal-year labels 2005 can therefore require monthly CRSP observations in 2006–2007; actual datadate-to-return dates must be checked rather than treating fyear labels as calendar return years.

The annual Fama–MacBeth aggregation is reported, but the within-year cross-sectional estimator is not named. Preserve it as unknown rather than infer OLS; choosing an estimator is an implementation issue for exact coefficient replication.

requirements.description: Compustat annual event-year accounting variables, auditor-opinion code, SIC, auditor and firm identifiers for all baseline fits.

required_coverage.population: 1980–1997 qualified-report event firms and matched clean controls; also the larger support-fit populations
required_coverage.detail: Fields support TA, BP, MKTCAP, DE, PERFORM, auditor opinion and matching. The earliest time-series Jones event is 1980; its eight-year fit begins 1972, and within-fit predictor lags require 1971 values. The paper nevertheless says 1972 is the first available data year.

routes.mapping_notes: Catalog labels and exact probe verify annual fields corresponding to the paper’s Compustat items and explicit opinion coding. `auop` codes 1/2 are specified by the paper.
routes.coverage_notes: A bounded probe verifies access and columns only. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this resource and required period/population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No coordinator coverage confirmation establishes the 1971–1997 event, fit and matched-control populations; paper vintage starts at 1972, creating a one-year support-fit boundary tension.

requirements.description: Apply the 1980–1997 event-year sample restrictions and match 173 qualified firms to 173 clean controls on year, two-digit SIC industry, auditor type and nearest total assets.

required_coverage.population: Initial Compustat observations screened for qualified opinion, one qualification per firm, complete/nonnegative accounting controls and classifiable SIC; final 173 matched pairs
required_coverage.detail: The source reports 112,384 initial firm-years, then staged exclusions, 173 unique qualified firms, and 173 controls. The exact nearest-assets tie-break and auditor-type crosswalk are not supplied.

routes.mapping_notes: Fields support opinion, industry, auditor and size matching; the auditor-type classification and nearest-asset tie rule remain unspecified.
routes.coverage_notes: A bounded probe verifies access and columns only. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this resource and required period/population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Exact match-pair construction and screening history cannot be verified from the bounded field probe or without a complete sample/population confirmation.

requirements.description: Firm-specific time-series Jones OLS support fits for each event-year firm using the eight annual observations ending immediately before the event year, plus event-year DA raw measures.

required_coverage.population: All event firms with the required pre-event eight-year history, before the later baseline missing-value and matched-pair screens
required_coverage.detail: For event year t, fit rows are t−8 through t−1; each row’s ΔTA and ΔRevenue predictors use t−1 values, so raw inputs begin t−9. For 1980 events this means fit years 1972–1979 and raw years back to 1971.

routes.mapping_notes: The Jones OLS dependent variable and predictor fields are present. An eight-year per-firm estimation population is distinct from the final 173 matched pairs.
routes.coverage_notes: A bounded probe verifies access and columns only. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this resource and required period/population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No coverage confirmation establishes complete per-firm eight-year histories. The stated 1972 first-year availability conflicts with the lagged 1971 raw balance/revenue values required for 1980 fits.

requirements.description: Cross-sectional Jones support-fit rows within each event-year × two-digit SIC cell.

required_coverage.frequency: annual firm-year observations by event year and 2-digit SIC cell
required_coverage.population: All firms in each event-year × two-digit SIC estimation cell before applying the final matched qualified/control screen; exact cell population requires confirmation
required_coverage.detail: Support models use current-year and lagged annual fields. The event-year 1980 cell requires 1979 lag data. The source reports variable cell sizes and a median fit N, not a common population cutoff.

routes.mapping_notes: Annual Jones fields and SIC are live; the full eligible firm population in each cell and whether later sample screens enter the fit are not fully specified.
routes.coverage_notes: A bounded probe verifies access and columns only. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this resource and required period/population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No coverage confirmation verifies the full year×industry support-fit population or the paper’s exact cell inclusion rule.

variable_coverage.construction: Total accruals in year t, scaled by total assets at the end of year t−1. requirements.description: Daily Datastream firm-security data to construct closing quoted spreads, daily returns/zero returns, quarterly price impact, return variability, market value, and daily share turnover. USD trading volume can be constructed as share Volume × close_usd; market value can be built from close_usd × numshrs.

required_coverage.population: International firm securities in up to 35 IFRS treatment countries (24 EU) and 21 benchmark countries. For the supporting trading-cost fit, the source reports 699,517 quarterly estimates, exceeding the 561,590 factor-regression observations; therefore inputs must include the broader support-fit population before factor complete cases and later baseline screens. The exact firm/security roster and local coverage are unconfirmed.
required_coverage.detail: Baseline outcomes and supporting models run in 2001Q1–2009Q4. The three firm controls are lagged four calendar quarters, so the earliest raw control quarter is 2000Q1; the union is 2000Q1–2009Q4. Window arithmetic: anchor 2001–2009 plus 12-month lookback gives the conservative year envelope 2000–2009.

variable_coverage.construction: For each firm security and trading day compute (ask−bid)/the quote midpoint from closing bid/ask, then take the quarterly median and natural log. Datastream is the primary source; the paper supplements Bloomberg spreads for Czech Republic, Luxembourg, Slovakia, and Slovenia and CRSP spreads for U.S. firms in unspecified early years.

Code the post-mandate IFRS observation for firms in the Table 1 EU countries whose IFRS mandate was bundled with substantive enforcement changes; use actual Worldscope fiscal-period-end dates, the quarter-after-first-fiscal-year-end rule, ITEM7536 for IFRS reporting, and the dated Datastream–Worldscope firm link.

Code the post-mandate IFRS observation for the remaining EU countries without bundled enforcement changes, using Table 1 country coding, the firm’s actual Worldscope fiscal-period-end date, the following-calendar-quarter switch, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
Code post-mandate IFRS observations for non-EU IFRS adoption countries using Table 1 membership/date, actual firm fiscal-year ends, Worldscope ITEM7536, and the dated security-to-firm link.
At quarter end compute close_usd×numshrs/1,000,000 for market value in US$ millions, lag four calendar quarters, then take the natural log.
For each trading day compute US$ turnover as share Volume×close_usd divided by same-day market value close_usd×numshrs; take the quarter median at t−4, then take the natural log.
Compute the standard deviation of daily Datastream returns within quarter t−4, then take the natural log.

review_notes: The paper’s Table 3 column (6) is the selected three-quarter-year-trends baseline; no later robustness specification or WLS sensitivity model is added.

variable_coverage.construction: Estimate the quarterly firm-level total round-trip trading-cost proxy from daily security returns and the equal-weighted local-market return series using the cited log-likelihood system; impose the stated ≥24 daily returns, ≥20% nonzero-return, and ≥1 basis-point estimate filters. This is a generated support measure from two jointly required raw series.
Use the daily equal-weighted local market index return series paired to each firm-day as the aggregate-market-return input to the quarterly trading-cost system.

For each firm-quarter form the four proxy inputs: median daily closing spread using the quote midpoint; zero returns divided by all potential trading days; median daily absolute return/USD volume excluding zero-return days; and the nested quarterly total-trading-cost estimate. Extract the first/only factor with eigenvalue>1 and compute ln(score+1). The cost-estimation output and the other proxies are all required inputs.

Code the post-mandate IFRS observation for firms in the Table 1 EU countries with bundled enforcement changes, using actual firm fiscal-year ends, the following-calendar-quarter switch, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
Code post-mandate IFRS observations for the remaining EU countries without bundled enforcement changes, using Table 1 country coding, actual firm fiscal-year ends, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
Code post-mandate IFRS observations for non-EU adoption countries using Table 1 country/date coding, actual fiscal-year ends, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
At quarter end compute close_usd×numshrs/1,000,000, lag four calendar quarters, and take the natural log.
Compute daily US$ share turnover as Volume×close_usd divided by same-day close_usd×numshrs, take the quarter median at t−4, and take the natural log.
Compute the within-quarter standard deviation of daily Datastream returns at t−4 and take the natural log.

design_coverage.reason: The selected Table 3 column (6) reports OLS and does not specify observation weights; no additional weight data are required for this baseline.

implementation_issues.description: The sample screen excludes firms with average market value below US$5 million, but the paper does not state the averaging period or whether the average is daily, quarterly, or over a different window. This prevents an exact reconstruction of the retained firm population.

Table 1 supplies country groups and mandate dates, and the paper defines activation using the quarter after each firm’s first fiscal-year end after the mandate. The available Datastream and Worldscope probes are current local snapshots, while the article was published in 2013. Historical values, security links, and coverage may differ from the authors’ extraction vintage.

The total-trading-cost proxy is extracted by a quarterly log-likelihood system from daily security and equal-weighted local index returns, with 24-return, 20%-nonzero, and 1-basis-point filters. The article does not print the likelihood system or all parameter/return conventions; it points to Lesmond et al. (1999) and an appendix in Daske et al. (2008), so that implementation must be confirmed before the supporting fit can be reproduced exactly.

The liquidity-factor rule specifies factor analysis and the first/only eigenvalue above one, but does not specify the extraction method, input standardization, score normalization/sign, or missing-input handling. These choices affect the exact factor score passed through ln(score+1).

The paper requires equal-weighted local market index returns but does not identify the exact index series or country-market construction. The local Datastream index RI and constituent/weight tables are candidate inputs; neither verifies the paper’s equal-weighted index definition or all required country/date coverage.

The zero-return denominator is all potential trading days per quarter. The Datastream date field does not establish whether every potential exchange session is represented when a firm has no valid return; the exchange calendar/observation rule is unresolved.

The paper says CRSP adds U.S. bid/ask data in the early sample years but does not state the cutoff years or exact CRSP product/quote-time convention. The local CRSP daily file has candidate BID/ASK fields, but the exact required dates and Datastream-to-CRSP firm match remain unverified.

review_notes: Table 2 reports 699,517 total-trading-cost observations versus 561,590 liquidity-factor observations. The support input population is therefore assessed before the smaller factor complete-case/regression sample; do not restrict support inputs to the final factor N.
The paper requires Bloomberg spreads for four smaller EU markets and CRSP spreads for early-year U.S. observations in addition to Datastream. The exact CRSP early-year cutoff is not printed.
The Datastream index series and constituent table were inspected as candidate local-market inputs; fields alone do not verify the equal-weighted series used by the authors.

evidence.description: Sample exclusions based on accounting standards and cross-listing.

evidence.description: Two-way standard-error clustering.

evidence.description: Quarterly median of daily quoted spreads.

evidence.quote: difference between the bid and ask price divided by the mid-point and measured at the end of each trading day
evidence.description: Daily closing quoted percentage spread definition.

evidence.description: Zero-return numerator and potential-trading-day denominator.

evidence.quote:
Price Impact is the quarterly median of the Amihud (2002) illiquidity measure (i.e., daily absolute stock
return divided by US$ trading volume).

evidence.description: Source description of quarterly return-cost estimation.

evidence.quote: we eliminate estimates below one basis point
evidence.description: Support-fit estimated-cost filter.

routes.source_name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission EDGAR
routes.mapping_notes: EDGAR filings are unstructured source documents. A public route exists, but extracting only the fiscal-year MD&A, identifying the correct 10-K/accession and linking it to Compustat remain manual/coverage questions.
routes.coverage_notes: SEC developer resources document public HTTPS access to EDGAR filings and filing indexes. This establishes a raw filing route, not complete MD&A extraction, filing-year matching or historical CIK coverage for the paper sample.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The route to historical state-of-incorporation by firm-year is not verified; a current company state or a filing header is not presumed to be complete for all years.

requirements.description: Fama–French 48 industry mapping needed for the industry fixed effects and industry-level clustered standard errors.

required_coverage.population: Compustat sample firm-years assigned to Fama–French 48 industries during 2000–2012.
required_coverage.detail: The source names FF48 industries. The current public definition assigns firms by SIC and June timing, but the paper’s exact vintage and assignment at fiscal year versus calendar year are not specified. Helper window check: anchor 2000–2012; lookback 0 months, lead 0 months gives conservative envelope 2000–2012.

routes.source_name: Kenneth R. French Data Library, 48 Industry Portfolio definitions
routes.mapping_notes: Official current FF48 definitions use four-digit SIC codes and annual June assignment. Historical category membership/revision vintage and the paper’s exact SIC source remain unverified.
routes.coverage_notes: The official 48-industry page exposes a downloadable industry-definition file and states the SIC-based portfolio assignment timing. This is the current public classification route; the exact historical classification vintage used in the paper is not identified.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The current public classification route is identified, but historical mapping vintage and exact paper-year assignment are not confirmed.

variable_coverage.construction: Fog: Gunning Fog Index for the MD&A section of the current annual report. It is 0.4 times words per sentence plus percent of complex words; words per sentence is total words divided by MD&A sentences, and complex words have at least three syllables. Reported formula: 0.4 × (words per sentence + percent of complex words). Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

MBE: Indicator equal to 1 when ΔEPS, the change in EPS from year t−1 to t, falls in the neighborhood from zero through the positive threshold; otherwise 0. The main tests use EPS before extraordinary items. Table 4 columns I, II, and III use intervals [$0, $0.01], [$0, $0.02], and [$0, $0.03], respectively. Reported formula: 1{0 ≤ ΔEPS ≤ cutoff}; 0 otherwise, with cutoff = $0.01, $0.02, or $0.03 per share in columns I–III. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

NegEarnChg: Indicator equal to 1 when ΔEPS, the change in EPS from year t−1 to t, is negative. Reported formula: 1{ΔEPS < 0}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Earnings: Operating earnings scaled by total assets. The research-design prose specifies beginning total assets; Appendix A specifies total assets at fiscal year-end. The denominator is therefore unresolved. The supplied text also does not operationalize the operating-earnings numerator beyond that label. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Loss: Indicator equal to 1 when Earnings is below zero. Reported formula: 1{Earnings < 0}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Size: Log of market value of equity at fiscal year-end. Appendix A does not specify the log base. Reported formula: log(market value of equity at fiscal year-end). Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

MTB: Market value of equity plus book value of liabilities, divided by book value of total assets, measured at fiscal year-end. Reported formula: (market value of equity + book value of liabilities) / book value of total assets. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Age: Number of years since the firm first appears in the CRSP monthly stock return file. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

SpecItems: Amount of special items divided by total assets; the source does not specify the total-assets timing. Reported formula: special items / total assets. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

EarnVol: Standard deviation of operating earnings during the prior five years. Reported formula: SD(operating earnings during the prior five years). Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

RetVol: Standard deviation of monthly stock returns in the prior year. Reported formula: SD(monthly stock returns in the prior year). Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

NBSeg: Natural logarithm of the number of business segments. The source does not report a zero-count handling rule. Reported formula: ln(number of business segments). Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

NGSeg: Natural logarithm of the number of geographic segments. The source does not report a zero-count handling rule. Reported formula: ln(number of geographic segments). Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

NItems: Number of Compustat items with non-missing values. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

M&A: Appendix A states that the indicator is 1 for firm-years in which the firm is an acquirer according to SDC Platinum M&A and also says “1 otherwise.” The non-acquirer coding is unclear. variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Natural log of the ratio of mean squared market-model-adjusted returns over announcement days −1, 0, and +1 to the variance of firm i’s market-model residuals during the non-event period. The non-event window is days −60 to −10 and +10 to +60 relative to the I/B/E/S earnings-announcement date. Formula: ln(mean(u_it² over event days −1, 0, +1) / variance of market-model residuals in the non-event period). Inputs/route requirements: r_datastream_daily, r_event_dates. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Indicator equal to one for firm-years in countries that adopted IFRS and zero for the control sample from countries retaining domestic accounting standards. Formula: 1 if firm-year is in an IFRS-adopting country; 0 otherwise.. Inputs/route requirements: r_ifrs_country_group, r_worldscope_annual. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

implementation_issues.description: The full source sample requires I/B/E/S announcements, Datastream daily returns/volume, and Worldscope annual fields for the exact 2002–2007 event/country population. Current field probes do not establish historical sample coverage, source vintages, required 40-day windows, $100 million screen, zero-return filter or country minimums.

Datastream InfoCode, Worldscope code, I/B/E/S ticker, firm identifier and country membership must be linked on valid dates. Existing probes show join-key columns but do not verify sample-specific links or equal-weighted within-country benchmark membership.

UE and DISP use analyst forecasts and a corresponding closing stock-price denominator. The exact estimate target/origin snapshot and denominator price date are not specified; the audit keeps actual-EPS, forecast-origin and closing-price dates separate.

Country-level controls rule of law, insider-trading enforcement, CIFAR and CAP/GDP lack exact source years/transforms and, for CAP/GDP, exact stock-versus-flow alignment. Their dates and routes remain unresolved.

Country-level IFRS group membership, treatment of mandatory vs voluntary adopters, and industry fixed-effect coding need source-matched country/industry maps; Worldscope field presence does not establish these classifications.

The market-model/event construction is source-described, including ±60-trading-day non-event windows and a 40-observation minimum on both sides. The exact current Datastream RI/VO/MV field mapping, currency convention and OLS estimation details still need source-vintage verification.

Book-to-market = book assets / (book assets - book equity + market value of equity), measured in the year before announcement. Equity field, market-value date and fiscal alignment are not stated; paper price-adjusts financial data to 1998.

implementation_issues.description: The Table 8 column (1) sample is reported as N=474 (237 cases and 237 controls), while Table 2's 237-case endpoint is described as requiring complete accounting and CRSP announcement-return data. The paper does not explicitly connect Table 8 case membership to that return-based screen, so the exact frozen case set is not identified by the text.

The eligible control-firm population, replacement and tie rules, all eligibility/missing-data screens, the control covariate date, and the explicit conditional-logit group ID are unreported. The source gives SIC fallback and a natural-log market-value caliper but these do not uniquely generate 237 controls or strata.

The reported sample period is an initial filing-date window, but predictor timing is relative to a going-private announcement and financial inputs are annual/fiscal. Announcement-to-filing offsets, prior-year fiscal label/end alignment, and the control-firm reference date are not specified.

The selected Table 8 FCF note uses (OIBD less tax expense plus deferred taxes less dividends)/assets; footnote 17 instead subtracts interest, defines current tax as item 16 less the change in item 35, and uses beginning-of-year assets. The source conflict is retained; the reported construction cannot be fully reconciled.
ROA is defined only as return on assets; no numerator, denominator, average-assets endpoints, or exact fiscal period is reported.

SalesGr is labeled prior-year sales growth but its formula, denominator, scaling and inflation-adjustment order are not specified. At least one additional prior fiscal-year sales observation is needed beyond the prior-year level.
Turnover is average monthly share turnover, with share volume divided by shares outstanding, but the averaging order, CRSP share units/conversion and exact prior-year monthly window are unspecified.

Table 8 parenthetical statistics are not identified as t-statistics, standard errors or another statistic, and no standard-error/variance correction or clustering is reported; coefficient inference cannot be matched exactly.

Historical CIK-to-GVKEY and GVKEY-to-PERMNO links are available as candidate tables, but the paper does not state link filters, primary security selection, issuer-versus-subject CIK choice, or validity-date rules; local field probes do not establish link coverage.

Current local Compustat/CRSP snapshots and current BEA historical estimates may differ from study-era data; the BEA series is now indexed to a later base and would be rebased to 1998. Preserve current-vintage differences in any reconstruction.

variable_coverage.construction: Deflate annual Compustat Global/NA XOPR using the country-year GDP deflator and compute ln(XOPR_t)−ln(XOPR_{t−1}); use the paper’s main XOPR measure excluding depreciation. Local xopr is a candidate field and its exact depreciation treatment is not confirmed.
Deflate annual SALE by the same country-specific GDP deflator and compute ln(SALE_t)−ln(SALE_{t−1}). Preserve the fiscal-year label and date separately.

Multiply the mean-zero EPL index, defined as (late-1990s REGEPL+TEMPEPL)/2, by current deflated DlnSALE. The public OECD components are available; firm-country linking and sample means require reconstruction.
Multiply contemporaneous annual real GDPGROWTH_{n,t} by DlnSALE_t. Current WDI provides a public candidate series; exact source vintage, country key and firm-year alignment remain unverified.
Compute AINT_t=ln(AT_t/SALE_t) and multiply it by current deflated DlnSALE. AINT and continuous controls are mean-zero rescaled per footnote 39.
Multiply the paper-defined common-law indicator (Australia, Canada, Ireland, UK, US = 1; other sample countries = 0) by current deflated DlnSALE.

Code DEC_t=1 when sales decrease in year t and multiply DEC_t by current deflated DlnSALE. The paper does not separately state whether the decrease flag is computed on nominal or deflated sales; use of the real SALE definition is a candidate mapping.
Multiply the mean-zero country EPL index, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE. EPL is static at the late-1990s reference; DEC_t is contemporaneous.

Multiply DEC_{t−1}, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE. DEC_{t−1} is a prior-year sales-decrease indicator and requires sales at t−1 and t−2; do not absorb that t−2 raw input into the start of the estimation sample.
Multiply contemporaneous GDPGROWTH_{n,t}, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE; the country-year growth input is contemporaneous even though the sales difference needs t−1.
Multiply current AINT_t, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE; AINT is ln(AT_t/SALE_t), with the continuous control mean-zero rescaled.
Multiply the paper-defined common-law-country indicator, DEC_t and current deflated DlnSALE.

The selected Model A equation is pooled across the firm-year panel without country or year fixed effects; those effects appear only in a separate sensitivity specification. Country-level random slope shocks are part of the composite error, not a fitted fixed-effects dimension.
Two-way clustering is by country and year; cluster-key construction must follow the same historical country and annual t mapping as the analysis panel.
No regression weights are reported for Model A.

The authors combine the level-1 and country-level equations and estimate pooled OLS under their stated zero-mean/exogeneity assumptions; do not substitute a random-coefficients ML or separate country-by-country fits.
