implementation_issues.description: The article reports 128,333 firm-years and 15,833 firms but does not give an exact observation roster or Global/North America allocation. Local probes confirm selected columns/readability only; no coordinator confirmation establishes the 1988–2008 source history or 1990–2008 estimation population.

The main XOPR measure excludes depreciation, while the local Compustat label for xopr is only “Operating Expenses - Total.” The exact source calculation and product mapping for both Global and North America remain unverified.

Firm-country selection, native-currency screening and joins to World Bank/OECD country keys are not fully specified. Available fic/loc fields are current identifiers, not verified historical country assignments; the non-financial industry screen also has no reported code rule.

The article cites the World Bank Databank but gives no exact GDP-deflator indicator code or vintage. Current WDI provides a GDP deflator index and annual inflation series; the exact deflator field used for real XOPR/SALE is not confirmed, and current values may differ from the paper-era snapshot.

The paper cites World Bank annual GDP growth without an indicator code or frozen vintage; current NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG is a public candidate, but the historical values, full 19-country-year coverage and the Compustat fyear-to-calendar-year join are not verified.

The paper specifies 1% tail exclusions and sales-change screens but does not state the percentile reference population/order of operations. Reproduce the stated filters without substituting winsorization; exact sample recovery remains unverified.

DEC is defined as a sales decrease, and the equation includes prior-year DEC(t−1), but the separate construction of the decrease flag from nominal versus deflated sales is not stated. Preserve the explicit t−1 indicator and its t−2 raw sales need.

review_notes: Only the frozen Model A main sample, Table 5 column (a), is assessed. Columns (b)–(d), Table 6–7 specifications and other robustness analyses are excluded.

The article’s source window is Compustat 1988–2008, but the retained estimation panel is 1990–2008 because the first two years support differences, prior-decrease predictors and screening. The DEC(t−1) construction separately requires SALES through t−2.
Compustat Global and North America are jointly required components; their local routes are not substitutes for one another and no local coverage confirmation establishes the sample.
The official OECD table is the cited late-1990s EPL source; WDI current series are public candidates but not evidence of the paper’s historical World Bank vintage or complete sample-country coverage.
Equation (3) and its printed PDF rendering were inspected: Model A includes DEC(t−1) in the current sales-decrease slope and is estimated by pooled OLS with two-way country/year clustering.

variable_coverage.construction: AdjROA_{t+1}: Industry-adjusted ROA at t+1: firm-specific ROA minus the median ROA in the same year and two-digit SIC industry; ROA is income before extraordinary items divided by lagged total assets. Formula: ROA_{t+1} − median(ROA_{same year, two-digit SIC}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BEAT_t: Indicator equal to 1 when net income divided by total assets is at least 0.01, or the change in net income divided by total assets from t−1 to t is at least 0.01, and BENCH is not 1; 0 otherwise. The earnings variables are scaled by beginning-of-year assets. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t≥0.01 or ΔNI-scaled_t≥0.01, and BENCH_t≠1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

JUSTMISS_t: Indicator equal to 1 when net income or its change from t−1 to t, each scaled by total assets, is at least −0.01 but below zero, and neither BENCH nor BEAT is 1; 0 otherwise. The earnings variables are scaled by beginning-of-year assets. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t∈[−0.01,0) or ΔNI-scaled_t∈[−0.01,0), and BENCH_t≠1, BEAT_t≠1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BENCH_t: Indicator equal to 1 when either net income divided by total assets or the change in net income divided by total assets from t−1 to t is at least 0 and less than 0.01; 0 otherwise. The paper elsewhere describes the denominators as total assets at the beginning of the year. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t∈[0,0.01) or ΔNI-scaled_t∈[0,0.01)}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

R&D RM_t: Indicator equal to 1 if the residual from the normal R&D expense model (Equation 1) is in the lowest quintile; 0 otherwise. Formula: 1{residual(Eq.1) in lowest quintile}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BENCH_t × R&D RM_t: Product of BENCH_t and R&D RM_t; each component is the indicator defined in the paper, so the interaction equals one only when both indicators equal one. Formula: BENCH_t × R&D RM_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AdjROA_t: Industry-adjusted ROA: firm-specific ROA minus median ROA in the same year and two-digit SIC industry; ROA is income before extraordinary items divided by lagged total assets. Formula: ROA_t − median(ROA_{same year, two-digit SIC}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SIZE_t: Natural logarithm of total assets. Formula: ln(total assets_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MTB_t: Market value of equity divided by book value of equity. Formula: market value of equity_t / book value of equity_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RETURN_t: Size-adjusted abnormal return: monthly buy-and-hold raw return minus the monthly buy-and-hold return on a size-matched decile portfolio, compounded over the 12 months of fiscal year t. Formula: compound_{12 months in fiscal year t}(monthly buy-and-hold raw return − monthly buy-and-hold size-decile portfolio return). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ZSCORE_{t−1}: Modified Altman financial-health measure lagged one period in Equation (6): 3.3×net income/lagged assets + 1.0×sales/lagged assets + 1.4×retained earnings/lagged assets + 1.2×working capital/lagged assets. Formula: ZSCORE_{t−1}; ZSCORE_t=3.3(NI_t/A_{t−1})+1.0(Sales_t/A_{t−1})+1.4(RetainedEarnings_t/A_{t−1})+1.2(WorkingCapital_t/A_{t−1}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
RD_t/A_{t−1}: R&D expense (COMPUSTAT Data46) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: RD_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
1/A_{t−1}: Reciprocal of total assets at t−1, the scaled constant regressor printed in the model. Formula: 1/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MV_t: Natural logarithm of market value, calculated from COMPUSTAT Data199 × Data25. Formula: ln(Data199_t × Data25_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Q_t: Tobin’s Q, calculated using the COMPUSTAT items shown in the paper: ((Data199×Data25)+Data130+Data9+Data34)/Data6. The paper does not further define those data items in this description. Formula: ((Data199_t×Data25_t)+Data130_t+Data9_t+Data34_t)/Data6_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

INT_t/A_{t−1}: Internal funds (COMPUSTAT Data18 + Data46 + Data14) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: (Data18_t+Data46_t+Data14_t)/Data6_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
RD_{t−1}/A_{t−1}: Prior-year R&D expense (COMPUSTAT Data46) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: RD_{t−1}/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BEAT_t: Indicator equal to 1 when net income divided by total assets is at least 0.01, or the change in net income divided by total assets from t−1 to t is at least 0.01, and BENCH is not 1; 0 otherwise. The earnings variables are scaled by beginning-of-year assets. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t≥0.01 or ΔNI-scaled_t≥0.01, and BENCH_t≠1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

JUSTMISS_t: Indicator equal to 1 when net income or its change from t−1 to t, each scaled by total assets, is at least −0.01 but below zero, and neither BENCH nor BEAT is 1; 0 otherwise. The earnings variables are scaled by beginning-of-year assets. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t∈[−0.01,0) or ΔNI-scaled_t∈[−0.01,0), and BENCH_t≠1, BEAT_t≠1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BENCH_t: Indicator equal to 1 when either net income divided by total assets or the change in net income divided by total assets from t−1 to t is at least 0 and less than 0.01; 0 otherwise. The paper elsewhere describes the denominators as total assets at the beginning of the year. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t∈[0,0.01) or ΔNI-scaled_t∈[0,0.01)}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Aggregate RM_t: Indicator equal to 1 if the sum of residuals from R&D model 1, SG&A model 2, and the production component multiplied by −1 is in the lowest quintile; 0 otherwise. The source labels the production component “model 3,” although its production-cost equation is model 4. Formula: 1{lowest quintile of residual(Eq.1)+residual(Eq.2)−residual(production-cost model)}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BENCH_t × Aggregate RM_t: Product of BENCH_t and Aggregate RM_t; each component is the indicator defined in the paper, so the interaction equals one only when both indicators equal one. Formula: BENCH_t × Aggregate RM_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AdjROA_t: Industry-adjusted ROA: firm-specific ROA minus median ROA in the same year and two-digit SIC industry; ROA is income before extraordinary items divided by lagged total assets. Formula: ROA_t − median(ROA_{same year, two-digit SIC}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SIZE_t: Natural logarithm of total assets. Formula: ln(total assets_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MTB_t: Market value of equity divided by book value of equity. Formula: market value of equity_t / book value of equity_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RETURN_t: Size-adjusted abnormal return: monthly buy-and-hold raw return minus the monthly buy-and-hold return on a size-matched decile portfolio, compounded over the 12 months of fiscal year t. Formula: compound_{12 months in fiscal year t}(monthly buy-and-hold raw return − monthly buy-and-hold size-decile portfolio return). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ZSCORE_{t−1}: Modified Altman financial-health measure lagged one period in Equation (6): 3.3×net income/lagged assets + 1.0×sales/lagged assets + 1.4×retained earnings/lagged assets + 1.2×working capital/lagged assets. Formula: ZSCORE_{t−1}; ZSCORE_t=3.3(NI_t/A_{t−1})+1.0(Sales_t/A_{t−1})+1.4(RetainedEarnings_t/A_{t−1})+1.2(WorkingCapital_t/A_{t−1}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

PROD_t/A_{t−1}: Production costs, defined as cost of goods sold plus change in inventory (COMPUSTAT Data41 + Data303), divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: PROD_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
1/A_{t−1}: Reciprocal of total assets at t−1, the scaled constant regressor printed in the model. Formula: 1/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MV_t: Natural logarithm of market value, calculated from COMPUSTAT Data199 × Data25. Formula: ln(Data199_t × Data25_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Q_t: Tobin’s Q, calculated using the COMPUSTAT items shown in the paper: ((Data199×Data25)+Data130+Data9+Data34)/Data6. The paper does not further define those data items in this description. Formula: ((Data199_t×Data25_t)+Data130_t+Data9_t+Data34_t)/Data6_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

INT_t/A_{t−1}: Internal funds (COMPUSTAT Data18 + Data46 + Data14) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: (Data18_t+Data46_t+Data14_t)/Data6_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
S_t/A_{t−1}: Total sales (COMPUSTAT Data12) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: S_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
ΔS_t/A_{t−1}: Change in total sales from t−1 to t divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: ΔS_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
ΔS_{t−1}/A_{t−1}: Lagged change in total sales, ΔS_{t−1}, divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: ΔS_{t−1}/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
RD_t/A_{t−1}: R&D expense (COMPUSTAT Data46) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: RD_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
1/A_{t−1}: Reciprocal of total assets at t−1, the scaled constant regressor printed in the model. Formula: 1/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MV_t: Natural logarithm of market value, calculated from COMPUSTAT Data199 × Data25. Formula: ln(Data199_t × Data25_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Q_t: Tobin’s Q, calculated using the COMPUSTAT items shown in the paper: ((Data199×Data25)+Data130+Data9+Data34)/Data6. The paper does not further define those data items in this description. Formula: ((Data199_t×Data25_t)+Data130_t+Data9_t+Data34_t)/Data6_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

INT_t/A_{t−1}: Internal funds (COMPUSTAT Data18 + Data46 + Data14) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: (Data18_t+Data46_t+Data14_t)/Data6_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
RD_{t−1}/A_{t−1}: Prior-year R&D expense (COMPUSTAT Data46) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: RD_{t−1}/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SGA_t/A_{t−1}: SG&A expense (COMPUSTAT Data189) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: SGA_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
1/A_{t−1}: Reciprocal of total assets at t−1, the scaled constant regressor printed in the model. Formula: 1/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MV_t: Natural logarithm of market value, calculated from COMPUSTAT Data199 × Data25. Formula: ln(Data199_t × Data25_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Q_t: Tobin’s Q, calculated using the COMPUSTAT items shown in the paper: ((Data199×Data25)+Data130+Data9+Data34)/Data6. The paper does not further define those data items in this description. Formula: ((Data199_t×Data25_t)+Data130_t+Data9_t+Data34_t)/Data6_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

INT_t/A_{t−1}: Internal funds (COMPUSTAT Data18 + Data46 + Data14) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: (Data18_t+Data46_t+Data14_t)/Data6_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
ΔS_t/A_{t−1}: Change in total sales from t−1 to t, divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: ΔS_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ΔS_t/A_{t−1} × DD_t: Interaction of change in total sales from t−1 to t divided by total assets at t−1 and an indicator equal to one when sales revenue decreases between t−1 and t, zero otherwise. Formula: (ΔS_t/A_{t−1}) × DD_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

implementation_issues.description: The paper describes the baseline as cross-sectional regression but does not name the underlying estimator; the year-by-industry support fits likewise do not identify the within-cell estimator.
Equation (1) states 1988–2000, while the general estimation text states 1988–2002 for equations 1–4; the raw envelope conservatively uses the broader period.
The paper uses legacy numeric Compustat Data item codes; no exact item-code-to-current-column crosswalk is supplied, so candidate fields are not treated as verified mappings.
Aggregate RM is described using production model 3 in the appendix/table definition, while the production-cost support fit is Equation 4; the intended residual version is ambiguous.

BENCH_t: Indicator equal to 1 when either net income divided by total assets or the change in net income divided by total assets from t−1 to t is at least 0 and less than 0.01; 0 otherwise. The paper elsewhere describes the denominators as total assets at the beginning of the year. Formula: 1{NI-scaled_t∈[0,0.01) or ΔNI-scaled_t∈[0,0.01)}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Aggregate RM_t: Indicator equal to 1 if the sum of residuals from R&D model 1, SG&A model 2, and the production component multiplied by −1 is in the lowest quintile; 0 otherwise. The source labels the production component “model 3,” although its production-cost equation is model 4. Formula: 1{lowest quintile of residual(Eq.1)+residual(Eq.2)−residual(production-cost model)}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

BENCH_t × Aggregate RM_t: Product of BENCH_t and Aggregate RM_t; each component is the indicator defined in the paper, so the interaction equals one only when both indicators equal one. Formula: BENCH_t × Aggregate RM_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

AdjROA_t: Industry-adjusted ROA: firm-specific ROA minus median ROA in the same year and two-digit SIC industry; ROA is income before extraordinary items divided by lagged total assets. Formula: ROA_t − median(ROA_{same year, two-digit SIC}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
SIZE_t: Natural logarithm of total assets. Formula: ln(total assets_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MTB_t: Market value of equity divided by book value of equity. Formula: market value of equity_t / book value of equity_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RETURN_t: Size-adjusted abnormal return: monthly buy-and-hold raw return minus the monthly buy-and-hold return on a size-matched decile portfolio, compounded over the 12 months of fiscal year t. Formula: compound_{12 months in fiscal year t}(monthly buy-and-hold raw return − monthly buy-and-hold size-decile portfolio return). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

ZSCORE_{t−1}: Modified Altman financial-health measure lagged one period in Equation (6): 3.3×net income/lagged assets + 1.0×sales/lagged assets + 1.4×retained earnings/lagged assets + 1.2×working capital/lagged assets. Formula: ZSCORE_{t−1}; ZSCORE_t=3.3(NI_t/A_{t−1})+1.0(Sales_t/A_{t−1})+1.4(RetainedEarnings_t/A_{t−1})+1.2(WorkingCapital_t/A_{t−1}). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

PROD_t/A_{t−1}: Production costs, defined as cost of goods sold plus change in inventory (COMPUSTAT Data41 + Data303), divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: PROD_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
1/A_{t−1}: Reciprocal of total assets at t−1, the scaled constant regressor printed in the model. Formula: 1/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
MV_t: Natural logarithm of market value, calculated from COMPUSTAT Data199 × Data25. Formula: ln(Data199_t × Data25_t). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

Q_t: Tobin’s Q, calculated using the COMPUSTAT items shown in the paper: ((Data199×Data25)+Data130+Data9+Data34)/Data6. The paper does not further define those data items in this description. Formula: ((Data199_t×Data25_t)+Data130_t+Data9_t+Data34_t)/Data6_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

INT_t/A_{t−1}: Internal funds (COMPUSTAT Data18 + Data46 + Data14) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: (Data18_t+Data46_t+Data14_t)/Data6_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
S_t/A_{t−1}: Total sales (COMPUSTAT Data12) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: S_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
ΔS_t/A_{t−1}: Change in total sales from t−1 to t divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: ΔS_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
ΔS_{t−1}/A_{t−1}: Lagged change in total sales, ΔS_{t−1}, divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: ΔS_{t−1}/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
RD_t/A_{t−1}: R&D expense (COMPUSTAT Data46) divided by total assets at t−1. Formula: RD_t/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.
1/A_{t−1}: Reciprocal of total assets at t−1, the scaled constant regressor printed in the model. Formula: 1/A_{t−1}. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

requirements.description: Annual Compustat accounting inputs for the expected-accrual construction and both matched-sample baseline fits: total assets; sales and receivables; gross PPE; current assets/liabilities and working capital; retained earnings; EBIT; market equity; liabilities/debt; and the next-year operating-income outcome. Also supplies fiscal-year, fiscal-year-end, SIC and native GVKEY fields for the stated annual population and matching rules.

required_coverage.population: U.S. corporations on the paper’s Compustat full-coverage and research files, restricted to eligible 1986–1995 firm-years and the relevant matched sample. The exact correspondence between those 1995 file populations and current local COMP.FUNDA is unverified.
required_coverage.detail: Anchor sample years are fiscal-year labels t=1986–1995. Raw accounting inputs include A_{t−1}, ΔREV/ΔAR from t−1 to t, and the persistence outcome E_{t+1}; the union is 1985–1996. Current format/population descriptors are present as fields but their historical filter semantics and population coverage are not confirmed.

variable_coverage.construction: TA_t/A_{t−1}; total accruals is dated t and divided by total assets at t−1. The paper does not state how TA is computed; do not infer an arithmetic formula.
1/A_{t−1}, the reciprocal of total assets at the prior fiscal-year observation.
(ΔREV_t−ΔAR_t)/A_{t−1}: change in total sales revenue less change in accounts receivable, divided by total assets at t−1. Exact current Compustat revenue/receivable variants are unverified.
PPE_t/A_{t−1}, gross PPE divided by prior-year total assets.

|UA_t|, where UA_t = TA_t/A_{t−1} minus the expected-accrual fit from Equation (3) using coefficients for the two-digit SIC-by-fiscal-year cell. The source does not define TA arithmetic or the exact support-pool population.

OCF_t/A_{t−1} as displayed in Equation (4) and the Table 2 note. The preceding prose describes OCF as cash flows from operations already scaled by lagged assets; the potential double scaling and raw OCF construction remain unresolved.
LA_t = natural log of total assets at t.
LEV_t = total liabilities at t divided by total assets at t.

FC_t is the Altman Z-score: 1.2×working capital/assets + 1.4×retained earnings/assets + 3.3×EBIT/assets + 0.6×market value of equity/book value of total debt + sales/assets. Source field variants and units require verification.

AGE_t is years since the firm’s original exchange listing date as of t. CRSP name-history NAMEDT is only a candidate and is not assumed to equal that listing date; a date-valid Compustat–CRSP link is required.
SHORT_t equals 1 for two- or three-year audit-firm/client tenure as of fiscal year-end, 0 otherwise; the four-to-eight-year group is the comparison group. The year of an auditor change is omitted.
LONG_t equals 1 for audit-firm/client tenure of nine or more years as of fiscal year-end, 0 otherwise; the four-to-eight-year group is the comparison group. Apply the source’s merger-continuity rule.

implementation_issues.description: The source names total accruals TA but does not give its arithmetic. The expected-accrual model and persistence inputs depend on TA, so choosing an accrual calculation would change the target variable.

Equation (4) displays OCF_t/A_{t−1}, while the preceding prose defines OCF as cash flows from operations already scaled by lagged total assets. The raw OCF construction and intended single-versus-double scaling are unresolved.

The support model is estimated in two-digit-SIC-by-fiscal-year cells using “all companies,” but the source does not identify whether that population is all Compustat observations, the screened sample, or the matched sample. Expected UA residuals depend on this cell population.
The cross-sectional modified-Jones supporting fit is specified, but its estimator and cell-level sample sizes are not reported; do not infer OLS from the equation form.

The source gives the nearest-size matching procedure and SIC fallback levels, but does not state tie handling, matching replacement/reuse, or a deterministic fallback rule when multiple matches qualify. Exact matched-sample composition may therefore differ.

Build tenure/Big 6 classifications from historical auditor identities, omit the auditor-change year, and continue tenure through Big 8-to-Big 6 firm mergers as the source directs. The current auditor code meanings and predecessor/successor identity map are not verified.

AGE requires original stock-exchange listing dates linked to each Compustat company. The candidate CRSP name date is not established as a listing date, and the date-valid GVKEY–PERMNO match has not been validated for the sample.

The author used the 1995 annual Compustat files with historical auditor records beginning in 1976. Current local COMP.FUNDA fields do not verify that vintage, population, or the required 1976–1997 history of annual and event fields.
The main Equation (4) estimator is explicitly OLS, but the source does not identify the standard-error/variance correction or clustering dimension used for the reported t-statistics.

evidence.quote: Data considerations : Observations were deleted if (a) financial data were not available on COMPUSTAT; or (b) the auditor could not be determined from the annual COMPUSTAT tapes. <sup>12</sup> 2. design_coverage.reason: The selected column (2) includes firm fixed effects; the article identifies OLS only as a comparison without firm fixed effects and does not identify the estimator used for the selected fixed-effects fit.
Baseline standard errors are clustered by firm and year. Supporting market-model and rolling CSCORE fit standard-error details are not reported in the source.
The selected regression tables/method descriptions report no weighting scheme; the source does not identify weighted fits.
The selected baseline is a firm fixed-effects specification, but the paper does not identify the estimator for that selected fit.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

review_notes: All frozen baseline fits and their weekly-market/CSCORE supporting models are retained. No coordinator local coverage confirmation is supplied; bounded probes establish access and field presence only.
The source specifies weekly CRSP returns, while the local catalog lists daily stock/index products; weekly inputs require an independently documented aggregation convention.
Author-prepared research data and later robustness variables are not used as primary inputs.

design_coverage.reason: The selected column (2) includes firm fixed effects; the article identifies OLS only as a comparison without firm fixed effects and does not identify the estimator used for the selected fixed-effects fit.
Baseline standard errors are clustered by firm and year. Supporting market-model and rolling CSCORE fit standard-error details are not reported in the source.
The selected regression tables/method descriptions report no weighting scheme; the source does not identify weighted fits.
The selected baseline is a firm fixed-effects specification, but the paper does not identify the estimator for that selected fit.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

review_notes: All frozen baseline fits and their weekly-market/CSCORE supporting models are retained. No coordinator local coverage confirmation is supplied; bounded probes establish access and field presence only.
The source specifies weekly CRSP returns, while the local catalog lists daily stock/index products; weekly inputs require an independently documented aggregation convention.
Author-prepared research data and later robustness variables are not used as primary inputs.

design_coverage.reason: The selected column (2) includes firm fixed effects; the article identifies OLS only as a comparison without firm fixed effects and does not identify the estimator used for the selected fixed-effects fit.
Baseline standard errors are clustered by firm and year. Supporting market-model and rolling CSCORE fit standard-error details are not reported in the source.
The selected regression tables/method descriptions report no weighting scheme; the source does not identify weighted fits.
The selected baseline is a firm fixed-effects specification, but the paper does not identify the estimator for that selected fit.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The Ball–Shivakumar sample excludes financial and utility firms, but the source does not define the SIC ranges or classification rule. Historical SICH is present, but exact sample mapping remains unresolved.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

review_notes: All frozen baseline fits and their weekly-market/CSCORE supporting models are retained. No coordinator local coverage confirmation is supplied; bounded probes establish access and field presence only.
The source specifies weekly CRSP returns, while the local catalog lists daily stock/index products; weekly inputs require an independently documented aggregation convention.
Author-prepared research data and later robustness variables are not used as primary inputs.

design_coverage.reason: The selected column (2) includes firm fixed effects; the article identifies OLS only as a comparison without firm fixed effects and does not identify the estimator used for the selected fixed-effects fit.
Baseline standard errors are clustered by firm and year. Supporting market-model and rolling CSCORE fit standard-error details are not reported in the source.
The selected regression tables/method descriptions report no weighting scheme; the source does not identify weighted fits.
The selected baseline is a firm fixed-effects specification, but the paper does not identify the estimator for that selected fit.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.
The selected firm-fixed-effects baseline fit is reported, but the estimator used for that FE fit is not identified; OLS is specified only for comparison without firm fixed effects.

The Ball–Shivakumar sample excludes financial and utility firms, but the source does not define the SIC ranges or classification rule. Historical SICH is present, but exact sample mapping remains unresolved.

The paper’s Table 1 control definitions and the equation text differ on control timing: Table notes label most controls in fiscal year t, while the prose says all controls are measured at the beginning of year t. The temporal audit uses the explicit beginning-of-year statement for those controls and preserves the conflict.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

review_notes: All frozen baseline fits and their weekly-market/CSCORE supporting models are retained. No coordinator local coverage confirmation is supplied; bounded probes establish access and field presence only.
The source specifies weekly CRSP returns, while the local catalog lists daily stock/index products; weekly inputs require an independently documented aggregation convention.
Author-prepared research data and later robustness variables are not used as primary inputs.

implementation_issues.description: The 1964–2007 period is reported for the predictive regressions/major variables, while CRASH and NCSKEW are t+1 outcomes and crash-risk measurement extends 12 months through three months after the fiscal-year-end. The initial CRSP–Compustat draw ends in 2007 and the paper says 2007 is its predictive-regression cutoff. The exact regression-year versus outcome-year convention and resulting final raw dates are unresolved; retain unknown upper endpoints for future-risk inputs.

The exact weekly return aggregation boundaries and fiscal-year mapping are not given. The expanded market model uses market-index leads/lags up to two weeks, and the source requires at least 26 weekly returns per fiscal year. Daily DSF/DSI fields are present, but a week-construction convention remains necessary.

The paper specifies a CRSP–Compustat intersection but not the CCM primary-link/type/overlap selection rule. CCM supplies candidate effective-dated identifiers; exact target-population linking remains unresolved.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.

The CSCORE support fit is described as a five-year rolling panel regression, but the estimator, window orientation/endpoints, per-window population and inclusion rules are not stated. Eq. (5) uses its fitted coefficients to construct the required CSCORE.

The CSCORE construction’s LEV is debt-to-equity, but the debt/equity components are not defined; ROA_(t+1) is named without a numerator/denominator formula. Candidate Compustat fields cannot resolve these definitions.
Use current Compustat/CRSP vintages for the original paper period. Restated accounting fields, identifier histories and return-adjustment conventions may differ from the authors’ source vintage.

review_notes: All frozen baseline fits and their weekly-market/CSCORE supporting models are retained. No coordinator local coverage confirmation is supplied; bounded probes establish access and field presence only.
The source specifies weekly CRSP returns, while the local catalog lists daily stock/index products; weekly inputs require an independently documented aggregation convention.
Author-prepared research data and later robustness variables are not used as primary inputs.

The MB market-to-book ratio is not fully defined by numerator, denominator, adjustments or timing. The source also gives both beginning-year CSCORE characteristics and fiscal-year control definitions; the regression text says controls are at the beginning of t. An exact MB construction and alignment must be resolved.

The CSCORE support fit is described as a five-year rolling panel regression, but the estimator, window orientation/endpoints, per-window population and inclusion rules are not stated. Eq. (5) uses its fitted coefficients to construct the required CSCORE.

The CSCORE construction’s LEV is debt-to-equity, but the debt/equity components are not defined; ROA_(t+1) is named without a numerator/denominator formula. Candidate Compustat fields cannot resolve these definitions.

Source definition: Annual operating cash flows scaled by average total assets. evidence.quote: The sample for our main analysis is based on all CEO firm-years in the ExecuComp database between 1993 and 2010.
evidence.description: Main analysis sample is CEO firm-years in ExecuComp for 1993–2010.

evidence.quote: This database covers S&P 1500 index companies and companies that were once part of the S&P 1500 index.
evidence.description: ExecuComp population description.

evidence.quote: We then delete observations with missing COMPUSTAT accounting data and missing Center for Research in Security Prices stock price, return, and trading volume data in estimating our crash risk measures and control variables.
evidence.description: Sample drops observations missing Compustat/CRSP data and firms with fiscal-year-end price below $1.

evidence.quote: we require that the CEOs hold stock options at least twice during our sample period that are more than 100 percent in the money.
evidence.description: Option-based CEO measure requires two observations with options more than 100% in the money and becomes one from first qualifying year.

evidence.quote: we compute the realizable value per option as the total realizable value of the exercisable options divided by the total number of exercisable options.
evidence.description: Option moneyness uses realizable value per exercisable option and fiscal-year-end share price.

evidence.quote: the second overconfidence measure, OC_SZ, takes the value of one if the firm meets at least three of the following five criteria and zero otherwise
evidence.description: OC_SZ threshold and five-part decision rule.

evidence.quote: Excess investment is in the top quartile of firms within industry-years, where excess investment is the residual from a regression of total asset growth on sales growth
evidence.description: Excess investment requires growth regression residuals and industry-year quartile ranking.

evidence.quote: the industry is defined as a three-digit Standard Industrial Classification code.
evidence.description: Three-digit SIC industry definition used for OC_SZ criteria.

evidence.quote: firm has an OC_SZ score equal to one
evidence.description: OC_MSZ follows the first year the CEO’s firm has an OC_SZ score of one.

evidence.quote: we first estimate the firm-specific weekly returns for each firm and year because we are interested in firm-specific return crashes.
evidence.description: Firm-specific weekly returns are estimated separately for each firm and year.

evidence.quote: Specifically, the firm-specific weekly return, denoted W, is defined as the natural log of one plus the residual return from the expanded index model regression
evidence.description: Weekly firm-specific return is log one plus the residual from expanded market/industry index model.

evidence.quote: To estimate equation (1), we require that at least 26 weekly return observations be available for each firm and year.
evidence.description: Each firm-year index fit needs at least 26 weekly observations.

evidence.quote: fall more than 3.2 standard deviations below the mean firm-specific weekly returns over the entire fiscal year
evidence.description: Crash week threshold uses 3.2 within-year standard deviations below the firm-year mean.

evidence.quote: we calculate NCSKEW for a given firm in a fiscal year by taking the negative of the third moment of firm-specific weekly returns for each sample year and dividing it by the standard deviation of firm-specific weekly returns raised to the third power
evidence.description: NCSKEW is negative third moment divided by weekly-return standard deviation cubed.

evidence.quote: we separate all the weeks with firm-specific weekly returns below the annual mean
evidence.description: DUVOL splits firm-year weekly firm-specific returns into below-mean and above-mean weeks.

evidence.quote: we use logit regression when CRASH is the dependent variable and ordinary least squares (OLS) when either NCSKEW or DUVOL is the dependent variable
evidence.description: Baseline uses logit for CRASH and OLS for NCSKEW/DUVOL.

evidence.quote: All the independent variables are measured in year t - 1.
evidence.description: All main regression independent variables are lagged one year.

evidence.quote: we also include their financial reporting opacity measure (OPAQUE) and its squared term as additional control variables
evidence.description: Both OPAQUE and its square are baseline controls.

evidence.quote: In all regressions, we also include industry and fiscal year indicators to control for industry and time fixed effects.
evidence.description: Industry and fiscal-year indicators are included in all main regressions.

evidence.quote: standard errors corrected for firm and year double clustering
evidence.description: Reported Table 3 standard errors are double clustered by firm and year.

evidence.quote: The average monthly share turnover over the current fiscal year period minus the average monthly share turnover over the previous fiscal year period
evidence.description: DTURNOVER compares current-year and previous-year average monthly turnover.

evidence.quote: monthly share turnover is calculated as the monthly trading volume divided by the total number of shares outstanding during the month
evidence.description: Monthly turnover is volume divided by monthly shares outstanding.

evidence.quote: SIZE The log of the market value of equity MB The market value of equity divided by the book value of equity LEV The total long-term debt divided by total assets ROA The income before extraordinary items divided by lagged total assets
evidence.description: Appendix control definitions for SIZE, MB, LEV and ROA.

evidence.quote: ONEPCT_OPT/(ONEPCT_OPT + SALARY + BONUS)
evidence.description: Option incentive ratio numerator divided by numerator plus salary and bonus.

evidence.quote: INCENTIVE_STK The incentive ratio for executive stock holdings, defined similarly to INCENTIVE_OPT
evidence.description: Stock incentive ratio is said to be defined similarly to the option ratio; no formula is given.

evidence.quote: The prior three years’ moving sum of the absolute value of discretionary accruals
evidence.description: OPAQUE is a prior three-year moving sum of absolute discretionary accruals.

variable_coverage.construction: Normal accruals / total assets: Normal accruals divided by lagged total assets, estimated cross-sectionally for each industry-year. Formula: NormalAccruals_t / Assets_{t−1}. Raw inputs are in R_ANN; preserve unresolved source definitions and do not tune to reported coefficients.
1 / total assets: Reciprocal of lagged total assets. Formula: 1 / Assets_{t−1}. Raw inputs are in R_ANN; preserve unresolved source definitions and do not tune to reported coefficients.

ΔRevenue − ΔReceivables: Change in revenue less change in receivables, scaled by lagged total assets. Formula: (ΔRevenue_t − ΔReceivables_t) / Assets_{t−1}. Raw inputs are in R_ANN; preserve unresolved source definitions and do not tune to reported coefficients.

Property, plant, and equipment: Property, plant, and equipment divided by lagged total assets. Formula: PPE_t / Assets_{t−1}. Raw inputs are in R_ANN; preserve unresolved source definitions and do not tune to reported coefficients.

ΔCash from operations: Change in cash from operations divided by lagged total assets. Formula: ΔCFO_t / Assets_{t−1}. Raw inputs are in R_ANN; preserve unresolved source definitions and do not tune to reported coefficients.

ROA: Return on assets included as a control in the normal-accrual fit per endnote 6; the printed equation does not show its placement or coefficient. variable_coverage.construction: Source definition: Indicator equal to one for a Big 6 audited firm and zero otherwise; COMPUSTAT auditor codes 1–8 are classified as Big 6. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Absolute value of short-term working-capital accruals, scaled by sales. Working-capital accruals are the first two terms of the total-accruals identity. Formula: |(ΔCA−ΔCash)−(ΔCL−ΔSTD−ΔTP)|/Sales. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Absolute value of depreciation and amortization, scaled by sales. Formula: |Dep|/Sales. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Firm size measured by the natural logarithm of total sales, in millions of dollars. Formula: ln(total sales in millions of dollars).. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Leverage measured by debt-to-total-assets ratio. Formula: total debt/total assets. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals. Source definition: Price-to-earnings ratio at fiscal year-end. Formula: fiscal-year-end price-to-earnings ratio. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals. Source definition: Indicator equal to one when shares outstanding increase by more than 10 percent during the current fiscal year, and zero otherwise. Formula: 1 if shares outstanding increase >10%; 0 otherwise. Inputs/route requirements: r_share_count. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Indicator equal to one when net income divided by lagged assets is negative and the absolute change in net income divided by lagged assets exceeds 10 percent; zero otherwise. Formula: 1 if NI/A_{t−1}<0 and |ΔNI/A_{t−1}|>0.10; 0 otherwise. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Total accruals for firm j in year t, scaled by lagged total assets. Total accruals equal the change in noncash current assets less the change in operating current liabilities and depreciation and amortization. Formula: [(ΔCA−ΔCash)−(ΔCL−ΔSTD−ΔTP)−Dep]/A_{j,t−1}. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_sic_codes. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: The reciprocal of lagged total assets, included as the scaled constant term. Formula: 1/A_{j,t−1}. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_sic_codes. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Change in sales revenues less change in accounts receivable, scaled by lagged total assets. Formula: (ΔREV_{jt}−ΔAR_{jt})/A_{j,t−1}. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_sic_codes. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Property, plant, and equipment scaled by lagged total assets. Formula: PPE_{jt}/A_{j,t−1}. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_sic_codes. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Change in cash flow from operations scaled by lagged total assets. Formula: ΔCFO_{jt}/A_{j,t−1}. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_sic_codes. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Discretionary accruals, defined as the residual from equation (2), equal to actual total accruals less fitted nondiscretionary accruals. Source definition: One-period lagged discretionary accruals, where DAC is the residual from equation (2). Formula: DAC_{j,t−1}. Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_sic_codes. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

Source definition: Inverse Mills ratio generated from the auditor-choice probit equation (3) and included to control for potential self-selection. The equation (4) lead-in and Table 5 note instead cite auditor-choice model (4), although equation (4) is the accrual-choice model. Formula: Inverse Mills ratio from Eq. (3). Inputs/route requirements: r_comp_fundamentals, r_auditor_history. Current source-field mapping, exact identifier linkage, or full period/population coverage remains as stated on those requirements; do not tune to reported coefficients.

design_coverage.reason: Annual fits are separate year-by-year cross-sections; the selected baseline equation does not identify fixed-effect terms. The source does not explicitly say fixed effects are absent.
No cluster variable is reported. Inference uses annual coefficient distributions/Fama–MacBeth time-series t-values; the DAC support equation reports no separate clustered error correction.
No regression weights are reported. The minimum-firm threshold and year-by-industry estimation are grouping rules, not observation weights.

Generate annual inverse Mills ratios from Eq. (3), then estimate the accrual-choice equation cross-sectionally in each year 1984–1998 for the full, Cpoor or Cgood group; report 15-year average coefficients and time-series t-values. Per-year N is not reported.

implementation_issues.description: The source population uses 1999 Compustat PC-Plus Active and Research files. Current WRDS Compustat column presence does not establish legacy item mapping, PC-Plus value equivalence, 1982–1998 coverage, or the original firm/year restrictions.

Equation (2) is fit separately for each year and two-digit SIC cell with at least 20 firms, but cell-specific sample sizes, complete group membership and all legacy Compustat item mappings are not provided by the current probe.

NewAud and OldAud require a continuous historical client-auditor sequence. OldAud also needs a subsequent auditor change; the source data span ends in 1998 while the final 1998 row may require a 1999 transition. Historical code #149 meaning and transition coverage remain unresolved.

CFO scaling differs across source passages: Table 5 and the frozen variable definition show lagged total assets, while equation (4) prose says total assets without specifying a lag. Assessment/audit retain the Table 5 lagged-assets scale and document the conflict.

Lambda is defined in the model prose as the inverse Mills ratio from the auditor-choice probit Eq. (3), but the accrual-choice lead-in/Table 5 note also refers to model (4), which is the second-stage accrual model. Preserve the source-supported Eq. (3) construction and flag the contradictory reference.

Annual coefficients and t-statistics use 15 yearly cross-sections. Exact second-stage estimator and any additional serial-correlation adjustment beyond the stated time-series/Fama–MacBeth variation should follow the original table/text; per-year N is not reported.

review_notes: No local historical/population coverage confirmations were supplied. Bounded Compustat probes verify current fields only; they do not verify 1999 PC-Plus item meanings or full source-period sample coverage.

Source formula: 1{FE ≥ 0 and ADJFE < 0}; FE = (actual EPS − median forecast) / beginning-of-year stock price; ADJFE = NDEPS − median forecast; NDEPS = actual EPS − DA per share. Source definition: Indicator equal to one when forecast error (actual EPS minus the median consensus forecast, divided by beginning-of-fiscal-year stock price) is nonnegative while adjusted forecast error is negative. The paper specifies the median consensus forecast closest to the earnings announcement and I/B/E/S actual EPS from the Historical Summary tape for forecast-error calculations. ADJFE is NDEPS minus the median forecast; NDEPS equals actual EPS minus discretionary accruals per share (equivalently, cash flow from operations plus nondiscretionary accruals per share). Thus positive discretionary accruals allow the firm to cross the forecast threshold. Zero otherwise. Raw component fields: COMP.FUNDA: gvkey, datadate, fyear, fyr, sich, au, at, act, che, lct, dlc, dltt, dp, oiadp, oancf, ppent, sale, ib, ni, lt, seq, ceq, prcc_f; IBES.STATSUM_EPSUS: TICKER, CUSIP, STATPERS, MEASURE, FISCALP, FPI, NUMEST, MEDEST, MEANEST, STDEV, FPEDATS, ACTUAL, ANNDATS_ACT, ACTDATS_ACT, USFIRM; IBES.ACT_EPSUS: TICKER, CUSIP, PENDS, ANNDATS, VALUE, MEASURE, PDICITY, USFIRM; CRSP.MSF: PERMNO, PERMCO, DATE, PRC, SHROUT, RET, CUSIP; CRSP.CCMXPF_LINKTABLE: gvkey, lpermno, linkdt, linkenddt, linkprim, linktype, liid; WRDSAPPS.IBCRSPHIST: TICKER, PERMNO, sdate, edate, ncusip, SCORE Preserve raw missing values and denominators; do not impute missing source components or force an observed classification.

implementation_issues.description: The article’s discretionary-accrual residual is asset-scaled, but its conversion to the per-share DA subtracted from actual EPS is not specified.
HORIZON is measured from earnings announcement to forecast month in the main-model definition but from fiscal year-end in the Table 2 note; the source does not reconcile them.
TENURE treats auditor mergers as continuation and BIGN changes across Big 8/6/5/4 eras; complete historical merger and auditor-code crosswalk is not supplied.
Industry fixed-effect count differs between the text (52 two-digit SIC industries) and Table 4 note (53 represented codes); the two-way cluster dimensions are also unnamed.
Forecast-data winsorization is reported for forecast-error calculations, but the article does not say whether it applies to the Table 4 MBE classification.
The estimator for the supporting annual two-digit-SIC/year Jones fits is not named; this is an implementation choice, not a missing raw-data source.

review_notes: For SHORT, Equation (3) specifies tenure >1 and <4, while the appendix says three years or less; first-year engagements are excluded, so the definitions agree within the retained sample.

The paper does not report the conversion from the asset-scaled Jones residual DA to the per-share discretionary accrual used in NDEPS.
Footnote 16 specifies forecast-data winsorization for forecast-error calculations; its application to Table 4 MBE is not clear, so it is not recorded as a setting applied to this equation.
Coverage remains undetermined without coordinator-supplied historical/population confirmations. Exact successful local field probes are reused; they establish columns only.
Table 4 retains both frozen model/result-set IDs and the shared Jones construction.

variable_coverage.construction: Earnings: Quarterly net income before extraordinary items deflated by market value of equity at the end of the previous quarter. Source formula: Quarterly net income before extraordinary items / prior-quarter-end market value of equity.. Required resource bundles R-COMPQ R-CRSP-MONTH R-COMP-CRSP-LINK R-INDUSTRY-PEERS; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

Return: Buy-and-hold raw stock returns during quarter t. Source formula: Quarterly buy-and-hold raw stock return.. Required resource bundles R-COMPQ R-CRSP-MONTH R-COMP-CRSP-LINK R-INDUSTRY-PEERS; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

Firm stock return: Daily stock return for an acquisition participant (acquirer or target) used to estimate market-model parameters for announcement CARs. Source formula: not reported as a closed formula in the paper. Required resource bundles R-CRSP-DAILY R-CRSP-INDEX R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

CRSP value-weighted return: CRSP value-weighted market return used as the market-model return input. Source formula: not reported as a closed formula in the paper. Required resource bundles R-CRSP-DAILY R-CRSP-INDEX R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

Daily stock return: Target firm daily stock return. Source formula: not reported as a closed formula in the paper. Required resource bundles R-CRSP-DAILY R-CRSP-INDEX R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

Daily market return: Daily market return used as the regressor in the target return-synchronicity regression. Source formula: not reported as a closed formula in the paper. Required resource bundles R-CRSP-DAILY R-CRSP-INDEX R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

ACQ_CAR: Acquirer three-day cumulative abnormal return centered on announcement days −1 to +1. Abnormal returns use the market model with CRSP value-weighted returns; parameters are estimated over event days −205 to −6. Source formula: Three-day cumulative abnormal return over event days [−1,+1] using market-model returns; estimation window [−205,−6].. Required resource bundles R-CRSP-DAILY R-CRSP-INDEX R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

TRG_COMPRNK: Target firm financial statement comparability for t−1. Firm-pair comparability is the negative of the average absolute difference between predicted earnings from the two firm-specific accounting systems applied to the same target-firm returns; the target score averages this across all other firms in the same two-digit SIC industry. TRG_COMP is ranked into deciles 0–9 and divided by nine to form TRG_COMPRNK on [0,1]. Source formula: TRG_COMPRNK_{i,t−1} = DecileRank_{0..9}(TRG_COMP_{i,t−1}) / 9; TRG_COMP_{i,t−1} = mean_{j in same SIC2, j≠i}[-mean_t |E(Earnings^i_i,t) − E(Earnings^i_j,t)|].. Required resource bundles R-COMPQ R-CRSP-MONTH R-COMP-CRSP-LINK R-INDUSTRY-PEERS; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

ACQ_SIZE: Acquirer size, measured as the natural logarithm of acquirer market value at the end of the quarter before the announcement. Source formula: ln(acquirer market value at prior-quarter end).. Required resource bundles R-CRSP-MONTH R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

ACQ_LEV: Acquirer pre-acquisition leverage: long-term plus short-term debt divided by total assets at fiscal year-end before the acquisition announcement. Source formula: (long-term debt + short-term debt) / total assets, fiscal year-end before announcement.. Required resource bundles R-COMPANNUAL R-CRSP-MONTH R-COMP-CRSP-LINK R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

ACQ_TOBIN_DUM: Indicator for acquirer Tobin’s Q relative to the sample median, with conflicting coding: the research-design text says 1 for Q below the median; the Appendix says 1 for Q above the median. Acquirer characteristics are measured at fiscal year-end before the announcement unless specified otherwise. Source formula: not reported as a closed formula in the paper. Required resource bundles R-COMPANNUAL R-CRSP-MONTH R-COMP-CRSP-LINK R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

ACQ_ROA: Acquirer ROA for the year ended before the announcement year, calculated as operating income before depreciation divided by average total assets. Source formula: Operating income before depreciation / average total assets.. Required resource bundles R-COMPANNUAL R-CRSP-MONTH R-COMP-CRSP-LINK R-SDC-CRSP-LINK; candidate live fields and unresolved semantic/date mapping are recorded on those requirements.

ACQ_FCF: Acquirer free cash flow: operating income before depreciation less interest expense, tax expense and dividends, scaled by total assets; acquirer characteristics are measured at the fiscal year-end before announcement unless otherwise specified. Source formula: (operating income before depreciation − interest expense − tax expense − dividends) / total assets.. variable_coverage.construction: RET_SUPP_t: The supplier’s two-day market-adjusted stock return on the day of and day following its customer’s QEA, measured as the supplier’s raw return minus the value-weighted market return on each day. The paper does not state whether the two daily adjusted returns are summed, compounded, or otherwise aggregated. The source does not specify an exact formula. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RET_CUST_t: Two-day market-adjusted stock return of the customer on the day of and the day following its own QEA; measured using the customer’s raw return minus the value-weighted market return on each day. The source does not specify an exact formula. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

CORR_t: Pearson correlation in the supplier’s and customer’s daily market-adjusted returns over the year immediately preceding the customer’s QEA; this is normal, non-event-period return correlation. Formula: PearsonCorr(daily market-adjusted returns_supplier, daily market-adjusted returns_customer; preceding year). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

PCT_SALES_t: Percentage of the supplier’s annual sales made to the customer in the fiscal year before the customer’s QEA. Formula: supplier annual sales to customer / supplier total annual sales (percentage). Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RET_CUST_t × CORR_t: Product of (The customer’s two-day market-adjusted stock return on the day of and day following its QEA, measured as daily raw return minus the value-weighted market return; the paper does not state how the two daily adjusted returns are aggregated.) and (The Pearson correlation between supplier and customer daily market-adjusted returns over the year immediately before the customer’s QEA; this is normal, non-event-period return correlation.). Formula: RET_CUST_t × CORR_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RET_CUST_t × PCT_SALES_t: Product of (The customer’s two-day market-adjusted stock return on the day of and day following its QEA, measured as daily raw return minus the value-weighted market return; the paper does not state how the two daily adjusted returns are aggregated.) and (The percentage of the supplier’s annual sales made to the customer in the fiscal year preceding that customer’s QEA; the source does not state whether the stored measure is a fraction or is multiplied by 100.). Formula: RET_CUST_t × PCT_SALES_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

CORR_t × PCT_SALES_t: Product of (The Pearson correlation between supplier and customer daily market-adjusted returns over the year immediately before the customer’s QEA; this is normal, non-event-period return correlation.) and (The percentage of the supplier’s annual sales made to the customer in the fiscal year preceding that customer’s QEA; the source does not state whether the stored measure is a fraction or is multiplied by 100.). Formula: CORR_t × PCT_SALES_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

RET_CUST_t × CORR_t × PCT_SALES_t: Product of (The customer’s two-day market-adjusted stock return on the day of and day following its QEA, measured as daily raw return minus the value-weighted market return; the paper does not state how the two daily adjusted returns are aggregated.), (The Pearson correlation between supplier and customer daily market-adjusted returns over the year immediately before the customer’s QEA; this is normal, non-event-period return correlation.), and (The percentage of the supplier’s annual sales made to the customer in the fiscal year preceding that customer’s QEA; the source does not state whether the stored measure is a fraction or is multiplied by 100.). Formula: RET_CUST_t × CORR_t × PCT_SALES_t. Raw inputs and limitations are recorded in the linked requirements.

implementation_issues.description: The paper does not state whether the two daily market-adjusted returns are summed, compounded, or otherwise aggregated into the two-day RET_SUPP/RET_CUST measure.
The baseline is described as cross-sectional regression without naming the estimator.
Industry fixed-effect classification and whether it is supplier or customer industry are not identified; firm-clustered standard errors do not say which pair member is clustered.

PCT_SALES is described as a percentage of annual supplier sales to a customer but the data scaling and precise prior fiscal-year alignment are not specified; RATIO log base and annual fiscal-year alignment are also unspecified.

The paper manually links customer names to Compustat and relies on exact historical QEA dates and intraday timing; the local segment link and quarterly report-date fields do not establish those matches/timestamps.
Table 7 Model 6 has fewer observations than Model 3, but no additional sample-reduction rule is reported.

Cases followed beyond2006 and market-revelation/resolution dates remain a separate unresolved requirement.

variable_coverage.construction: Observed transaction-price change Δp_t; requires transaction prices p_t and the immediately preceding transaction price. The source does not bound the calendar time to that previous trade.
Signed order flow q_t = D_t × shares traded, with D=+1 for buys and −1 for sells classified using Lee–Ready. Trade size and quote-assisted order sign are required.
Order-sign change D_t−D_(t−1), using Lee–Ready signs; its previous-transaction input has no source-bounded calendar interval.

GHLAMBDA is the quarterly average of retained stock-month λ estimates after the 10% significance screen; retained λ is multiplied by 1,000 for presentation. The equation (2) estimator/inference rule is not specified.

POST=1 for quarters 1–8 after the earliest qualifying revelation (amendment, following filing reflecting agreed changes, or public release of letters); POST=0 for the eight quarters before the first letter; the intervening case period is omitted.
Quarterly average of daily share turnover; a candidate construction is daily CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding, but the denominator/unit convention is not stated.
Standard deviation of daily stock returns within the quarter; CRSP RET/RETX and return adjustment convention are not specified by the paper.
Natural log of market value of equity at quarter end; candidate CRSP construction is abs(PRC)×SHROUT, but the scale/unit inside the log is not stated.
Quarter-end market value of equity divided by quarter-end book equity. CRSP market value and Compustat quarterly equity are candidate inputs; the exact book-equity items/adjustments are unspecified.

Proportion of firm shares held by institutions at quarter end; requires manager holdings, a shares-outstanding denominator and CUSIP/PERMNO matching. Aggregation/denominator/product details are not given.
Number of analysts making earnings forecasts during the quarter from I/B/E/S records; exact fiscal-period and analyst deduplication/count window are unspecified.

Current-quarter EPS used as the regression outcome over the past ten years.
Same-fiscal-quarter prior-year EPS predictor (t−4 quarters) in the ten-year persistence regression; adds one year of raw EPS history before the fit window.
CAR, the three-day (-1,+1) cumulative abnormal return around each quarterly earnings announcement; source says CRSP firm return minus CRSP value-weighted market return.

SUE, unexpected earnings based on the median analyst forecasts issued within 90 days before the quarterly earnings announcement and deflated by quarter-end share price; exact numerator, forecast selection and measure are not specified.
POST indicator for the eight quarters after the earliest qualifying revelation and zero for the eight quarters before the first comment letter, omitting the intervening case period.
POST × SUE interaction, constructed from the case-level POST indicator and SUE.
NONLINEAR = SUE × |SUE|.
PERSIST, the slope from the supporting regression of current-quarter EPS on same-quarter prior-year EPS over the past ten years; fit unit/estimator/intercept are unspecified.
PREDICT, square root of the error variance from the supporting EPS persistence regression.
BETA, the supporting market-model regression coefficient from the year before the earnings announcement; return series/proxy/frequency/fit unit are unspecified.
Quarter-end market value of equity divided by quarter-end book value of equity; exact Compustat equity construction is unspecified.
Natural log of market value of equity; the ERC-specific valuation date and scale are not specified.
Indicator for negative quarterly earnings. The exact earnings item, adjustment and zero/missing coding are unspecified.
Indicator for an earnings announcement for the fourth quarter; fiscal versus calendar quarter coding is unspecified.
Indicator equal to one when the earnings surprise is zero or positive; depends on the unresolved SUE construction.
Interaction SUE × PERSIST. The second interaction factor is PERSIST; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × PREDICT. The second interaction factor is PREDICT; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × BETA. The second interaction factor is BETA; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × MTB. The second interaction factor is MTB; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × SIZE. The second interaction factor is SIZE; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × LOSS. The second interaction factor is LOSS; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × Q4. The second interaction factor is Q4; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.
Interaction SUE × MEETBEAT. The second interaction factor is MEETBEAT; each source component retains its own temporal window in the audit.

implementation_issues.description: The Table 4 column (2) regression estimator is not named, and intercept/weighting treatment is not reported for this full model. The paper reports firm/year FE and firm-clustered SEs but does not identify the firm key used for those dimensions.

SUE is not expressed as an exact numerator formula; the forecast product/adjustment, 90-day analyst-record selection, revision handling, analyst deduplication and forecast vintage are not specified. Quarter-end share-price adjustment and actual EPS alignment also remain open.

The ten-year EPS persistence regression does not specify fitting unit, estimator, intercept, missing-quarter rule or exact actual-EPS series. Its prior-year same-quarter predictor requires an additional 12 months of raw history beyond the ten-year fit window.

BETA’s one-year market model does not identify dependent returns, market return proxy, return frequency, fit unit, intercept or estimator. r_beta_spec keeps the unspecified raw market-model inputs explicit.
The ERC SIZE definition omits its valuation date and unit; quarter end is stated for the separate GHLAMBDA SIZE control only and cannot be carried over silently.
LOSS’s earnings item/zero coding and Q4’s fiscal-versus-calendar quarter rule are not identified; MEETBEAT follows the unresolved SUE construction.

The post window requires case-specific resolution and the first of amendment, a later filing reflecting agreed changes, or public release of letters. Exact case dates and content decisions are not supplied.
Reconstruct the historical CIK/GVKEY/PERMNO/I/B/E/S ticker links and resolve effective dates and duplicate matches; the firm key used for fixed effects and clustered errors is unstated.

evidence.description: Sample collection period and included filing forms.

evidence.description: Final comment-letter sample counts.

evidence.description: The source unit is a filing review episode, not a single letter.
