evidence.quote: We define the pre period as the eight quarters prior to the first comment letter issued by the SEC
evidence.description: Pre-analysis event window.

evidence.quote: Therefore, our post period begins with the first quarter after the earliest of these three events
evidence.description: Post-window start is defined by the first qualifying disclosure/revelation event; actual case dates are not reported.

evidence.quote: Such revelations occur in one of three ways: an amended filing resulting from the comment letter
evidence.description: The source identifies amendments, a subsequent annual/quarterly filing reflecting agreed changes, or public release of the letters as revelation events.

evidence.quote: To capture any comment letter effect on the information environment, we apply the following regression model
evidence.description: Equation (1) reports a firm/year fixed-effects regression, but does not name the estimator/intercept/weighting procedure.

evidence.quote: In all our regression analyses, we cluster standard errors by firm
evidence.description: Firm-level clustering is stated, but the source does not identify the firm key.

evidence.quote: We estimate equation (2) for each stock-month using intraday transaction data.
evidence.description: GHLAMBDA supporting fit uses intraday transaction data at the stock-month level.

evidence.quote: q is signed order flow that equals D multiplied by the number of shares traded
evidence.description: Equation (2) signed order-flow construction.

evidence.quote: D is the sign of the order (equal to 1 for buy orders and −1 for sell orders) classified based on the Lee and Ready (1991) algorithm
evidence.description: Order-sign classification and direction.

evidence.quote: CAR is the three-day cumulative abnormal return surrounding each firm’s quarterly earnings announcement
evidence.description: ERC outcome is a short-window return around earnings announcements.

evidence.quote: abnormal returns are CRSP firm-specific returns less CRSP value-weighted market returns
evidence.description: CRSP firm returns and CRSP value-weighted market returns define abnormal returns.

evidence.quote: Analyst forecasts and actual earnings are taken from I/B/E/S.
evidence.description: I/B/E/S source for analyst forecasts and actual earnings.

evidence.quote: We add SUE as an independent variable and interact POST and SUE to capture the change in the ERC following comment letter resolution
evidence.description: ERC post-period interaction construction.

evidence.quote: VOLUME is the average daily share turnover during the quarter
evidence.description: GHLAMBDA volume control timing and definition.

evidence.quote: VOLATILITY is the standard deviation of the daily stock return during the quarter
evidence.description: GHLAMBDA volatility control timing and definition.

evidence.quote: INSTOWN is the proportion of the firm’s shares held by institutions at the end of the quarter
evidence.description: Institutional ownership timing and high-level definition.

evidence.quote: FOLLOWING is the number of analysts making earnings forecasts during the quarter
evidence.description: Analyst-following timing and high-level definition.

evidence.quote: SIZE is the natural logarithm of the market value of equity at the end of the quarter
evidence.description: GHLAMBDA size measure is quarter-end.

evidence.quote: MTB is the ratio of market value of equity to the book value of equity at the end of the quarter
evidence.description: GHLAMBDA market-to-book measure is quarter-end.

evidence.quote: NONLINEAR is defined as SUE ×| SUE |
evidence.description: Nonlinear earnings-surprise control construction.

evidence.quote: PERSIST is the slope coefficient from a regression of current quarter earnings per share
evidence.description: Persistence score is an estimated slope; the source also identifies same-quarter prior-year EPS and a past-ten-year window.

variable_coverage.construction: INEW_t = ITOTAL_t − IMAINTENANCE_t; ITOTAL = CAPX + acquisitions + R&D − SalePPE; maintenance = depreciation and amortization. Scale the annual measure by average total assets; exact current-field mapping and average-asset timing remain uncertain.

Prior-year V/P = VAIP divided by market equity (Compustat price item 25 × shares item 199); VAIP uses common equity, annual dividends, and operating income after depreciation with r=0.12 and persistence 0.62. The source PDF’s multiplication was visually verified; exact local vintage/field mapping is unresolved.
Prior-year leverage uses book short- and long-term debt divided by book total debt plus book equity. Current Compustat debt/equity fields are candidates; item mapping is unverified.

Prior-year change in firm market value. The source does not define exact endpoints, fiscal/calendar alignment, or whether dividends/corporate-action adjustments enter.
Lagged INEW is its own prior-year value, constructed from ITOTAL−IMAINTENANCE and scaled by average assets; because it is t−1, the average-asset denominator reaches t−2.

Residual from Table 2 Model IV, observed INEW_t less its fitted value; INEW uses current-year investment components and average total assets. The support model’s underlying raw inputs are separately mapped in the supporting model entries.
FCF<0_t equals FCF_t when FCF_t<0 and zero otherwise; FCF_t = CFO_t−D&A_t+R&D_t−fitted INEW_t, scaled by average total assets.
FCF>0_t equals FCF_t when FCF_t>0 and zero otherwise; FCF_t = CFO_t−D&A_t+R&D_t−fitted INEW_t, scaled by average total assets.

evidence.quote: We obtain financial data from the 1997 Compustat Annual Industrial and Annual Research files for the period 1972–1997.
evidence.description: Original Compustat vintage and source period.

evidence.quote: For each year t from 1972 to 1992, we retain all observations with non-missing data for the following:
evidence.description: Sample anchor and nonmissing screen.

evidence.quote: CapExt is capital expenditures, Compustat data #128,
evidence.description: Capital expenditure item.

evidence.quote: P and BVE are measured at the end of fiscal year t - 1 because they are used as deflators.
evidence.description: Deflator timing.

evidence.quote: Per share values of P, BVE, and future earnings, Et +1 to Et +5, are adjusted for stock splits and stock dividends using the cumulative adjustment factor, Compustat data 27
evidence.description: Per-share adjustment factor.

evidence.quote: Since earnings variability is calculated using data for five years following year t
evidence.description: Five-year forward outcome window.

evidence.quote: In cases where EPS data are absent in any of the years from t + 1 through t + 5, SD(Et+1,t+5) is set equal to the mean SD(Et+1,t+5) of the firms in the same Altman Z-Score decile portfolio
evidence.description: Missing-future outcome imputation.

evidence.quote: We rank the firms according to their Z -scores and assign each observation a decile rank.
evidence.description: Year-t Z-score deciles.

evidence.quote: We estimate R&D assets in year t as the sum of R&D expenditures for the past years, each depreciated at the rate of 20% per year (i.e., assuming straight line depreciation over five years).
evidence.description: Five-year R&D capitalization formula.

evidence.quote: Estimation of capitalized R&D requires five years of R&D expenditures, which reduces the sample size for this analysis from 42,776 to 29,408.
evidence.description: Table 4 history/sample restriction.

evidence.quote: The earliest year is set at 1972 because prior to that year
evidence.description: Source availability statement relevant to pre-1972 history.

evidence.quote: Leveraget is the ratio of long-term debt to the market value of equity plus long-term debt
evidence.description: Equation (5) leverage definition.

evidence.quote: Leveraget is the sum of long-term debt, data #9, and debt in current liabilities, data #34
evidence.description: Data-section leverage definition.

evidence.quote: Leveraget is the book value of debt divided by debt plus the market value of equity both at the end of fiscal year t.
evidence.description: Table 3 leverage note.

evidence.quote: Et is primary earnings per share before extraordinary items and discontinued operations, data #58,
evidence.description: EPS definition/item.

evidence.quote: MVt is the market value of equity, measured as the natural logarithm of the product of the fiscal-year closing price and common shares outstanding [log(data #199*data #54)]
evidence.description: Market capitalization inputs.

evidence.quote: The sample size is 42,776 in Panel A and 40,569 in panel B.
evidence.description: Table 3 baseline fit samples.

evidence.quote: bottom and top one percentiles to the highest values of the 1st and 99th percentiles.
evidence.description: General-section winsorization rule.

evidence.quote: We winsorize all variables by setting the values in the 1st and 100th percentiles to the minimum and maximum values in the 2nd and 99th percentiles.
evidence.description: Table 3 selected-fit winsorization.

evidence.quote: Observations with deflated EPS values of less than −1 or greater than 1 are winsorized at −1 and +1.
evidence.description: Table 3 EPS clipping.

evidence.quote: Reported t-tests are adjusted for autocorrelation using the Newey-West correction with 5 lags.
evidence.description: Table 3 coefficient-series inference.

evidence.quote: Variables are winsorized by setting the values in the 1st and 100th percentiles to the minimum and maximum values in the 2nd and 99th percentiles.
evidence.description: Table 4 selected-fit winsorization.

evidence.quote: Reported t-tests are adjusted for autocorrelation using the Newey-West correction with 5 lags.
evidence.description: Table 4 coefficient-series inference.

evidence.quote: Model: SD(Et+1,t+5) = α + β1tR&Dt + β2tCapExt + β3tAdvExt + β4tMVt + β5tLeveraget + errort+1,t+5
evidence.description: Table 3 baseline equation.

evidence.quote: The OJ model yields the following pricing equation
evidence.description: Physical page 5 gives the Ohlson–Juettner pricing relation and its cost-of-equity expression. The risk premium is a deterministic inferred outcome rather than an additional fitted regression.

evidence.quote: we use the average of forecast two-year growth
evidence.description: The implemented OJ short-term growth averages the two-year forecast growth and five-year analyst growth; nominal perpetual growth is tied to the 10-year Treasury yield less 3 percentage points.

evidence.quote: We estimate b for each firm year by regressing 60 lagged monthly returns against the corresponding monthly returns on the CRSP value-weighted index.
evidence.description: Beta is fit separately for each firm-year from 60 lagged monthly returns and winsorized to [0.2, 4].

evidence.quote: we regress daily returns for the preceding year against the daily CRSP value-weighted index and use the variance of the residuals
evidence.description: The preceding-year daily market-model residual variance is the UNSYST measure.

evidence.quote: Using factor analysis, we identify a single factor, EARNVAR, which measures earnings variability.
evidence.description: The paper forms EARNVAR from analyst forecast error, EPS variability and forecast dispersion using factor analysis.

evidence.quote: We use the log of market capitalization of equity (hereafter referred to as the size)
evidence.description: Page 7 defines size; the preceding page defines leverage as log long-term debt divided by equity market value.

evidence.quote: measuring the average of the risk premium in the prior year for all firms in the same industry as per the Fama–French (1997) classification
evidence.description: RPIND uses prior-year mean firm risk premium among all same-industry firms under the cited classification; the exact risk-premium measure is not identified.

evidence.quote: at least five analyst forecasts in I/B/E/S for that year

evidence.quote: UNA: We compute the ratio of [cash ? all investments and advances - debt preferred equity] to [assets - liabilities]. The denominator in this ratio is total net assets, while the numerator is intended to proxy for that component of net assets whose fair-values are likely most verifiable (Richardson et al. 2005). Thus this ratio is intended to capture the verifiability of net assets (VNA). Items excluded from the numerator include plant and equipment, receivables, payables, inventories, advances, etc. Fair-value estimates of these items are likely less verifiable than cash, investments, debt, and preferred equity. Thus as the VNA ratio decreases, subjectivity in estimating the fair value of goodwill is expected to increase. To obtain a measure that increases in the subjectivity of estimating the fair value of goodwill, we multiply VNA by -1. We then rank the resulting value in-sample and denote it UNA, where ‘‘UNA’’ refers to the unverifiability of net assets.

evidence.quote: For this reason we sum over three future periods: one, two or three years after the initial quarter in which the pro forma earnings number is announced.

evidence.quote: where future cash flow is measured as either CFO or FCF, summed over one, two or three years starting with quarter t þ 1.
evidence.description: Future cash-flow windows begin with the quarter after the current observation.

evidence.quote: All variables are calculated as per share amounts, which are then scaled by total assets per share at the end of the initial fiscal quarter (data item #9/data item #15).
evidence.description: Equation (1) scaling rule and cited item numbers.

evidence.quote: Total assets are defined as Total assets (#44) divided by shares outstanding (#15).
evidence.description: Table 1's total-assets-per-share definition conflicts with the equation's #9/#15 citation.

evidence.quote: we obtain the unadjusted IBES database.
evidence.description: Authors use unadjusted IBES to avoid split adjustment of historical EPS.

evidence.quote: Pro Forma Earnings is the IBES reported actual earnings per share.
evidence.description: Pro Forma Earnings definition.

evidence.quote: GAAP earnings is defined as earnings per share before extraordinary items and discontinued operations, using either basic (data item #19) or diluted (data item #9), depending on the IBES basic/diluted flag.
evidence.description: GAAP EPS basis is selected to match the IBES basic/diluted flag.

evidence.quote: Operating income per share is defined in Compustat (data item #177)
evidence.description: Special Items are constructed from Compustat operating income per share less GAAP earnings per share.

evidence.quote: We define Growth as the change in sales from the same quarter in the previous year (data item #2).
evidence.description: Sales Growth uses same-quarter prior-year sales.

evidence.quote: We also control for Accruals, defined as GAAP earnings less cash from operations.
evidence.description: Accruals definition.

evidence.quote: we adjust it to a diluted basis, if necessary, by using the most recent annual dilution factor, computed from basic shares outstanding (data item #54) and diluted shares outstanding (data item #171).
evidence.description: Annual dilution-factor adjustment for quarterly operating income per share.

evidence.quote: CFO_SUM1, 2, and 3 are cash from operations (#108) scaled by the applicable weighted average shares outstanding (#15), summed for one, two or three years starting with quarter t þ 1.
evidence.description: CFO outcome includes a per-quarter weighted-share denominator within the future horizon.

evidence.quote: FCF_SUM1, 2, and 3 are calculated as cash from operations (#108) - capital expenditures (#90), scaled by the applicable weighted average shares outstanding (#15), summed for one, two or three years starting with quarter t þ 1.
evidence.description: FCF outcome uses CFO less capex, with per-quarter weighted-share scaling.

evidence.quote: To limit the influence of outliers, all variables are winsorized at the 1% and 99% levels.
evidence.description: Winsorization rule.

evidence.quote: we estimate equation (1) separately for each quarter and report the mean of the resulting coefficient estimates.
evidence.description: Quarterly regressions and mean coefficients.

evidence.quote: We then compute a t-statistic based on the quarterly estimates (i.e., a Fama-MacBeth t-statistic), multiplying the traditional standard error by the Newey-West adjustment in order to account for the possible serial correlation in the quarterly estimates.
evidence.description: Fama–MacBeth inference with Newey–West correction.

required_coverage.detail: The paper ends the sample in 1997 because that is the last year for the Bushee (1998) institutional classifications; classifications must map manager IDs to the reported type in each year. Helper window check: anchor 1988–1997; lookback 0 months, lead 0 months gives conservative envelope 1988–1997.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No verified local or public raw route for the Bushee manager-year classifications was established in the allowed catalog and evidence checks.

requirements.description: Monthly CRSP total security returns used to construct one-year size-adjusted buy-and-hold returns after the annual report and market value/size rankings.

required_coverage.frequency: monthly security returns and month-end prices/shares
required_coverage.population: NYSE, AMEX and NASDAQ common stocks in the study sample and the size-decile benchmark universe.
required_coverage.detail: The abnormal-return holding period begins in the fourth month after fiscal year end and lasts one year; the 1997 sample endpoint can require CRSP returns into calendar 1999 depending on fiscal year-end. Helper window check: anchor 1988–1999; lookback 0 months, lead 0 months gives conservative envelope 1988–1999.

routes.mapping_notes: Catalog fields identify monthly total returns, prices and shares. Compound firm buy-and-hold returns over the paper’s period; formation timing and eligible size-decile benchmark universe are separate unresolved requirements.
routes.coverage_notes: An exact-resource probe supports bounded readability and the listed live columns. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this study period and target population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: No frozen coordinator coverage confirmation supports this local snapshot for the required historical population; route completeness therefore remains undetermined.

requirements.description: Same-size-decile portfolio buy-and-hold return benchmark subtracted from each firm’s buy-and-hold return; preserve the source benchmark portfolio population and formation rules.

required_coverage.frequency: monthly portfolio return and size membership
required_coverage.population: The paper-defined same-size-decile portfolio universe corresponding to each sample firm and annual formation period.
required_coverage.detail: CRSP monthly stock returns and size inputs exist, but the paper extraction does not specify the reference portfolio universe, exact size formation date, breakpoints, weighting or reconstitution convention. Helper window check: anchor 1988–1999; lookback 0 months, lead 0 months gives conservative envelope 1988–1999.

routes.mapping_notes: Raw security returns and size inputs are present; the paper’s same-size-decile benchmark population and formation rule are not fully specified.
routes.coverage_notes: An exact-resource probe supports bounded readability and the listed live columns. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this study period and target population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: The portfolio benchmark population, breakpoint universe and timing are not identified well enough to verify a complete benchmark route.

requirements.description: Date-effective mapping between CDA Spectrum CUSIPs, CRSP securities and Compustat firms for annual holdings, return, and firm-year joins.

required_coverage.population: CDA 13F holdings CUSIPs and public-company CRSP/Compustat identifiers in the 1988–1997 sample and return window.
required_coverage.detail: Use CRSP name history for CUSIP/NCUSIP-to-PERMNO and CCM for GVKEY-to-PERMNO; preserve validity dates and security class restrictions. Helper window check: anchor 1988–1999; lookback 0 months, lead 0 months gives conservative envelope 1988–1999.

routes.mapping_notes: Historical name records expose dated CUSIP/NCUSIP to PERMNO fields. The relationship to each CDA report-date CUSIP and Compustat CUSIP still needs date-valid linkage and coverage confirmation.
routes.coverage_notes: An exact-resource probe supports bounded readability and the listed live columns. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this study period and target population.

routes.mapping_notes: The table exposes date-effective GVKEY–PERMNO links. The valid historical link universe and link-type selection must be verified.
routes.coverage_notes: An exact-resource probe supports bounded readability and the listed live columns. No coordinator coverage confirmation was supplied for this study period and target population.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Exact link fields are readable, but historical identifier coverage and relation to the 13F CUSIP population lack coordinator confirmation.

variable_coverage.construction: Earn_t: Net income before extraordinary items (Compustat item #123), scaled by average total assets. Reported formula: Compustat #123 / average total assets. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Accruals_{t-1}: Lagged Accruals, where Accruals = Earn − CashFlows; for the matching fits the inputs are lagged one year. Reported formula: Accruals_{t-1} = Earn_{t-1} − CashFlows_{t-1}. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

CashFlows_{t-1}: Lagged net cash flow from operating activities (Compustat item #308), scaled by average total assets. Reported formula: CashFlows_{t-1} = Compustat #308 / average total assets. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Earn_{t+1}: Net income before extraordinary items (Compustat item #123), scaled by average total assets. Reported formula: Compustat #123 / average total assets. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Accruals_t: Earn_t minus CashFlows_t; Earn is net income before extraordinary items (Compustat #123) scaled by average total assets, and CashFlows is net cash flow from operating activities (Compustat #308) scaled by average total assets. Reported formula: Earn_t − CashFlows_t. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

H_Accruals_t: The interaction of the HIO indicator H with Accruals_t. H equals one for HIO and zero for LIO; HIO firm-years are ranked in the top third of yearly institutional holdings and must have at least 5% transient institutional holdings, while LIO firm-years are absent from 13-F filings or have zero institutional ownership. Reported formula: H × Accruals_t. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

CashFlows_t: Net cash flow from operating activities (Compustat item #308), scaled by average total assets; this is the Table 4/5 definition. Reported formula: Compustat #308 / average total assets. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

H_CashFlows_t: The interaction of HIO indicator H (one for HIO and zero for LIO) with CashFlows_t. HIO requires top-third yearly institutional holdings and at least 5% transient ownership; LIO is absent from 13-F filings or has zero institutional ownership. Reported formula: H × CashFlows_t. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

R_{t+1}: One-year-ahead size-adjusted annual buy-and-hold return beginning four months after fiscal year end, adjusted by subtracting the return on the same size-matched portfolio. Reported formula: Firm buy-and-hold return − same-size-decile portfolio buy-and-hold return. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

Earn_{t+1}: Observed one-year-ahead net income before extraordinary items (Compustat item #123), scaled by average total assets; this realized outcome is an input to the pricing equation. Reported formula: Compustat #123 earnings at t+1 / average total assets at t+1.. Link the cited raw fields and any fit-derived parameter through the listed requirements; retain the source timing, units, scaling, and unresolved definition differences.

design_coverage.reason: Use the 1988–1997 Compustat annual Industrial/Research and NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ sample; exclude financial firms and utilities; exclude sales < $25m, assets < $50m, and prices outside $1–$250; apply the paper’s LIO/HIO screens, persistence match and ±0.03 accrual-persistence match as applicable.
Join annual Compustat, CRSP return/size series, CDA CUSIP holdings and Bushee manager classifications with date-valid identifiers.
The selected Mishkin-equation baselines report no fixed-effect dummy family; no extra FE data are identified.
No standard-error cluster correction is specified for the selected Mishkin system; none is inferred.
No regression weights are reported; firm-level asset scaling is part of input construction, not a regression weight.
The paper estimates the two Mishkin equations simultaneously with generalized nonlinear least squares. The support persistence regression’s exact estimator/window is not named.

Retain the paper’s sample thresholds, full-sample top-third annual institutional holdings ranking, at least 5% transient holdings for HIO, LIO no filing or zero ownership, and ±0.03 accrual-persistence matching.

implementation_issues.description: The firm-specific persistence regression’s estimator and time-series window are not reported; this parameter controls matching and enters the pricing equation.

The source defines operating cash flow as Compustat #308−#124 in the persistence section but elsewhere uses #308; preserve the frozen baseline formula and flag the source conflict. Historical numeric-item mappings are not inferred from current field names.

HIO/LIO classification requires Bushee manager-year trading-type categories, annual institutional holdings rankings and the 5% transient threshold; the needed manager classification route and identifier linkage are not verified.
The same-size-decile buy-and-hold benchmark lacks a reported formation date, breakpoint universe, weighting rule and reference portfolio population.
Current Compustat, CRSP and 13F holdings vintages may differ from the authors’ source vintages; no historical coverage confirmation is present.

review_notes: The frozen baseline fits use the matched Mishkin forecasting and pricing equations; later accrual hedge-portfolio and analyst-revision regressions are not included.
Preserve the source’s #308 versus #308−#124 cash-flow conflict and the unexplained size-decile benchmark universe.

evidence.quote: When earnings and cash flows at t+1 are missing because the firm has been delisted for performance related reasons we make the following adjustment: we assume that firm has liquidated and so investors lose all their invested capital (i.e., the book value of equity). Construct GSCORE as G1 + G2 + G3 + G4 + G5 + G6 + G7 + G8. Source definition: Additive index equal to the sum of the eight binary growth-fundamental signals G1–G8. Each signal defaults to 0 and equals 1 when its stated criterion is met: G1, ROA above the contemporaneous median for low-BM firms in the same two-digit SIC industry; G2, cash-flow ROA above that median; G3, cash-flow ROA above ROA; G4, quarterly ROA variance over the prior four years below that median; G5, variance of quarterly year-over-year sales growth, comparing Q0 with Q−4, over the prior four years below that median; G6–G8, respectively, R&D, capital-expenditure and advertising intensity above their corresponding medians. The intensity measures use beginning assets as denominator. G4 and G5 use quarterly data and require at least six quarters; when the required quarterly data are missing, the signals are coded zero rather than dropping the observation. Industry medians are at the two-digit SIC level within low-BM firms.. Exact current-vintage field-to-paper mapping limitations are recorded on the linked routes and in review notes.

variable_coverage.construction: XRET_(t+1)=∏_(12 months)(1+firm monthly raw cum-dividend RET)−∏_(12 months)(1+matched Size–BVE/MVE portfolio monthly RET). Firm returns run from month 5 of fiscal year t+1 through month 4 of t+2; portfolio returns are value-weighted monthly returns constructed on July–June periods. Keep the two source windows distinct until their assignment is resolved.

GΔRDA_(t+1) is the within-year five-group rank (0–4 divided by 4) of ΔRDA, sorted descending so the rank falls as ΔRDA rises. ΔRDA is the source-retained change in five-year-capitalized RDASSET from t to t+1 divided by NOA; the denominator year is not specified.

GRDA_t is the within-year five-group rank of RDA_t, divided by four and increasing in RDA. RDASSET_t uses RDEXP_t through t−4; RDA_t divides by MVE at the end of the fourth month following fiscal-year-end t, computed from security price and shares.

GARNOA_(t+1) is the within-year five-group rank of adjusted return on net operating assets. Adjusted earnings add reported R&D expense and subtract RDAMORT; RDAMORT_s=0.2×Σ_(j=1..5)RDEXP_(s−j). Adjusted NOA adds the five-year RDASSET to reported NOA. The denominator year is contradictory: Table 8 says t+1; Appendix note 17 says t.

evidence.quote: Our primary sample employs common stocks from the intersection of the Compustat fundamental annual database and the CRSP stock return database from 1996 to 2011.
evidence.description: Primary annual Compustat/CRSP intersection and stated study window.

evidence.quote: Consequently, the pre-SFAS 142 period in our sample is from 1996 to 2000, and the postSFAS 142 period is from 2004 to 2011.
evidence.description: Pre/post baseline years and excluded transition period context.

evidence.quote: we limit our sample to firm-years with a positive goodwill balance on Compustat at the beginning of the year.
evidence.description: Beginning-goodwill sample restriction.

evidence.quote: In the pre-SFAS 142 period, we define the estimated goodwill impairment as the reduction in the goodwill balance during the year if (i) the reduction exceeds a 5% threshold relative to the beginning goodwill balance and (ii) the firm also reports negative special items (SPI) that are at least as large as the reduction in goodwill.
evidence.description: Pre-period estimated impairment definition and Compustat components.

evidence.quote: Under the SFAS 142 regime, there is no goodwill amortization, and so we replace the 5% threshold with a 0% threshold.
evidence.description: Post-period threshold in the frozen baseline definition.

evidence.quote: We then exclude observations with both a decline in the number of segments and a reduction in the goodwill balance from our sample.
evidence.description: Possible-divestiture screen.

evidence.quote: We set missing GDWLIP to zero for firms with a positive goodwill balance.
evidence.description: Actual Compustat impairment missing-value rule.

evidence.quote: E_IMPDUMt (IMPDUMt) is a dummy variable that is equal to one if firms have nonzero E_GDWLIP (GDWLIP) in year t and zero otherwise.
evidence.description: Definition of estimated and Compustat dependent-variable indicators.

evidence.quote: GTAt-1 is GDWL divided by total assets (AT) at the end of year t-1.
evidence.description: GTA numerator/denominator and end-of-year t−1 date.

evidence.quote: ROAt-1 is operating income after depreciation (OIADP) in year t-1 divided by average total assets (AT).
evidence.description: ROA numerator and the source’s unspecified average-assets denominator.

evidence.quote: IMPIt-1 is equal to one for observations with GTAt-1>10% and ROAt-1 < 0, minus one for observations with GTAt-1 < 5% and ROAt-1 > 5% and zero otherwise.
evidence.description: IMPI indicator thresholds and three-way values.

evidence.quote: BTMt-1 is book value of equity (CEQ) divided by market value of equity (PRCC_f*CSHO) at the end of year t-1.
evidence.description: Book-to-market inputs and date.

evidence.quote: BTMG1t-1 is an indicator variable that is equal to one if BTMt-1 is greater than one and zero otherwise.
evidence.description: BTMG1 threshold.

evidence.quote: Panel A reports conditional logit regressions of Eq. (1) estimated at firm clusters.
evidence.description: Conditional-logit estimator and firm-level cluster statement; the text does not separately state a fixed-effect group implementation or cluster key.

evidence.quote: Numbers in the parentheses are zstatistics.
evidence.description: Table 3 inference display.

Monthly discretionary information-risk factor-mimicking return. Each month, firms are independently ranked into quintiles using their most recent DiscAQ; the factor is average monthly excess return for the top two quintiles minus that for the bottom two. Fiscal-year-t DiscAQ scores are used to form portfolios for the 12-month period beginning in fiscal year t+1. Returns are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles before portfolio formation. DiscAQ is the Eq. (6) residual, based on AQ from Eq. (5); AQ is the time-series standard deviation of Eq. (5) residuals over years t−4 through t.. Construct the return or annual score only after the event/industry support population is formed and the firm/date mapping is valid.

Interaction of the event-time indicator DT (1 for t ≥ 0, including month 0; 0 earlier) with DiscIR_t.. Construct the return or annual score only after the event/industry support population is formed and the firm/date mapping is valid.

Monthly innate information-risk factor-mimicking return. Each month, firms are independently ranked into quintiles using their most recent InnateAQ; the factor is average monthly excess return for the top two quintiles minus that for the bottom two. Fiscal-year-t InnateAQ scores are used to form portfolios for the 12-month period beginning in fiscal year t+1. Returns are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles before portfolio formation. design_coverage.reason: The paper specifies country and industry-year effects, but not which industry field/classification or the exact dated country/industry assignment rule.
The Table 4 access models do not report regression weights.

implementation_issues.description: The O-Score formula in the original Appendix visibly prints “to” between the −1.32 intercept and the 0.407 log-assets term. The source’s arithmetic operator is unresolved, so the frozen construction cannot be uniquely calculated without choosing an unsupported formula.

The source defines the issue-level repeated-issue screen as deleting same-type issues by the same firm within one year but does not identify which issue is retained. For firm-year Public Market Dummy it does not state how a year with both bond and loan borrowing is coded; the continuous amount ratio also lacks a currency-normalization rule.

The article gives bond and loan issuer match identifiers, but local entity-resolution priorities, the Datastream-to-Worldscope security link, current-vintage sample codes and full historic match coverage are not confirmed.

The source requires World Bank GDP growth and S&P sovereign country ratings, and local mandatory-IFRS dates, but no exact local country-year resource/field route is present in the inspected local catalog/resource index.

The local S&P rating candidate is a Compustat North America rating table, while the paper’s borrower/rating sample is global; the paper does not identify the global rating data vintage, scale crosswalk, estimator or fallback rule for estimated ratings.

No local coverage confirmation establishes the SDC, Dealscan, Worldscope, Datastream or annual rating-support populations over their required study/history windows. Exact-field probes establish only current file access and field presence.

review_notes: The three Table 4 Panel A full-sample fits remain distinct: issue-level probit, firm-year probit and firm-year OLS. The issue-level fit reports 13,546 observations after fixed-effect prediction losses, while the source sample flow reports 4,676 access bonds plus 9,327 access loans before that loss. The annual rating-construction population is kept as a separate cross-sectional support fit before final baseline screens. Source-defined Worldscope field codes are retained; the O-Score operator, mixed-market firm-year outcome rule and vendor-link rules remain unresolved.

Breadth is measured as quarterly or overlapping trailing-four-quarter change; risk is a trailing 3/12-month daily squared-excess-return measure, square-rooted and ranked into deciles. Table 5 includes the three aligned breadth×risk products and only the risk main effect at t. No additional transformation or winsorization of these baseline variables is reported.

implementation_issues.description: The general Section 3 definition and Table 5 note give opposite signs for size-adjusted returns. The assessment follows the general firm-minus-size-portfolio definition (p. 7), which is also consistent with the p. 24 negative breadth-return interpretation, and flags the table-specific reversal. The paper does not explicitly reconcile the two statements, so the original Table 5 coding cannot be confirmed from the frozen source alone.

Breadth scale conflicts: Table 5 says multiply by 100, while the main fraction definition and the p. 24 interpretation of 0.01 as one percentage point support an unscaled proportion. The construction uses the unscaled fraction and retains the table-note conflict for review.

The daily excess-return subtraction order is reversed between Section 3 and the Table 5 note. The construction follows Section 3; because the difference is squared, reversing the sign does not change the daily squared-excess-return input.

The paper reports quarterly regressions and mean coefficient estimates but does not identify the within-quarter estimator. Preserve it as unknown; selecting an estimator is an implementation choice that can affect exact replication.

The official current Fama/French series uses the newer CRSP CIZ source vintage and may reconstruct historical returns differently from the data available to the 2007 paper. Its daily 48-industry series is a candidate standard source, but exact vintage and stock-to-portfolio mapping are not verified.

evidence.quote: We use size-adjusted returns, computed as the difference between the security’s return and the return on the security’s size-matched decile portfolio over the corresponding period.

evidence.quote: the monthly measures equal the sum of daily squared excess returns. Excess returns are computed by subtracting the daily value-weighted industry return from the security’s daily return.

evidence.quote: Panel A (B) of this table reports mean coefficient estimates and t-statistics from quarterly regressions of one-quarter-ahead (1-year-ahead) size-adjusted returns on prior, current, and next period measures of the change investor recognition and their interactive terms with idiosyncratic risk.

evidence.quote: Percentage quarterly change in breadth (DBreadthQTR) equals the difference in the number of institutions (13F filers) holding the firm’s stock at the beginning and at the end of the quarter divided by the total number of institutions at the beginning of the quarter and multiplied by 100.
evidence.description: The Table 5 note says to multiply quarterly breadth changes by 100.

evidence.quote: Percentage annual change in breadth (DBreadthANN) equals the difference in the number of institutions holding the firm’s stock at the end of quarter t - 4 and at the end of the current quarter divided by the total number of institutions at the end of quarter t - 4, and multiplied by 100.
evidence.description: Annual breadth compares current-quarter holdings with quarter t−4 holdings and uses the earlier-quarter filer count as denominator.

evidence.quote: The monthly measures equal the sum of the daily squared excess return, which equal the difference between the daily value-weighted industry return and the firm’s daily returns.
evidence.description: The Table 5 note reverses the daily excess-return subtraction order; the difference is squared before aggregation.

evidence.quote: The idiosyncratic risk measures are ranked each quarter into deciles and the ranks are normalized to range from -.5 to +.5 (denoted Rank i-risk).

evidence.quote: The t-statistics are adjusted using the Newey–West correction with four lags

implementation_issues.description: The paper reports quantile regression but does not state the fitted quantile, which is necessary to reproduce the Table 2 coefficients.
The source reports PCOST as the log of total assets but does not identify the logarithm base; the scale of this regressor is therefore not fully specified.
The paper manually matches 725 of 1,237 loans with missing ticker symbols to Compustat but gives no manual-match rules or record-level link identifiers.
The paper refers to Dichev and Skinner (2002) for effective loan-life adjustments for refinanced, rolled-over, amended, or replaced loans, but does not restate that procedure.

Loan-quarter dates must align with Compustat fiscal quarters for quarter-end current ratio, earnings-management measures, controls, and firm/quarter-year indicators; the exact loan-date to fiscal-quarter match rule is not stated.
DGDP is described only as the change in GDP from last year; country/series, level-versus-growth transformation, frequency, vintage, and alignment are not specified.
The paper uses the 2007 Dealscan release and a study-period Compustat vintage; current local tables have no confirmation that they reproduce those vintages or the paper’s 1992–2007 population.
Equation (1) estimates TAC_q/A_(q−1), while the printed Eq. (2) subtracts fitted scaled terms from TAC_q without displaying the same divisor; the paper does not reconcile AEMDA scaling.
Equation (6) scales CFO by prior-quarter assets, while the prose/appendix defines CFO as operating cash flow divided by total assets; REMCFO scaling is internally inconsistent.
The paper describes the abnormal production, expense, and CFO measures as residuals from cross-sectional equations but does not name the estimator for those residual-generating fits.
The paper reports a keyword search over SEC 10-Q, 10-K, and 8-K filings to screen FAR firms but does not give the full query, accession list, or coding resolution for hits.

The paper states Δ/MVA is winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles but does not define whether cutpoints are pooled over all firm-years, calculated by year, or based on a different sample. This affects the outcome used in the trend fit.

variable_coverage.construction: FULDISC is 1 for disclosure of all required auditor-change 8-K Item 4 items, 0 for test firms receiving an SEC comment letter; code initial 8-K Item 4 for controls and corrected 8-K/A Item 4 for test firms.
LNMV is ln Compustat market value of equity at fiscal-year end when the 8-K was issued; candidate current fields are mkvalt or csho×prcc_f, with exact product/scale mapping unverified.
BODINDPCT is the number of independent board members divided by total board members, manually coded from the relevant DEF14A proxy statement.
BODMEET is annual board meetings counted from the DEF14A proxy statement.
CEOCHAIR is 1 if the CEO is also board chair and 0 otherwise, coded from DEF14A.
AUDCOM is 1 if the board has an audit committee and 0 otherwise, coded from DEF14A.
ACMEET is the annual number of audit-committee meetings from DEF14A.
FINEXPRT counts financial experts; retain the frozen source conflict: Table 2 says audit committee or board, while the text says audit committee only.
CFOTENURE is years the CFO held the position, coded from DEF14A; appointment-date evidence and exact proxy timing need manual mapping.
CFOBOD is 1 if the CFO is a board member and 0 otherwise, coded from DEF14A.
INTCONMW is 1 for a reported material weakness under SOX 404, using SOX 302 reported information for smaller firms not subject to 404; Audit Analytics and filing text are candidate routes.
BIG4DEPART is 1 if the departing auditor immediately before the change was Big 4, coded from the auditor-change 8-K.

EXTFIN is subsequent-fiscal-year equity plus debt financing divided by total assets; candidate current Compustat fields include scstkc, spstkc, prstkc, dvc, dltis, dltr, dlcch and at, subject to semantic/unit mapping.

BKRPTRANK is the decile rank of Altman Z with the highest bankruptcy-risk decile (lowest Z) assigned 10 and descending risk assigned smaller values; exact Z version and ranking population remain unresolved.
